# Centralised update management — programme wave 4 (spec W4, node side): update/rollback/gate/watchdog/sync — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A node moves itself safely and says so: `ccrc update` reports every phase to `~/.ccrc/update.json`, runs one at a time under a lock, can detach from the unit it restarts, proves the box came back healthy (or restores it and exits 4), and — with no `--to` — follows the control plane's projection, which a fleet node now pulls every minute; `ccrc rollback` is a verb, a server-role box has a watchdog for the update that died with it, and `rollout` can follow a channel and tolerates a box one wave older.

**Architecture:** Everything here is bash in `ccd/ccrc` and `ccd/ccrc-doctor-checks` (plus one new sibling executable, `ccd/ccd-update-sync`, and four systemd unit files), tested under the fixture HOMEs `ccrc-update.test.ts`, `ccrc-install.test.ts`, `ccrc-uninstall.test.ts`, `ccrc-rollout.test.ts` and `ccrc-doctor.test.ts` already carry. `cmd_update` (`ccd/ccrc:11305-11488` at `d759c914`) gains, in call order, a report writer (`_upd_phase`), a `--detach` re-exec point, a lock (`_upd_lock`), the projection reader (`_upd_intent_state`, `_acct_pool_state`'s bounded-read discipline from `ccd/ccd:2162` made role-aware per spec §9), a `previous` baseline, a spine-death classifier fed by the staged spine's `install-step` marker, a per-OS health gate (`_upd_gate`) and a two-arm restore (`_upd_restore`). `ccd-update-sync` copies `ccd-pool-sync` discipline for discipline, but VALIDATES a text document (the route answers the §9 document itself) instead of rendering JSON. `cmd_rollback`, `cmd_channel` and `cmd_watchdog` are thin verbs over those same functions, so there is one install path, one gate, one reader and one sweep.

**Tech Stack:** bash ≥ 4.4 (`set -uo pipefail`, no `-e`), `flock` (util-linux; Homebrew on macOS), `jq`, `curl`, `python3` (the puller's whole-document validator), systemd `--user` timers (Linux only), vitest under `server/test`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-centralised-update-management-design.md` — §9 (`ccd-update-sync`, the reader and its role-aware table, `--channel`, the floor on every path, the W4 cap words), §10 (`--detach`, the lock, `update.json`, `previous`), §11 (the gate per OS, spine death, `_upd_restore` arms 2–3, `cmd_rollback`, the watchdog, doctor `provenance`), §12 (the unarmed-exposure doctor check), §14 (`ccrc channel`, `--check caps=`, `rollout --channel`), §16 (the server self-update risk), and the §18 rows from "the projection is whole-or-nothing" through "`--channel` refuses off the control plane", "the puller is installed where its timer looks", "`_inst_caps` writes each wave's words", "the floor is checked on every path", and every row from "`--detach` escapes the cgroup" through "doctor `provenance` WARNs, never FAILs" except the dispatcher/op/route rows, plus "the exposure check reads both inputs correctly". The spec's `ccd/ccrc` line numbers are stale by 100–400 lines; every anchor below was re-measured at `d759c914`, and every task re-locates by identifier before editing.

**Out of scope (said once):** the agent `update` op and `AgentReady.ops` sending, `server/src/update/dispatch.ts`, the `apply`/`rollback` routes and the PWA controls (programme wave 5); versioned installs, `ccrc versions`, `_upd_restore` arm 1 and the `versions` cap word (programme wave 6); `deploy/deploy.sh` and `deploy/build-release.sh` (spec §19 — so a `deploy.sh`-installed fleet box has no `ccd-update-sync` and its reader takes the not-configured arm, which is the spec's own table); `ccd/ccd` (untouched unless a task proves it must be, and then re-stamped with `markGenerated`); `KillMode` on `ccrc.service`/`ccrc-agent.service` (spec §17).

**Relation to W2.** W2 (the control plane: `MIGRATIONS[13]`, the store, the inventory, the resolver, the routes) is planned — its final plan is committed, `git show 1288beec:docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-22-centralised-update-w2-control-plane.md` — and is being built CONCURRENTLY with this wave; it merges FIRST. Nothing here imports W2's code before Task 15, and every name this wave shares with W2 is W2's committed spelling (ruling R17: where this plan and W2's committed plan differ, W2's wins and this plan changes): `UPDATE_PHASES` (the thirteen words in spec §6 order) and `IN_FLIGHT_UPDATE_PHASES` (exactly the nine non-terminal words `queued resolving fetching verifying backing-up installing restarting checking restoring`, which Task 9's watchdog spells as `UPD_IN_FLIGHT_PHASES`) — W2 Task 1, `shared/api.ts`; the projection grammar (spec §9's nine-line document, unix SECONDS, `lease = issued + PROJECTION_LEASE_S`, 900) and its route `GET /api/updates/intent/:nodeId`, answering `200` with `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and the document itself (so the puller validates text, it does not render JSON) — W2 Tasks 12 and 13; the projection file `~/.ccrc/update-intent`, mode 0600, written tmp-then-rename by W2's server-role writer on every resolution and sweep (ruling R3); `NODE_ID_RE`, a lowercase UUID, declared once in `server/src/coord/store.ts` — W2 Task 5; `REPORT_TIME_MAX_S = 99_999_999_999` and `reportFrom` in `server/src/update/inventory.ts` — W2 Task 11, which reads `update.json`'s `phase`/`target`/`startedAt`/`updatedAt`/`detail` BY NAME, converts the two times from seconds to ms once, nulls any time above `REPORT_TIME_MAX_S`, and IGNORES every other key; the per-node release refusal for a `failed` report whose detail begins `provenance:` (W2's `provenance:` detail prefix) — W2 Task 11's sweep plan (`startsWith('provenance:')`, which this wave's `provenance: ` prefix satisfies); `previous` and `floor` line 1 read through `isReleaseTag` (`tagLineFrom`), so D-3231's `untagged` reads NULL; and `CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS` (W2 Task 9's `updateDeadlineMs`, default 900000). **Settled by the coordinator's rulings (2026-09-23), no longer open:** (1) **`update.json`'s `startedAt`/`updatedAt` are unix SECONDS** (rulings R1, R14) — `_upd_phase` writes `date +%s`, portable to macOS; every test regex and every age computation in this wave (the watchdog's staleness, the wedged bound) is in seconds; `CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS` stays a millisecond knob and is divided by 1000 at the one place the watchdog compares it; W2's report precedence is `startedAt*1000 + 999 >= updateStartedAt` (W2's D-3199 in its committed plan, which stands — ruling R1). The decisions file's "epoch ms" is superseded. (2) **the seventh key `pid` (D-3237) stays** (rulings R2, R15) — W2's reader ignores unknown keys and W2 Task 11 pins "an extra key is ignored"; Task 15's second pin asserts it from this side. Task 15 waits for W2's merge: it begins with `git fetch origin main && git merge origin/main` at the merge sha the coordinator's brief names, re-checks every name above against W2's merged code (a difference there is a departure, never a silent edit), and replaces W2's embedded-python projection pin in `update-projection.test.ts` with the real `ccd-update-sync` and the real reader.

## Global Constraints

- **The canonical version is the tag** `vX.Y.Z`, tested by `cmd_update`'s inline shape `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` (`ccd/ccrc:11322`) — `ccd/ccrc` has no `$SHAPE` variable (the spec's word; `SHAPE` lives in `deploy/release-*.sh`); every new tag test in bash reuses that literal, and the `v` is stripped only inside `_ver_newer` (`ccd/ccrc:1636`).
- **`ccd/ccrc` is `set -uo pipefail` (`:68`), never `-e`:** every new step captures its rc explicitly (`|| rc=$?`, `|| _ccrc_die …`); a step that omits it continues past its own failure.
- **`update.json` details are printable ASCII.** `_upd_json_str` (Task 1) spells the file's three non-ASCII characters in ASCII (`—` → `-`, `…` → `...`, `→` → `->`) and turns any other byte outside 0x20–0x7E into `?`; a detail a task writes joins its clauses with `; ` (or `-`) rather than ` — `, and leads with its verdict so spec §8's 200-character cut trims only the tail (D-3249). Stdout and stderr sentences keep their spec wording.
- **Exit codes of `ccrc update` after this wave:** 0 moved or already there; 1 refused or failed; 2 usage; 3 moved, doctor FAIL, gate passed (D-3114, unchanged); 4 the gate failed and `_upd_restore` ran (new). `cmd_rollout` relays 3 and continues, and stops on 4 like any other non-zero.
- **The exec surface is untouched** — nothing in `agent/` changes; `EXEC_COMMANDS`/`FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS`/the whitelist are programme wave 5's neighbours, not ours.
- **`deploy/deploy.sh` and `deploy/build-release.sh` are untouched** (spec §19) — including `deploy.sh`'s own `ccd-pool-sync` census, the seventh surface `agent/test/deploy-verify.test.ts` pins, which `ccd-update-sync` deliberately does NOT join.
- **macOS goes through the platform layer:** `_svc_is_active` (`ccd/ccrc:932`), `_svc_run_detached` (`:1016`), `_svc_restart` (`:883`), `_plat_mv_notdir` (`:211`), `_plat_mktemp` and `_ccrc_job_stayed_up` (`:11840`), `_dr_unit_file` (`ccd/ccrc-doctor-checks:775`). `update.json`'s times and every age this wave computes are `date +%s` (unix seconds, ruling R14), which needs no platform helper; `_plat_epoch_ms` is not used by this wave. No new platform helper is expected; if one proves necessary it lands above `# ── END PLATFORM LAYER` in BOTH `ccd/ccrc` and `ccd/ccd`, and `ccd/ccd` is re-stamped. Callers of platform helpers need no sentinel. The arms the spec makes Linux-only (`--detach`, the two timers, the watchdog) refuse or skip on Darwin by name.
- **Fixture HOMEs only** (`mkTmp`, `tmpHelpers.ts`; the update harness's `updateEnv`) — never `ccd` or `ccrc` against the live `$HOME`; `systemctl`, `systemd-run`, `launchctl`, `curl`, `ssh` are recording stubs or poisons.
- **The `pathWithout` allowlist rule** (`ccrc-install.test.ts:641`, the list at `:686-707`): any new shell-out a new INSTALL-path step makes is added to that list in the same commit, or every single-absence fixture dies at the new step instead of reaching its own subject. Measured at `d759c914`: every tool the planned install-side steps use (`mkdir cp mv rm chmod cmp date`) is already listed; a task that adds any other adds it. The update harness's own bare PATH, `pathWithoutJq`, gains `flock` and `mkdir` symlinks in Task 2 (the lock is taken before the jq preflight, so without them D-3140's case would die at the lock instead of at jq).
- **The session-hook citation-corpus tax:** every line inserted into `ccd/ccrc` shifts the frozen anchors `session-hook.test.ts` audits (`byFile['ccd/ccrc']`, the **Files:**-pass and `|`-row sets, the site-level set, the headline total). Tasks 1–15 do not chase it; Task 16 re-measures it ONCE by S6-R11 (`session-hook.test.ts:8069-8074`) — failure sets DUMPED from `git archive` trees of the base and the tip and diffed, never retyped — and states the composition of each moved literal.
- **Deviation numbers are issued by the allocator** (`POST /api/ledger/deviations`) and defined in the same act. This plan's departures carry the numbers the coordinator minted for run 129 on 2026-09-23 (the section below). A departure found while executing takes the next unspent number of the run's RESERVE block, which the coordinator minted beside it and names in the wave brief; it is defined in `## Deviations found` in the same commit that first cites it, and an unspent reserve number is never written as a `D-` token anywhere (`deviation-refs.test.ts` holds the highest cited number equal to the highest defined one). Never a concrete `D-TBD-` spelling (`dtbd.test.ts`).
- **Commit on the workspace branch only**, at least one commit per task (`feat(ccrc): …` / `test(ccrc): …`); a separate feature branch wedges the done-fingerprint with `stale-tip`.
- **No residue classes in tracked text** — no hostnames, usernames, absolute home paths, docserver URLs or the org name (`topology-clean.test.ts`, the pre-push hook); fixtures use invented owner/repo values; run `test/topology-clean.test.ts` before every commit that adds a file.
- **Suites run in the foreground, one file at a time, from inside the package:** `cd server && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/<file>.test.ts` (timeout ≥ 600000 ms) — never bare `npx vitest`; the full unsharded server suite and the agent and pwa suites run once, in Task 16.

## Review Focus

Five failure modes the spec implies and no existing pin exercises — most likely first. A reviewer reads these before the diff.

1. **A rollout against one box still on an older `ccrc`** — the rollout that ships this wave is exactly that fleet. An older `--check` line has no `caps=`/`floor=`; an older `ccrc update` refuses `--from` as an unknown argument (exit 2, so rollout would stop at the first box having touched nothing — or worse, at the second, having moved the first); an older box has no `ccrc channel`. Task 12 adds the tests: rollout parses a pre-W4 check line (fields absent, `state` still correct, no stray field swallowed into it), passes `--from rollout` only to a box whose `caps=` lists `update-json`, and `--channel` against a box that prints no `channel:` line refuses at exit 2 before anything is touched.
2. **A projection lease in the past on a fleet box whose timer was stopped** — the server down 15 minutes is enough. The failure is silent fallback: `stale` or `unreadable` read as `not-configured`, and the box following `stable` instead of refusing. Task 8 adds the tests: fleet + timer unit file present + an expired `lease` → exit 1 naming the lease's age and `systemctl --user start ccd-update-sync.service`; fleet + timer unit file present + file ABSENT → `unreadable`, never the `following stable` sentence; and a `lease` exactly equal to now is still `ok` (the comparison is strict).
3. **A doctor check whose rc disagrees with its verdict line.** `cmd_doctor` cross-checks them (`ccd/ccrc:2572-2587`) and reports a mismatch as a FAIL naming ccrc as buggy — easy to trip in a check with a SKIP arm (rc 3 and exactly one SKIP line) or a two-class answer. Task 11 adds the test: every quadrant of `update-exposure` and every arm of `provenance` run through the full `ccrc doctor`, asserting the verdict line AND that no `the check exited` line appears.
4. **A restore child that re-acquires the lock.** Arm 2's child is a real `ccrc update` process; if the `CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD` exemption misfires, the child exits 1 with `another update holds …` and every automatic restore silently degrades to arm 3's MIXED tree — and the same silent degradation follows if the child's staged spine is launched with a `{UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-` while its `UPD_LOCK_FD` is empty (`ambiguous redirect`, the spine never runs; Task 6's finding, answered by Task 2's conditional subshell close). Task 6 adds the test: a FULL-flavour gate failure whose arm-2 child completes under the parent's lock (its transcript carries no lock sentence, `update.json` ends `reverted: arm2: …`); Task 2 adds the two measurement pins (marker = `$PPID` with no holder → refused; marker naming another pid → acquires normally).
5. **A detached run killed mid-install on a server-role box.** Nothing measures it (the process that holds the server-side deadline is the one being restarted), the lock dies with it, `update.json` stays non-terminal, and a naive watchdog either never acts or rolls back a box that finished. Task 9 adds the tests: a stale `installing` report, no holder, `/health` on the old version → `rollback --from watchdog` runs; the same with the box measuring converged → rewritten `failed: 'abandoned by its updater; box measures converged at <v>'`, no rollback; a live holder → exit 0 and the sentence; a live holder past 2× the deadline → the wedged sentence.

## Deviations found

Plan-level departures from the spec's literal text, found while planning against the measured tree at `d759c914`; each carries the number the allocator issued for it (run 129, minted 2026-09-23). The first ten were fixed by the coordinator's decisions; the rest were found while writing the task interfaces and bodies, and each names the task that found it. A task that finds another adds a bullet here in the same form and names itself.

- **D-3227** — the server-role watchdog is a verb, `ccrc watchdog`, in `ccd/ccrc`, run by `ccrc-update-watchdog.service`'s `ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/ccrc watchdog`. Spec §11 names the unit pair and its logic but not its executable; a new sibling binary would join the census `ccd-pool-sync` carries (`_inst_bins`, both summary echoes, `cmd_uninstall`'s lists, the wrapper sweep, `TOOLCHAIN_EXECUTABLES`, the install fixture) for code that needs functions — `_upd_gate_probe`, `_upd_phase`, `_box_build_fields`, `_upd_lock_holder` — that already live in `ccd/ccrc`. A verb adds no binary, no census entry and no second copy of the gate. Cost if wrong: one dispatch-table line, and a watchdog that runs from the tree it watches — which is also the tree a restore rewrites, so its next tick runs the restored copy.
- **D-3228** — `--from` is a closed six-word vocabulary, `cli pwa restore rollback watchdog rollout`, declared once in `ccd/ccrc` as `UPD_FROM_WORDS`, default `cli`; any other word exits 2. Spec §10 and §11 name `pwa`, `restore`, `rollback` and `watchdog` in prose and never state a closed set, a default or the refusal; `cli` names the hand-typed run and `rollout` names `cmd_rollout`'s. The word reaches `update.json`'s `from`, where a free-text value would be attribution nobody can enumerate. Cost if wrong: a seventh caller needs a one-word edit here and in the spec.
- **D-3229** — `--detach` requires `--to` (exit 2 without it). Spec §10's re-exec argv always carries `--to <tag>`, and a detached run that resolved a channel itself would print its `following stable` or refusal sentence into a transient unit nobody reads; the caller that detaches (the agent op, programme wave 5) always names the tag. `cmd_rollback --detach` resolves its default target from `~/.ccrc/previous` BEFORE the re-exec, so its detached argv carries `--to` too. Cost if wrong: an operator who wants a detached channel-following run types the tag `ccrc channel` prints.
- **D-3230** — the lock opens `{ exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>>"$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK"; } 2>/dev/null`, like the plain-lock precedents in the tree (`ccd/ccd:6912` ws-add, `:10106` the reap lock, `:13608`, `:19307`, `:4410` with its compound-redirect rule at `:4381-4409`; `ccd/ccrc:6337` `_acct_marker_lock`), not the spec's `exec {fd}<>`. The one `<>` precedent, the compaction lock (`ccd/ccd:3104`, `:3266`), opens an ALIAS by its link-off-canonical protocol for a reason this lock does not have. Append-open creates the file and never truncates it; nothing reads the lock file's bytes (the holder's pid and target come from `update.json`), so read access buys nothing. Cost if wrong: none measured — `flock(2)` locks the open file description either way.
- **D-3231** — a box whose running stamp carries no `version` (an unversioned or `deploy.sh` build) writes `untagged` on `~/.ccrc/previous` line 1, and `unstamped` on line 2 when no stamp could be read. Spec §10 says `previous` holds "tag and sha of what is running" and is silent on a box with no tag. `ccrc rollback` with no `--to` refuses `untagged` by name (exit 1, naming `--to`), arm 2 skips straight to arm 3 for it, and W2's reader (`previous` line 1 through `isReleaseTag`) reads it as NULL — one line that never pretends to be a tag. Cost if wrong: an unversioned box's automatic restore is always arm 3, which is what spec §11 already says of it.
- **D-3232** — `update --check`'s machine line gains ` caps=<comma-joined words>` and ` floor=<vX.Y.Z|none|unreadable|malformed>` BEFORE ` state=`: `check: box=… sha=… target=… caps=… floor=… state=…`. `cmd_rollout` reads `state` as everything after the LAST `state=` (`ccd/ccrc:12165`, `${line##*state=}`), so a field appended after it would be swallowed into the state word on every newer box. The spec says only that the line "gains `caps=<words>`"; `floor=` is added because M4's passthrough needs rollout to know which box is below its floor before it touches either, and it carries two words beyond the decisions file's `tag|none` so a present-but-unreadable floor never reads as no floor (the D-3136 principle). Cost if wrong: none — an older rollout ignores both fields, and this rollout tolerates their absence.
- **D-3233** — `--check` answers a fifth state word, `below-floor` (after `current`, `incomplete`, `behind`, `unversioned`), when the target is strictly older than the box's floor and the box is not already current on it (M3: today `--check` never reads the floor and answers `behind` for a target `update` would refuse). `cmd_rollout` refuses such a box at exit 2 before touching either box unless `--downgrade` was typed, and then passes `--downgrade` through to that box's `ccrc update` (M4). Cost if wrong: a rollout that used to "succeed" into an update refusal now refuses one step earlier, with nothing touched.
- **D-3234** — `rollout --channel stable|dev` reads each box's OWN projection over ssh, by running that box's `ccrc channel` and taking its `desired-<ch>` field, never an HTTP route: spec §14 says rollout "reads each node's resolved `desired` from the server", but `rollout` runs from a machine with ssh and no session, the projection IS the server's resolution for that node (written by the server on a server-role box, pulled by `ccd-update-sync` on a fleet box), and the box's own reader is the one function that already tells `ok` from `stale`/`unreadable`/`malformed`. Rollout pins ONE version for both boxes: it takes the one tag the boxes' `desired-<ch>` values name, refuses at exit 2 when they name two different tags, and refuses at exit 2 when neither names one. A box answering `none` names no target of its own, and W2's `resolveOnChannel` answers that NULL for a converged node (`notNewerThanFloor`) and equally for `rolledBack`, `noEligible` (tags this node refused on provenance included), `pinnedIneligible`, `pinnedAtOrBelowFloor` and `noFloor` — the line does not say which — so such a box is admitted only when its own `--check --to <pinned>` line reads `state=current`; otherwise rollout refuses at exit 2 before touching either box (`rollout: the <label> box's projection resolves no <ch> target (desired-<ch> none; its reason is on the console's update screen) and it is not already on <tag> — nothing was touched`), and neither `--force` nor `--downgrade` lifts it: pinning the other box's tag onto it could undo a rollback, override a pin, or push the very release it refused after the first box already moved. Cost if wrong: a rollout from a laptop sees the projection as of the last sync — at most one timer period old, and refused outright once its lease ends.
- **D-3235** — the one cross-side pin spec §9 asks for (the route's real output fed through `ccd-update-sync`, then the real reader) lands in THIS wave's last implementation task, Task 15, after W2 merges, and replaces W2's embedded-python fixture pin; W2 and this wave are built concurrently, so neither can run the other's real code before the merge. Until then the puller and the reader are pinned against documents built from the spec §9 grammar. Task 15 is also where the watchdog's `UPD_IN_FLIGHT_PHASES` is measured against W2's real `IN_FLIGHT_UPDATE_PHASES` and `update.json`'s seconds against W2's real `reportFrom`. Cost if wrong: the ms-vs-seconds class of defect (C1, `server.ts:2679-2688`) is caught one task later than it could be — and still before this wave's PR.
- **D-3236** — `cmd_rollback` runs its re-install as an in-process `cmd_update --to <tag> --downgrade --from rollback` (or `--from watchdog`) after taking the lock itself: a rollback is by definition a move below the floor the last update raised, so it carries `--downgrade` explicitly in addition to spec §9's `--from rollback|watchdog` floor exemption, and the floor file itself is never lowered (`_inst_installed` only raises it, `ccd/ccrc:11217-11259`). Cost if wrong: none beyond a redundant flag — the WARN line names both reasons.
- **D-3237** (found planning Task 2) — `update.json` carries a seventh key, `pid`, after spec §10's six (`{target, phase, startedAt, updatedAt, detail, from, pid}`). The lock refusal must name "pid N, target vX" and the watchdog's wedged sentence "updater pid <n>"; the decisions file reads both from `update.json`, and the spec's key list has no pid. The lock file's own bytes stay empty (D-3230). Settled (rulings R2, R15): W2's `reportFrom` reads the five report fields by name and ignores every other key, W2 Task 11 pins "an extra key is ignored" (`reportFrom(… {pid: 4242, …})` equals the report without it), and Task 15's second pin asserts the same from this side. Cost if wrong: one integer per report.
- **D-3238** (found planning Task 3) — the detached argv is spec §10's template, `"$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" <verb> --to <tag> --from <who>`, with any of `--force`, `--downgrade`, `--allow-unsigned`, `--no-gate` the caller typed appended after `--from <who>` in that fixed order. Dropping them would be D-3139's "silently drop the flag you also typed" trap; refusing them would make a detached downgrade impossible. The agent op's argv (programme wave 5) carries none, so it is exactly the spec's. Cost if wrong: a detached run does what its caller typed.
- **D-3239** (found planning Task 1) — spec §8 has W2's sweep write a per-node release refusal for a `failed` report whose detail BEGINS `provenance:`, and no text says which of `_upd_fetch`'s dies produce that prefix. Exactly the two that are verdicts on the RELEASE carry it: the bundle that FAILS verification (verifier exit 1) and the release that ships no bundle when `--allow-unsigned` was not typed. The verifier that could not RUN (its own sentence: "this is not a verdict on the bundle") and a non-404 bundle download failure do not — a node fault must halt, not refuse a good release fleet-wide for this node. Mechanism: `UPD_FAIL_PREFIX="provenance: "` set for those two `_ccrc_die` calls only; W2 Task 11's sweep tests `detail.startsWith('provenance:')`, which the prefix satisfies. Cost if wrong: a refusal the operator clears with `ack`.
- **D-3240** (found planning Task 4) — spec §11 says a spine death at or after `_inst_tree` runs the gate "and a failed gate runs `_upd_restore` and exits 4", and is silent on a gate that PASSES. Then: no restore, no `_upd_sweep` (the spine did not finish, so the supervisors are not moved onto a half-placed tree), `update.json` ends `failed: 'spine died at <step>'` — written again after the gate, whose own `checking` phase overwrote Task 4's (Task 5's correction) — and the run exits 1 naming the remedy on one `rerun:` line, `ccrc update --to <v> --force` (a rollback's is D-3264's, through `_upd_rerun_hint`). Cost if wrong: a box that moved and answers healthy on the new version waits for an operator's `--force` rerun instead of being swept.
- **D-3241** (found planning Task 4) — `cmd_install`'s 27 bare step lines (`ccd/ccrc:9168-9194`) become one array, `CCRC_INST_SPINE`, iterated through `_inst_step` (which writes `install-step` and calls the step). The spine-death classifier must know which steps precede `_inst_tree`, and a second hand list of the spine in `cmd_update` is the two-copies defect `single-definition.test.ts` exists to refuse. The order pin (`ccrc-install.test.ts:1906`) moves to read the array and additionally refuses any bare `_inst_*` call left in `cmd_install`'s body; the two other readers of that body's bare step lines, `ccrc-install-graphify.test.ts`'s `steps()` (`:503-507`) and `runbook-holds.test.ts`'s FACT 1 (`:205-213`), move in the same commit (Task 4's correction — both would otherwise read zero steps). A step name the running tree's array does not list (a newer spine's step) classifies as at-or-after the tree — the safe direction, it runs the gate. Cost if wrong: one refactor of a function every install runs, pinned by the order test before and after.
- **D-3242** (found planning Task 5) — spec §11's fleet-Linux gate arm is "`is-active ccrc-agent.service` plus `_ccrc_job_stayed_up`", but `_ccrc_job_stayed_up` (`ccd/ccrc:11840`) reads `launchctl print` and is Darwin-only by call site (its own comment, `:11825-11831`); its Linux twin is `deploy/verify-service.sh`, the two-sample MainPID check `_inst_enable` already runs (`:10511`). The fleet-Linux arm runs `bash "$CCRC_HERE/../deploy/verify-service.sh" ccrc-agent.service`, guarded `[ -f ]` exactly as `_inst_enable` guards it. Cost if wrong: none — it is the check the spec's words mean, on the platform it runs on.
- **D-3243** (found planning Task 7) — a `--from rollback|watchdog` run whose gate fails does NOT run `_upd_restore`: the rollback target IS the known-good tag `_upd_restore` would return to, and arm 3 would copy back the tree the rollback just replaced. It writes `update.json failed: 'rollback to <tag>: gate: <why>'` and exits 1. Spec §11 says the rollback "runs arm 1 or arm 2 above, then the gate, then `_upd_sweep`" and is silent on a failing gate. Cost if wrong: a box whose rollback also fails is left for the operator, with the gate's reason on screen, instead of a MIXED tree.
- **D-3244** (found planning Task 7) — spec §11's pin "`rollback` refuses an unknown tag at exit 2" and its §18 row ("the existence check is removed") need a node-side existence test, and a node has no catalogue. `cmd_rollback` asks the release host: `_upd_asset_listed <tag> SHA256SUMS` — a 404 (curl exit 22) exits 2 `rollback: <tag> is not a published release`, any other curl failure exits 1 as unmeasured — before the lock and before any backup. The same helper answers arm 2's "does the previous release ship a bundle". Cost if wrong: one HEAD-sized request per rollback.
- **D-3245** (found planning Task 8) — spec §9 says `desired none` → "refuse, printing the server's reason", but the §9 document carries no reason line (its grammar is nine fixed keys, which W2 renders), so the node cannot print it. The refusal names where the reason is — the console's update screen, `resolveDetail` in `GET /api/updates` — and `--to <tag>`. Adding a `reason` line is a grammar change to a document both waves pin, and a free-text line inside a whole-document validator is the injection surface `ccd-pool-sync`'s `fullmatch` exists to close. Cost if wrong: the operator reads the reason on the screen instead of the terminal.
- **D-3246** (found planning Task 9) — spec §11's watchdog has two outcomes for a stale report with no live holder: converged-at-target → `failed: 'abandoned by its updater; box measures converged at <v>'`; failing probe → `rollback --from watchdog`. A third case exists and the spec does not name it: the probe passes but the box is NOT at the report's target. Its handling splits by the stale phase, because a passing probe on the OLD build does not show that the tree on disk is the old tree. The staged spine's one `installing` phase spans `_inst_tree`, `_inst_bins` and `_inst_files`, which run before `_inst_stamp` and `_inst_enable` (`ccd/ccrc:9175-9181`), and `_inst_tree` rsyncs `--delete` straight into the live `~/ccrc`. So an updater killed there leaves the old stamp and the old in-memory `ccrc.service` over a partly-new tree. (a) In `queued`, `resolving`, `fetching`, `verifying` or `backing-up` the tree cannot have moved, and the watchdog rewrites `failed: 'abandoned by its updater; box measures healthy at <current>, not at <target>'` and exits 0. (b) In every other in-flight phase (`installing`, `restarting`, `checking`, `restoring`, and any in-flight word added later) it writes NOTHING, prints `… — its tree may be partly replaced; not acting, re-measuring every tick`, and exits 0, so a later tick whose probe fails still reaches `rollback --from watchdog`. Neither arm rolls back, because "only a stale report with a failing health probe" rolls back. Cost if wrong: for (a), none, since the row leaves `applying` either way and the box it describes is healthy and unmoved. For (b), a healthy box's report stays non-terminal until the next update or a failing probe, which costs one `/health` request a minute. The error it prevents is a terminal report that shuts the watchdog out of design §11's own scenario, `ccrc.service` restart-looping a half-replaced tree.
- **D-3247** (found planning Task 11) — spec §11's doctor sentence, "this install was made with `--allow-unsigned`", has been false since D-3117: the marker's `unsigned` line is written for EVERY install `ccrc update` did not verify — a checkout `ccrc install`, `install.sh --release` (trust-on-first-use), a pre-W1 updater — not only for `--allow-unsigned`. The WARN names all three and keeps the spec's second clause: `this install was not verified by ccrc update (a checkout install, install.sh's trust-on-first-use, or --allow-unsigned); the next ccrc update verifies`. Cost if wrong: a longer sentence that is true on every box it prints on.
- **D-3248** (found planning Task 12) — `--check`'s `caps=` lists the words the RUNNING `ccrc` can do, from `_ccrc_cap_words` — the same function `_inst_caps` writes `~/.ccrc/ccrc-caps` from — not the file's contents: `--check` is answered by that `ccrc`, rollout asks what that `ccrc` accepts (`--from`, `--no-gate`), and the file can lag it (a spine that died before `_inst_caps`; D-3147's clear before every staged install). One function, so the two answers agree whenever the install completed. Cost if wrong: none measured — the server still reads the file, per spec §8.
- **D-3249** (found planning Task 1; its second half found planning Task 6, whose draft named it `detail-ascii` — one departure, that name retired and never numbered) — spec §8 bounds only what W2's reader ACCEPTS (a detail cut to 200 printable-ASCII characters) and says nothing of how the writer gets there. `_upd_json_str` first spells the three non-ASCII characters `ccd/ccrc`'s sentences use in ASCII (`—` → `-`, `…` → `...`, `→` → `->`), then turns every other byte outside 0x20–0x7E into `?`; a byte filter alone would put `???` on the console for every em dash in a die sentence. And the details this wave composes itself join their clauses with `; ` where spec §11 writes ` — ` (`arm2-refused: <prev> ships no bundle; run ccrc update --to <prev> --allow-unsigned by hand`, `arm2: restored <prev>; <reason>`, `arm3: tree MIXED, deploy.sh is the remedy…; <reason>`, `watchdog: rollback refused (exit <rc>); box unhealthy: <why>`, `spine died at an unrecorded step (no step marker; a spine older than W4 writes none)`), with the verdict FIRST, so the 200-character cut can only shorten the reason. Stdout and stderr sentences keep the spec's wording. Cost if wrong: the console reads `-` or `;` where the terminal showed `—`.
- **D-3250** (found planning Task 2; affirmed by ruling R16) — spec §10 exempts a restore child when "a fresh non-blocking `flock -n` … in a subshell FAILS". Read literally, a subshell that could not even OPEN the lock file counts as a failed flock and grants the exemption with no evidence of a holder. `_upd_lock_probe` answers four ways — rc 0 free (an ABSENT lock file too, without creating it), rc 1 held, rc 2 no `flock`, rc 3 UNMEASURED (the file exists and cannot be opened, or `flock` failed with anything but contention's 1) — and every caller has an explicit rc-3 arm: the restore child refuses (`… ~/.ccrc/update.lock could not be measured (probe rc 3) — refusing; a restore child runs only under a lock it can see`), `--detach` refuses with its own sentence before writing `queued`, and the watchdog exits 0 with `watchdog: the update lock could not be measured — not acting`. Folding rc 3 into rc 1 would grant the exemption on nothing; into rc 0 would let `--detach` spawn past a lock it could not see. Cost if wrong: a restore child with an unreadable lock file refuses and arm 3 runs instead of arm 2.
- **D-3251** (found planning Task 3) — spec §10 says both "`cmd_rollback --detach` takes the lock itself" and "the re-exec happens BEFORE the lock". This plan follows the second: the parent of every `--detach` run, `update` or `rollback`, only PROBES the lock (`_upd_lock_probe`, a non-blocking `flock -n` in a subshell); held → it refuses with the same `another update holds …` sentence before writing `queued`; the detached child takes the lock. A parent that took the lock would hand the transient unit a descriptor that keeps the lock held after the parent exits — exactly what re-exec-before-the-lock exists to prevent. Cost if wrong: a window between the parent's probe and the child's acquire; a child that loses that race refuses before it reports, so the parent's `queued` report stands until the server's deadline (or, on a server box, the watchdog) marks it.
- **D-3252** (found planning Task 4; reshaped reviewing Task 4) — spec §11 assumes the staged `ccrc install` writes `~/.ccrc/install-step`, and is silent on a staged spine that writes none — which WILL happen: a restore or rollback onto any release older than W4 runs a pre-W4 spine. With no marker, `cmd_update` measures the one thing left, the box's stamp: `_inst_stamp` runs after `_inst_tree`, so a stamp that moved off the sha read before the install (`_upd_stamp_moved`) proves the tree was placed, and the death is classified at-or-after — `update.json failed: 'spine died at an unrecorded step'`, gated like any moved death (Task 5). An unmoved stamp proves nothing either way (a death in `_inst_tree`, `_inst_bins` or `_inst_files` leaves it unmoved), so that death exits 1 with no gate and no restore — `update.json failed: 'spine died at an unrecorded step (no step marker; …)'` — and its sentence says `whether the tree was replaced is not known`, never `nothing was replaced`. (`~/ccrc/build.json` is not a usable measurement: `_inst_tree` never copies the release root's stamp.) Gating every unmarked death instead would gate, and possibly restore, a box whose tree was never touched. Cost if wrong: a pre-W4 spine that dies after `_inst_tree` but before `_inst_stamp` waits for an operator instead of being gated — and is told the tree's state is unknown.
- **D-3253** (found planning Task 4) — spec §11 says the staged install writes `install-step` "by `_inst_atomic`". `_inst_atomic <src> <dest> <mode>` places an existing SOURCE file, skips the write when `cmp` finds the destination identical, and places by bare `mv -f --` — which, onto a directory standing at the destination, moves the temp INTO it and answers 0. The marker has no source file and is rewritten before every step, so `_inst_step` follows the same discipline itself (`<dest>.tmp.$$`, `chmod 644`, one rename, the temp removed on failure) through `_plat_mv_notdir`, and `_upd_write_previous` places `previous` the same way. Cost if wrong: none observable — the file is still placed atomically; only the helper's name differs from the spec's text.
- **D-3254** (found reviewing Task 4) — spec §10 says `cmd_update` writes `~/.ccrc/previous` "(tag and sha of what is running) just before the staged install — except when `--from restore|rollback|watchdog`". Two more keeps, on any other `--from`, where what is running is not a completed baseline and a well-formed `previous` exists to keep: (a) the running stamp's tag equals the target (a `--force` reinstall), and (b) `~/.ccrc/installed` is ABSENT (an earlier update's spine died before its record). Without them, the rerun D-3240 prescribes — `ccrc update --to <v> --force` on a box whose stamp the dead spine already moved to `<v>` — records `previous: <v>`, losing the tag that last completed; a failing rerun's arm 2 then re-installs the release that just failed, and a bare `ccrc rollback` returns to it. A record that merely disagrees with the stamp (a `deploy.sh` push leaves the old one) is not (b): that tree is what ran. With no well-formed `previous`, the stamp is written as the spec says. Cost if wrong: after a `--force` reinstall of the running tag, `previous` still names the tag before it, so a bare `ccrc rollback` goes back one release further than "what ran before this run".
- **D-3255** (found planning Task 5) — when `_box_server_addr` answers "nothing configured" (no `CCRC_ADDR`, and no `CCRC_HOST`/`CCRC_PORT` in `~/.ccrc/ccrc.env`), the gate probes `127.0.0.1:7788` instead of failing. That rc is `_box_server_addr`'s SKIP for the doctor's `build` check (a box with no address "runs no server of its own"), but the gate only probes on a `server`/`both` box, which DOES run one — and a server whose env file names neither key binds exactly `server/src/config.ts:305-318`'s defaults, the pair `cmd_install`'s landing block already falls back to (`ccd/ccrc:9247-9248`) and the address `cmd_rollout` probes (`:12228`). Failing there would exit 4 and restore every older `server`/`both` box whose seed-once `ccrc.env` predates the two keys. A configured address that is malformed (resolver rc 2) still fails the gate with the resolver's own sentence. Cost if wrong: a box whose server listens elsewhere while its env file names nothing fails the gate with `no answer` on the default address — a real misconfiguration, now said.
- **D-3256** (found planning Task 5) — spec §11 says the gate waits for the role's signal and "Then `cmd_doctor` runs as today". Today (and here) the doctor is the staged spine's LAST act (`cmd_install` ends with `cmd_doctor`, `ccd/ccrc:9239`; `cmd_update`'s header step 3), so it has run before `cmd_update` regains control and the gate runs after it; a second doctor after the gate would print every verdict twice. The exit codes are the spec's either way: doctor FAIL + gate pass → 3; gate fail → 4 whatever the doctor said. Cost if wrong: the doctor's `services`/`build` lines may read a unit mid-restart that the gate, seconds later, measures up — the gate's line is the later measurement and decides the exit code.
- **D-3257** (found planning Task 6) — `ccrc update --from restore` is refused at exit 2 unless `CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD` equals the run's own `$PPID`, in the argument-refusal block, before `--detach`, the lock and any write; after it passes, `_upd_lock` inherits the lock or dies. A `--from restore` run skips the floor (Task 1), the `previous` baseline (Task 4) and the sweep (Task 6); typed by hand it would be a second way below the floor beside `--downgrade`, which spec §9 makes the only way down, and would leave live supervisors on a `ccd` the box no longer has. Consequence: Task 2's "a marker naming another pid acquires normally" pin must not use `--from restore`. Cost if wrong: an operator who wants that combination types `--downgrade`, which the refusal names.
- **D-3258** (found planning Task 6) — arm 3 copies back only the `tree` rows of `_upd_backup_pairs`. `~/.ccrc/memory` is backed up (R34) and NEVER restored: no install spine writes it and every live session does, so restoring a snapshot taken minutes earlier would erase what sessions wrote in between. `coord.db` is treated the same for the spec's own reason (§11, `db.ts:176-181`). Cost if wrong: an operator who wants the pre-update memory copies it from the named backup directory by hand.
- **D-3259** (found planning Task 6) — spec §11 says arm 3 "copies the backup back"; it copies each row to a staging path beside the live one and places it by RENAME (`_upd_restore_copy`); a live directory is moved aside and removed only after the new one is in place, and moved back if the rename fails. A `cp` onto the live `~/.local/bin/ccd` would rewrite a bash script every running `ccd supervise` is executing — the hazard `_inst_atomic` exists for. The hazard case pins it with a hard link on the new inode. Cost if wrong: one extra rename per row.
- **D-3260** (found reviewing Task 6) — arm 3 removes `~/.ccrc/installed` before copying anything back. Spec §11's arm 3 names only "the three dists, the bins, the units", but a spine that COMPLETED and then failed its gate has written the new build's stamp and record, agreeing, and arm 3 copies neither back — so the box would measure CONVERGED on the release it backed out of (`_upd_converged` 0, `update --check` `current`). Removed, it reads `incomplete`, the truth of a MIXED tree. The stamp is not restored: neither build's stamp is true of a MIXED tree. Cost if wrong: a box arm 3 did return whole re-installs on its next update instead of no-opping.
- **D-3261** (found reviewing Task 6) — `_upd_asset_listed` reads "the release does not carry this asset" only from a MEASURED 404 (`curl -f` exit 22 with `-w '%{http_code}'` = `404`); any other failure is unmeasured. curl -f's exit 22 is any status ≥ 400 (D-3143's lesson in `_upd_fetch`), so a 403 rate limit or a 5xx would otherwise make arm 2 refuse a restore it could run and `ccrc rollback` call a real tag unpublished (Task 7). Cost if wrong: one `-w` format string per question.
- **D-3262** (found planning Task 7) — `ccrc rollback --from <who>` names who ASKED (`cli` by hand, `pwa` from the console, `watchdog` from the server-role watchdog); the in-process `cmd_update` it runs is always `--from rollback`, or `--from watchdog` when the watchdog asked. Spec §9 has `cmd_rollback` pass `--from rollback|watchdog` to reach the floor exemption while §11's PWA argv carries `--from pwa`; one word cannot be both, and the run-kind word is the one three mechanisms key on — the floor exemption (Task 1), the `previous` exception (Task 4; a `--from cli` re-install would record the tag being rolled AWAY from as `previous`, so the next bare rollback would roll forward onto it) and the no-restore arm (Task 7). So a rollback's `update.json` reads `from: rollback` (or `watchdog`) from `resolving` on; the caller's word survives in the detached argv, in a detached rollback's `queued` report (written by the parent, `_upd_detach`) and in the transcript's `asked by --from <who>`. W2's inventory reads five report fields and not `from`, so nothing server-side loses anything. Cost if wrong: a console-driven rollback's local report says `rollback` where it could have said `pwa`.
- **D-3263** (found planning Task 7) — a rollback passes `--allow-unsigned` iff THIS box's completed-install record carries `unsigned` on line 2, read before `cmd_update` removes it; the verb has no `--allow-unsigned` flag of its own. Spec §11 states the rule for arm 2 (the pre-update marker) and is silent on a standalone rollback. A verified box never silently unsigns: its rollback to a release that ships no bundle refuses with `_upd_fetch`'s own sentence (a `provenance: `-prefixed report, D-3239), and the by-hand remedy is `ccrc update --to <tag> --downgrade --allow-unsigned`. A bundle that FAILS verification refuses either way. Cost if wrong: a verified box's operator types the update form once.
- **D-3264** (found planning Task 7) — D-3240's remedy, `ccrc update --to <v> --force`, is refused on a rollback: the target is below the floor and `--force` does not pass the floor (M7, Task 14). For `UPD_FROM ∈ rollback|watchdog` the sentence names `ccrc rollback --to <v>` instead, through one helper (`_upd_rerun_hint`): the box reads `incomplete` (no completed-install record), so `_upd_converged` answers 1 and the rerun re-installs. Cost if wrong: none — every other run's sentence is byte-identical.
- **D-3265** (found planning Task 8) — the reader refuses as `malformed` an `epoch`, `issued` or `lease` wider than 18 digits, though spec §9's grammar (`0|[1-9][0-9]*`) sets no width. Bash arithmetic is 64-bit and wraps silently: measured, `$(( 10#99999999999999999999 ))` is `7766279631452241919`, so a 20-digit lease compares as in force until the year 246 billion — a garbage document read as `ok`, the fail-open direction this reader exists to close. Eighteen digits is the widest decimal that cannot wrap (`10^18 − 1 < 2^63 − 1`) and is far past any unix-seconds value; Task 10's puller refuses anything over 11 digits for `issued`/`lease` (D-3270), so the two layers disagree only in the refusing direction. `ccd/ccd`'s `_acct_pool_state` carries the same unbounded grammar and the same wrap; it is out of scope here and named so it is not rediscovered. Cost if wrong: none — no writer emits a number that wide.
- **D-3266** (found reviewing Task 8) — spec §9 says "`desired none` → refuse", and `ccrc update` does; `ccrc update --check` does NOT. It reads a `none` line as "the control plane names nothing newer", compares the box against its own stamped tag (`target=<its tag>`, nothing fetched), and answers `current`/exit 0 on a box whose install completed, `incomplete`/exit 1 on one whose install did not, with the `none` sentence on the line after the machine line. The reason: W2's resolver answers `desired none` for every CONVERGED managed node (it names a tag only when one is strictly newer than the floor — W2's `resolveOnChannel`, `RESOLVE_DETAIL.notNewerThanFloor` — and a completed install raises the floor to the running tag), so a refusing `--check` would exit 1 with no `check:` line on every healthy managed box, where spec §14 has `--check` compare and exit 0 when current. A box with no stamped version still refuses, having nothing to compare. Cost if wrong: a `none` that is the server DECLINING (an ineligible pin, an unknown channel, no floor) also reads `current` in `--check` when the box's install completed — the node cannot tell the two apart, because the document carries no reason (D-3245) — so a script keyed on `--check`'s exit code sees 0 there; the second line still says the control plane named no target.
- **D-3267** (found planning Task 9) — spec §11 says only "a live holder → exit 0". Probing the lock and then acting leaves a window: an operator's fresh `ccrc update` takes the lock and writes `resolving`, and the watchdog then overwrites that live report with `failed: abandoned…`. So the watchdog takes `flock -n` itself on its own descriptor, keeps it through the re-measure and the rewrite, and releases it BEFORE `ccrc rollback --from watchdog`, which takes the lock itself; a refused rollback is recorded only when `flock -n` succeeds again and the report's `updatedAt` has not moved. An open or flock failure that is not contention is the probe's rc 3 and exits 0 with `watchdog: the update lock could not be measured — not acting` (ruling R16, D-3250). Cost if wrong: none measured; one extra open of the lock file per tick.
- **D-3268** (found planning Task 9) — a stale report on a box that passes the probe and is AT the report's target version, but whose `~/.ccrc/installed` does not name the stamp's sha (the spine died after `_inst_stamp`, before `_inst_installed`). This is neither the spec's converged case nor D-3246, whose sentence would say "not at <target>" when it is. The watchdog writes `failed: 'abandoned by its updater; box answers healthy on <v> but its install never completed (the completed-install record does not name its stamp); rerun: ccrc update --to <v> --force'`, exits 0, and never rolls back, because only a failing probe reverts. Cost if wrong: an operator reruns with `--force` instead of the box being called converged.
- **D-3269** (found planning Task 9) — the spec's unit pair names no timeout, and `systemd.service(5)` confirms a oneshot has none by default; while the unit runs, its timer starts no second instance, so a hung rollback (a download that never ends) would silence the one actor meant to bound a wedged update. `ccrc-update-watchdog.service` carries `TimeoutStartSec=1800`, twice the default deadline; on expiry systemd stops the cgroup and the next tick re-measures — at most one rollback attempt per 30 minutes on a box that stays unhealthy. Cost if wrong: a rollback slower than 30 minutes is cut short and retried.
- **D-3270** (found planning Task 10) — spec §9 says the puller validates the whole document against the grammar. The grammar alone accepts a 13-digit millisecond `issued`/`lease`, which the reader then reads as a lease ~56,700 years away (`ok`, never `stale`: the C1 defect at `server.ts:2679-2688`), and the reader cannot see it. So `ccd-update-sync` adds a VALUE pass after the whole-document pass: `issued` and `lease` carry at most 11 digits (W2's `REPORT_TIME_MAX_S` bound, unix seconds until 5138); `|issued − now| ≤ 86400` (further out, the node cannot judge a 15-minute lease, and a clock that is behind would read an ended lease as live); `issued ≤ lease ≤ issued + 86400`; and `desired` equals `desired-<channel>`, as §9 defines it. These are the semantic checks W2's embedded validator applied, minus its `lease − issued == 900`, which would tie every node to a server constant. Disclosed: removing only the digit check leaves the verdict unchanged (the clock bound and lease window still refuse), so its test pins the diagnostic message. Cost if wrong: a node whose clock is more than a day off refuses to sync, with a sentence saying so.
- **D-3271** (found planning Task 11) — spec §12 gives two inputs and one rule: FAIL iff reachable and not armed. It does not cover `$CCRC_EXPOSURE_FILE` present but not a readable regular file: its `CCRC_AUTH` would have won, so neither answer can be given. The check WARNs that whether `POST /api/updates/apply` is gated "was not measured", before any armed/reachable verdict; the existing `exposure` check already FAILs that file on its own terms. Cost if wrong: that one state gets a WARN instead of a guessed PASS or FAIL.
- **D-3272** (found planning Task 11; RULED by the coordinator 2026-09-23: D-139 stands and Task 11 implements the PASS alternative below — reversible by the operator) — the `unsigned` mark is written for every install `ccrc update` did not verify, which includes every box's FIRST install (a checkout `ccrc install`, `install.sh --release`); so from this wave on a clean fresh install's doctor tail closes yellow with one `provenance` WARN until the box's first verified `ccrc update`. That reverses, for this one check, operator ruling D-139 ("a fresh install ends green", recorded at `ccrc-install.test.ts:3228-3237`, where `auth` was made a PASS carrying next-steps text for the same reason). The test that pins D-139 (`:3216`) does not catch it — its fixture has no git stamp, so `provenance` SKIPs there (measured `0 warned`). Spec §11 says WARN and Task 11's interface follows it; the alternative, if D-139 stands, is written out in Task 11: the `unsigned` arm becomes a `_dr_pass` carrying the same next-steps text. Cost if wrong: every fresh install shows one standing WARN until its first update.
- **D-3273** (found planning Task 12) — `ccrc rollout` refuses at exit 2, before either box is touched, any box whose `--check` line reads `floor=unreadable` or `floor=malformed`: `rollout: the <label> box's ~/.ccrc/floor is <word> — its update would refuse; fix it on that box first ('ccrc update --check' there names it); nothing was touched`, with or without `--downgrade` — that box's own `ccrc update` would die on the floor file either way (`_upd_floor_check`'s unreadable and malformed refusals precede its `--downgrade` branch), and letting the rollout go ahead would move the first box and stop at the second, the half-moved fleet M3 exists to prevent. The spec names only the `below-floor` refusal. Cost if wrong: an operator fixes a corrupt floor file one step earlier, with nothing moved.
- **D-3274** (found reviewing Task 2) — `_upd_lock`'s acquisition tells contention from a flock that could not run, the way D-3250's probe does: `flock -n` rc 1 is `another update holds …`; any other rc dies `cannot lock ~/.ccrc/update.lock (flock rc <n>) — this is not another update holding it`. The plan's text read every acquisition failure as a holder, so a `Bad file descriptor` or `ENOLCK` refused every update while naming a holder that does not exist («No overloaded null at a seam»). Cost if wrong: none — both arms refuse; only the sentence differs.
- **D-3275** (found reviewing Task 6) — arm 2 counts a restore child that exits 3 as RESTORED, not failed. The plan's text sent every non-zero child to arm 3, but the child is a real `ccrc update` whose exit 3 means its spine completed and wrote its record and only its trailing doctor failed (D-3114) — the box is whole on the previous release. Arm 3 over it would delete the record the child just wrote and report a MIXED tree that is not mixed, and on any box with a standing doctor FAIL no restore could ever take arm 2. The `reverted` detail carries `(its doctor exited 3)`, so the console still shows the box is unhealthy. Cost if wrong: a box whose previous release installs but reports doctor FAILs is left on that release with its FAIL lines, instead of a MIXED tree with the same FAILs.
- **D-3276** (found reviewing Task 9) — the watchdog rolls back only a box whose tree this update may have moved, and only onto a tagged baseline. Spec §11 rolls back on "a stale report with a failing health probe", but `~/.ccrc/previous` is written at the END of `backing-up`, so a report stale in `queued`, `resolving`, `fetching`, `verifying` or `backing-up` still names the build BEFORE the running one — a rollback there undoes an update this run never applied. Those phases (D-3246's (a) set, stated once) rewrite `failed: 'abandoned by its updater; box unhealthy (<why>) and its tree never moved; nothing reverted'`; and a box whose running stamp carries no version (a deploy.sh push) is never rolled back (`… on an unversioned tree; not reverting`). Cost if wrong: an unhealthy box whose updater died before its tree moved waits for an operator instead of being downgraded one release further than it ever went.
- **D-3277** (found reviewing Task 9) — the watchdog re-reads the report UNDER its lock and stands down if `phase` or `updatedAt` moved since its first read (`watchdog: the report moved while measuring — next tick`, exit 0). D-3267 held the lock across the re-measure and the rewrite, but the report itself was read before `flock -n`, so an updater that wrote `done` and exited in that window had its terminal report overwritten, or its finished box rolled back. Cost if wrong: one extra jq read per tick.
- **D-3278** (found reviewing Task 9) — the watchdog's failing verdict needs three failing probe samples, `CCRC_WATCHDOG_PROBE_GAP_S` (default 5) seconds apart, taken under its lock; one passing sample is a pass. Spec §11 says "a failing health probe" without a count, and the update's own gate retries for 90 s, so one curl timeout or one `activating` sample during an unrelated restart would otherwise roll a box back — on every tick, forever, for a report D-3246 leaves non-terminal. Cost if wrong: a genuinely dead box is rolled back ~10 s later.
- **D-3279** (found reviewing Task 10) — `ccd-update-sync` refuses an `epoch` wider than 18 digits, the reader's own bound (D-3265). The plan's validator bounded `issued` and `lease` (D-3270) but left `epoch` to the grammar's unbounded `0|[1-9][0-9]*`, so a 20-digit `epoch` was installed over a good in-lease projection and the reader then refused every no-`--to` update as `malformed`, with a remedy that re-installed the same document. The puller must never install what the reader refuses. Cost if wrong: none — no writer emits an epoch that wide.
- **D-3280** (found reviewing Task 10) — `ccd-update-sync` hands the response body to its validator as BYTES from a bounded temp file: curl writes it with `--max-filesize 65536`, and the validator refuses a NUL byte and an over-cap body before decoding. The plan captured the body with `$( … )`, which silently drops NUL bytes — a malformed answer was repaired and installed (`ep\0och` became `epoch`) rather than refused — and held an unbounded body in memory until after the grammar pass. `ccd-pool-sync` shares both shapes; it is out of scope here and named so it is not rediscovered. Cost if wrong: one temp file per tick.
- **D-3281** (found reviewing Task 12; reason text amended by review fix round 1 m1, D-3289) — `rollout` refuses before touching either box any box whose `floor=` is a tag newer than the pinned target, WHATEVER its state word, unless `--downgrade` was typed (and then passes it through). D-3233 refused only `below-floor`, which `--check` never answers for a `current` box, and rollout still runs `update --to <tag>` on a current box when the other box moves. At the time this was found, `cmd_update` checked the floor before its converged no-op unconditionally, so a rolled-back box (current on an older tag, its floor still above it) would have died at its floor check after the first box had moved. D-3289 (fix round 1 I5) narrowed that ordering: the floor is now checked before the converged no-op only when the target differs from the box's own running version — for a box already current on the pinned target, the floor check is deferred until AFTER the converged no-op, so it would no-op rather than die there. The behaviour this entry describes is KEPT anyway (rollout pins one version fleet-wide, and refusing this box on its OWN reported floor before either box is touched is stricter than a bare `cmd_update` run needs but keeps `--downgrade` a real, explicit authorization rather than leaving it to each box's own converged check). Cost if wrong: an operator types `--downgrade` for a box that would have no-opped.
- **D-3282** (found in the final review) — `ccrc-update-watchdog.service` PREPENDS `%h/.local/bin` to the PATH it inherits from the user manager instead of replacing it. The plan copied `ccrc-models.service`'s `Environment=PATH=%h/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`, but the watchdog's one real act is `ccrc rollback`, whose `cmd_update` preflights `node` — and a box whose `node` is reachable only through the manager's PATH (as `ccrc.service` finds it) would die there, record a terminal refusal, and never be re-measured. Cost if wrong: a PATH longer by the manager's entries.
- **D-3283** (found in the final review; AMENDED in place, fix round 1 item 2 / review 155 C1 — the shape below is the ruled one, replacing this entry's own pre-amendment text, which argued the opposite) — `previous` names the LAST DIFFERENT release that ran before the current one; it is the bare-rollback target. A same-tag reinstall (`update --to <running tag> --force`, and every `rollout --force` on a converged box) is not a MOVE, so `_upd_write_previous`'s same-tag keep (D-3254 (a)) leaves `previous` UNTOUCHED regardless of whether THIS box's own install of the running tag ever completed — the completed-install record's agreement no longer matters to this arm at all. (This entry's own pre-amendment text made the opposite call: it kept `previous` only when the record was absent or named a sha OTHER than the running stamp's, and otherwise WROTE the running build as `previous` — reasoning that a record naming the running stamp's own sha means that build is a completed baseline. That write was itself the defect review 155 found (C1): it made a later bare `ccrc rollback`, after a failed same-tag reinstall, roll the box FORWARD onto the tag whose reinstall just failed, and lost the tag that last completed as a rollback target.) The restore-target half of this entry's original argument — arm 2 "restoring a release one BELOW the one the box actually ran" — is answered structurally instead, not by writing `previous`: `_upd_restore_arm2` now skips itself outright whenever this run's target is the tag that was already running (re-installing that tag is what just failed its gate, so there is nothing for arm 2 to restore TO), with its own stdout line, and falls straight to arm 3, the pre-update backup — which for a same-tag run IS that same release, so arm 3 is not mixing trees. Cost if wrong: a failed same-tag reinstall's automatic restore corrupts `previous` (rolling a later bare rollback forward onto the release that just failed) or falsely reports `REVERTED (arm 2)` for work arm 2 never did.
- **D-3284** (found in the final review) — `_upd_fetch`'s bundle fetch now captures `-w '%{http_code}'` exactly as `_upd_asset_listed` (D-3261) does, and only a MEASURED 404 is treated as "the release ships no provenance bundle" (kept `provenance: `-prefixed, admitted under `--allow-unsigned`); any other status or curl failure dies WITHOUT the prefix, verdict-first, naming the status as a transient fetch failure; the plan's `_upd_fetch` sent every `curl -f` exit 22 — which is ANY HTTP status ≥ 400, D-3143's own lesson — to the `provenance: `-prefixed die, so a transient 502/503/403 from the release host became a lasting per-node refusal of a good tag once W2's sweep read the prefix, breaking D-3239's own invariant that a node fault must halt, never refuse a release fleet-wide. Cost if wrong: one node stops seeing an otherwise-good release until an operator acks the refusal.
- **D-3285** (found in the final review) — three remedies that could not run now can: (i) `cmd_rollback` measures convergence itself (running stamp's version and sha against the completed-install record) before calling `cmd_update`, and prints `... --downgrade --force` with `return 0` instead of falling into `cmd_update`'s own `--force`-to-reinstall no-op, which `rollback` has no flag for and the floor refuses anyway; (ii) `_upd_rerun_hint` groups `restore` with `rollback`/`watchdog` (the `ccrc rollback --to <v>` form), since a `--from restore` child (arm 2) dies under the same raised floor its own parent already completed; (iii) `_upd_restore_arm2`'s arm2-refused by-hand remedy gained `--downgrade`, which the now-raised floor requires; the plan wrote all four remedies against a floor state that only held before the wave's own completed spine raised it, so each printed a command the box's own floor check would refuse the moment an operator followed it. (i)'s pre-check is only for a rollback typed by hand (`--from cli`, the default); every other caller reaches `cmd_update`'s converged path, which closes its report — the pre-check's own early `return 0` wrote none, so a `--from watchdog`/`--from pwa` run landing there left `update.json` stuck in-flight forever, and the watchdog would re-run the same rollback on every later tick. Cost if wrong: an operator follows a printed remedy and is refused a second time, with no working command left visible.
- **D-3286** (found in the final review) — `_check_provenance`'s unsigned-install PASS detail is reworded to match README's own final-review fix for the identical sentence: "the next `ccrc update` that installs a release (a newer one, or `--force` on this one) verifies it and clears the mark", replacing "the next ccrc update verifies"; the plan's (and phase A's coordinator-ruled) wording was false on exactly the box it describes — a box already at its target no-ops at `_upd_converged` before the staged spine ever runs, so the mark and the PASS both survive unchanged, never verified by "the next" update. The verdict (PASS, D-139) is unchanged. Cost if wrong: an operator reads a false promise that a plain `ccrc update` will clear a stale unsigned mark.
- **D-3287** (found by the wave's gate) — `install-census.test.ts`'s deploy.sh parity describe (#171, merged after this plan) withholds `ccd-update-sync` and the two update unit pairs by an exact, two-sided list: each must be placed by `ccrc install` and must NOT be placed by `deploy/deploy.sh`. Spec §19 leaves deploy.sh untouched, and the reader's role table depends on it: a deploy.sh fleet box with `ccd-update-sync.timer`'s unit file on disk would read "configured, never synced" and refuse every update without `--to`, where today it follows stable. Cost if wrong: a deploy.sh box follows stable and has no watchdog — the spec's stated behaviour for the fallback.
- **D-3288** (found in fix round 1, review 155 C1) — `_upd_restore_arm3`'s stdout line and its `update.json` detail say the tree is MIXED and name `deploy.sh` as the remedy unconditionally, which spec §11 arm 3 prescribes; a same-tag run (item 2's fix round 1 change) whose STAGED sha turns out equal to the OLD (running) build's sha is a genuine REPEAT, not a rebuild — the backup arm 3 copies back and the tree the new install just replaced are the SAME content, so nothing is mixed, and `deploy.sh` is the wrong remedy for a box whose gate failed for a reason that has nothing to do with a mismatched tree (its own health, most likely, or a transient probe failure). Arm 3 now compares `old_sha` (the running build's sha, captured before this run's spine cleared the completed-install record) against `UPD_STAGED_SHA` (the extracted tree's own sha) whenever `old_version` equals the target: equal says "this box's tree is `<tag>` again, the SAME release that was running before this update; nothing is mixed", names `ccrc doctor` and a plain reinstall as the remedy, and writes `arm3: restored <tag> (same build, not mixed)`; a same tag with a DIFFERENT sha still says MIXED, deploy.sh, exactly as before. Cost if wrong: an operator is told to run deploy.sh (or is left thinking the tree needs it) when a plain reinstall or a health check would have sufficed, or vice versa.
- **D-3289** (found in fix round 1, review 155-on-review I5) — spec §5's order ("`SHA256SUMS` → the tag is bound → the floor is checked (§9) → tarball → …") is followed for every target EXCEPT one: a target equal to the RUNNING version, where `cmd_update` now checks the floor AFTER the fetch (D-3283's own reasoning, narrowed) rather than before. `_upd_converged`'s first comparison (the running stamp's version against the resolved target) already answers "not converged" by construction whenever the versions differ, `--force` was typed, or no version is running at all — so in every one of those cases checking the floor before the fetch drops none of `_upd_converged`'s three comparisons and the below-floor refusal fires without the network spend, the verifier run, and the two extra `update.json` phases (`fetching`, `verifying`) a full fetch costs; measuring this (review 155-on-review, concern 2) also found the refusal REASON could change — a fetch failure (a `provenance: ` verdict, a transient error) can now win over the floor's own sentence when the fetch runs first. Only when the running version equals the target does convergence remain genuinely undecided until the staged sha is known, so the floor check is deferred there, exactly as fix round 1 item 17 shipped for every target. Cost if wrong: a below-floor target whose version differs from the running one pays the fetch, or reports the fetch's own failure instead of the floor's, before refusing.

### Task 1: `update.json` and `--from`

**Files:**
- Modify: `ccd/ccrc` — the node-files constants (inserted after `CCRC_CAP_WORDS=(verify node-id floor)`, `:1144`, so W1's "W1's words" comment stays attached to its line — the block that starts at `BOX_FLOOR_FILE`, `:1141`); the `UPD_*` globals (after `UPD_PROVENANCE=""`, `:1406`); `_ccrc_die` (`:1607`); `cmd_update`'s argument loop (`:11306-11321`), the `--to` shape check (`:11322-11326`) and D-3139 refusals (`:11333-11344`); the line after the `--check` arm's closing `fi` (`:11372`); the call sequence (`:11414-11425`), the `installing` line (`:11440`) and tail (`:11485-11488`); new `_upd_phase` and `_upd_json_str` after `_upd_fleet_warn` (`:11497-11506`); `_upd_fetch` (`:11565`: one phase call after the tarball download at `:11568-11569`; `UPD_FAIL_PREFIX` before its two verdict dies at `:11605-11606` and `:11621`); `_upd_floor_check` (`:11676-11702`); `usage()`'s `update` entry (`:1530-1549`, the last two lines `:1548-1549`)
- Test: `server/test/ccrc-update.test.ts` — `const REAL_MV` beside `REAL_NODE` (`:60`); `updateEnv` (`:152`) gains the `mv` recorder after `plant('rsync', …)` (`:254-255`); the D-3114 exit-3 case (`:696-719`) gains its report assertion; new file-scope readers and a new describe `ccrc update: update.json at every phase, and --from` appended at the end of the file (after the floor describe, `:1665-1781`)

**Interfaces:**
- Constants: `BOX_UPDATE_JSON="$HOME/.ccrc/update.json"`; `UPD_FROM_WORDS=(cli pwa restore rollback watchdog rollout)` — the one bash spelling of the vocabulary (D-3228); every sentence that lists it expands `${UPD_FROM_WORDS[*]}`, never a second hand copy.
- Globals (declared after `UPD_PROVENANCE`, `:1406`): `UPD_FROM="cli"`, `UPD_REPORTING=0`, `UPD_REPORT_TARGET=""`, `UPD_REPORT_STARTED=""`, `UPD_REPORT_PID=""`, `UPD_FAIL_PREFIX=""`. None is ever exported.
- argv: `ccrc update [--from <word>] | [--from=<word>]`. `--from` with no value → exit 2, stderr `ccrc: --from needs a value: one of cli pwa restore rollback watchdog rollout` then `usage`. A word outside `UPD_FROM_WORDS` → exit 2, `ccrc: --from expects one of cli pwa restore rollback watchdog rollout (got: <w>)` then `usage`. `--check` with `--from` → exit 2, `ccrc: update: --check and --from are exclusive — --check measures and writes nothing, --from attributes a run that moves this box; pick one` (one more `if` in the D-3139 block, its shape).
- `_upd_phase <phase> [detail]` → rc 0 ALWAYS, never calls `_ccrc_die`. Writes `$BOX_UPDATE_JSON` as ONE line of JSON plus `\n`, keys in exactly this order: `{"target":<"vX.Y.Z"|null>,"phase":"<phase>","startedAt":<int>,"updatedAt":<int>,"detail":<"…"|null>,"from":"<word>","pid":<int>}`. `target` = `$UPD_REPORT_TARGET` when it matches the tag shape, else `null`. Times are unix **SECONDS** from `date +%s` (portable to macOS; the unit is SETTLED with W2 — its committed Task 11 `reportFrom` reads `startedAt`/`updatedAt` as seconds, converts ONCE to ms, and reads a value above `REPORT_TIME_MAX_S = 99_999_999_999` — a ms stamp — as `null`; its precedence rule is `startedAt*1000 + 999 >= updateStartedAt` (W2's D-3199). `CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS` stays a millisecond knob, which only Task 9's watchdog divides by 1000). `now` must match `^[1-9][0-9]{0,10}$` (≤ `REPORT_TIME_MAX_S`'s eleven digits) or the phase is not written — the WARN below, because a `date` that did not answer would otherwise stage `"startedAt":,` (**added**: `pathWithoutJq`'s PATH carries no `date`). `startedAt` = `$UPD_REPORT_STARTED` when it is seconds-shaped by the same pattern, else set to `now` (the process's first call, or a preset Task 9 read from a report that was not seconds); `updatedAt` = now. `from` = `$UPD_FROM`. `pid` = `${UPD_REPORT_PID:-$$}` (D-3237). `~/.ccrc` made when absent; staged at `$BOX_UPDATE_JSON.tmp.$$`, `chmod 644`, placed by `mv -f --` (the rename the test observes). **Corrected:** a DIRECTORY at `$BOX_UPDATE_JSON` is refused before the `mv` (a `mv` onto a writable directory moves the file INTO it and succeeds — the shape `ccrc-install.test.ts:4084`'s D-3135 case records for `installed`). On any failure: `rm -f` the temp, stdout `update: WARN: could not write ~/.ccrc/update.json (phase <phase>) — the console will not see this phase; the update continues`.
- `_upd_json_str <s>` → stdout the JSON value for a detail: `null` for empty; else — **corrected** — the three non-ASCII characters this file's sentences use are first spelled in ASCII (`—` → `-`, `…` → `...`, `→` → `->`), then under `LC_ALL=C` every byte outside 0x20–0x7E becomes `?`, the result is cut to 200 characters, then `\` → `\\` and `"` → `\"`, wrapped in `"` (spec §8's bound, applied by the writer as well as W2's reader). Declared as a SUBSHELL function (`_upd_json_str() ( … )`) so its `LC_ALL=C` can never leak into the caller. Without the ASCII spelling every die sentence would reach the console with `???` for each em dash (D-3249, found planning this task).
- `_ccrc_die() { echo "$PROG: $*" >&2; [ "${UPD_REPORTING:-0}" = 1 ] && [ "$BASHPID" = "$$" ] && _upd_phase failed "${UPD_FAIL_PREFIX:-}$*"; exit 1; }` — the one hook that makes every die after the lock a `failed` report. **Corrected** (two additions to the skeleton's line): `[ "$BASHPID" = "$$" ]` keeps a die inside a command substitution — a subshell, which ends only itself — from reporting a failure the run never had (measured: no die sits inside a `$(…)` on the update path at `d759c914`, so this is defence, pinned by the extraction test below); `${UPD_FAIL_PREFIX:-}` because `ccrc-install.test.ts:4133` extracts this definition by `^_ccrc_die\(\) \{.*\}$` and runs it ALONE under `set -u` — **it must stay one line**. `UPD_REPORTING=1` is set by `cmd_update` on the install path only (in this task right after the `--check` branch returns; Task 2 moves it to the line after `_upd_lock`). `UPD_FAIL_PREFIX="provenance: "` is set immediately before exactly two dies in `_upd_fetch` — "provenance verification FAILED …" and "the release ships no provenance bundle …" — and nowhere else (D-3239).
- Phases this task wires in `cmd_update`: `resolving` before `_upd_resolve`; `fetching` before `_upd_fetch`; `verifying` inside `_upd_fetch` after the tarball's `curl`, before `_plat_sha256_check`; `backing-up` before `_upd_backup`; `installing` before the staged spine; `restarting` before `_upd_sweep`; `done` after `_upd_report` (detail null; on the D-3114 arm `doctor exited <rc> — the box moved; its health is ccrc doctor's`, which `_upd_json_str` writes as `doctor exited <rc> - the box moved; its health is ccrc doctor's`); `done` with detail `already converged at <v>` on the `_upd_converged` no-op; `failed` through `_ccrc_die`. `UPD_REPORT_TARGET` = `$to` at parse when given, `$UPD_VERSION` after `_upd_resolve`. Later tasks wire `queued` (Task 3), `checking` (Task 5), `restoring` and `reverted` (Task 6); no writer ever writes `unknown`.
- `_upd_floor_check <via> <downgrade> <from>` (replaces `<to> <downgrade>`): `via` is `--to vX.Y.Z` or `latest/download`, computed by the caller (Task 8 adds `the control plane (channel <c>)`). `from ∈ restore|rollback|watchdog` proceeds below the floor with stdout `update: WARN: <v> is below this box's floor <f> (resolved by <via>) — proceeding because this run is --from <from>; the floor stays <f>`. W1's two sentences (`:11697-11701`) stay byte-identical; `--downgrade` is tested first, so a run carrying both prints W1's line.
- `usage()`'s `update` entry gains one sentence (the report and `--from`); **corrected** — the skeleton's Files list names `usage()` and its Interfaces did not say what it gains.
- Harness: `updateEnv` plants an `mv` recorder in the fixture's `~/.local/bin` (the harness bin, first on PATH — `ccdWsHelpers.ts:214-218`): when its last argument ends in `/.ccrc/update.json` it appends the SOURCE file's one line to `$HOME/update-json-writes` using shell builtins only (so it works on `pathWithoutJq`'s bare PATH), then `exec`s the real `mv` by the absolute path resolved when planted. The enumerating test holds spec §6's `UpdatePhase` minus `unknown` as a literal (Task 15 swaps it for W2's `UPDATE_PHASES`) and a `PENDING` set `{queued, checking, restoring, reverted}`, each member commented with the task that removes it; it asserts that the union of writes across its fixture runs ∪ `PENDING` equals the twelve, and that every recorded line parses with the seven keys in order. A provenance-refusal fixture asserts the final line's `detail` begins `provenance: `; a verifier-exit-127 fixture asserts it does not.
- Reads: nothing new. Env: nothing new. Mutation rows: "`update.json` at every phase" (remove one phase's call → red); the rename (a `cp` in place of the `mv` → the recorder sees nothing); the prefix (drop `UPD_FAIL_PREFIX` → the refusal fixture reds); the directory guard; the subshell guard; the floor's `--from` arm; the `--check --from` refusal; the report's unit (`date +%s` → `_plat_epoch_ms` → every phase WARNs; with the seconds guard also dropped → the fields case reds on `REPORT_TIME`).
