(d) Append at the end of the file:

```ts
// ── update.json (design 2026-09-20 §10) — the node's report ───────────────
/** Every report `_upd_phase` placed, in order: the recording `mv` in
 *  `updateEnv` appends the staged file's line each time its destination is
 *  `~/.ccrc/update.json`, so each entry here arrived by rename. */
const reportWrites = (home: string): Array<Record<string, unknown>> =>
  (existsSync(join(home, 'update-json-writes'))
    ? readFileSync(join(home, 'update-json-writes'), 'utf8').split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '')
      .map((l) => JSON.parse(l) as Record<string, unknown>)
    : []);
const lastReport = (home: string): Record<string, unknown> =>
  JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.json'), 'utf8')) as Record<string, unknown>;
/** The seven keys, in the writer's order (D-3237 adds `pid`). */
const REPORT_KEYS = ['target', 'phase', 'startedAt', 'updatedAt', 'detail', 'from', 'pid'];
/** The report's clock: unix SECONDS (`date +%s` on `_upd_phase`'s `now=`
 *  line) — the unit W2's `reportFrom` reads, converting once to ms and
 *  nulling anything above `REPORT_TIME_MAX_S` (a 13-digit ms stamp). Ten
 *  digits until the year 2286. */
const REPORT_TIME = /^\d{10}$/;

describe('ccrc update: update.json at every phase, and --from (design §10)', () => {
  // Spec §6's UpdatePhase minus `unknown` — which is the READER's word for a
  // token outside the vocabulary and which no writer ever writes. Task 15
  // swaps this literal for W2's `UPDATE_PHASES` once W2 has merged.
  const WRITTEN_PHASES = ['queued', 'resolving', 'fetching', 'verifying', 'backing-up', 'installing',
    'restarting', 'checking', 'restoring', 'done', 'reverted', 'failed'];
  // Phases a LATER task wires. Each task deletes its own member in the commit
  // that writes it; Task 6 deletes the literal, and the union assertion below
  // becomes total.
  const PENDING = new Set<string>([
    'queued',     // Task 3 — `--detach` writes it before the spawn
    'checking',   // Task 5 — the health gate
    'restoring',  // Task 6 — `_upd_restore`
    'reverted',   // Task 6 — `_upd_restore`'s last word
  ]);
  const phases = (home: string): string[] => reportWrites(home).map((w) => String(w['phase']));
  const plantFloor = (home: string, v: string): void => {
    mkdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc'), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'floor'), `${v}\n`);
  };

  it('a moving run, a converged no-op and a refusal together write every wired phase, each by rename, seven keys in order (§18 "update.json at every phase")', () => {
    // 1. A run that moves the box (STUB flavour: update's own logic).
    const moved = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-moved-');
    plantOldBox(moved, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    packRelease(moved, stubTree(moved, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0' });
    let r = runUpdate(moved);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    expect(phases(moved)).toEqual(['resolving', 'fetching', 'verifying', 'backing-up', 'installing', 'restarting', 'done']);

    // 2. The converged no-op (the "already there" gate's three shas agree).
    const same = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-same-');
    plantOldBox(same, { version: 'v2.0.0' });
    writeFileSync(join(same, '.ccrc', 'build.json'),
      shippedStamp('v2.0.0', 'newsha0000000000000000000000000000000000'));
    writeFileSync(join(same, '.ccrc', 'installed'), 'newsha0000000000000000000000000000000000\n');
    packRelease(same, stubTree(same, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0' });
    r = runUpdate(same);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    expect(phases(same)).toEqual(['resolving', 'fetching', 'verifying', 'done']);
    expect(lastReport(same)['detail']).toBe('already converged at v2.0.0');

    // 3. A refusal after the lock: a die is a `failed` report.
    const refused = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-refused-');
    plantOldBox(refused, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    packRelease(refused, stubTree(refused, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0', bundle: false });
    r = runUpdate(refused);
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(phases(refused)).toEqual(['resolving', 'fetching', 'verifying', 'failed']);

    const written = new Set([...phases(moved), ...phases(same), ...phases(refused)]);
    expect(written.has('unknown'), 'a writer wrote the reader\'s word').toBe(false);
    for (const p of PENDING) expect(written.has(p), `${p} is written but still listed PENDING`).toBe(false);
    expect([...new Set([...written, ...PENDING])].sort()).toEqual([...WRITTEN_PHASES].sort());

    for (const home of [moved, same, refused]) {
      const raw = readFileSync(join(home, 'update-json-writes'), 'utf8').split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '');
      for (const l of raw) expect(Object.keys(JSON.parse(l) as object)).toEqual(REPORT_KEYS);
      // The file on disk IS the last rename, and no staged copy is left beside it.
      expect(readFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.json'), 'utf8')).toBe(`${raw[raw.length - 1]}\n`);
      expect(readdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc')).filter((f) => f.startsWith('update.json.'))).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  it('the report names the target once resolved, carries ONE startedAt and a non-decreasing updatedAt in unix seconds, `from` cli by default, and the run\'s pid', () => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-fields-');
    plantOldBox(home, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    packRelease(home, stubTree(home, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0' });
    // The test's own clock around the spawn, in seconds: the report's times
    // are THIS instant in THIS unit, not merely ten digits.
    const t0 = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
    const r = runUpdate(home);
    const t1 = Math.ceil(Date.now() / 1000);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    const w = reportWrites(home);
    expect(w.length).toBe(7);
    // latest/download: nothing names a tag until SHA256SUMS has been read.
    expect(w[0]!['phase']).toBe('resolving');
    expect(w[0]!['target']).toBeNull();
    for (const x of w.slice(1)) expect(x['target']).toBe('v2.0.0');
    expect(new Set(w.map((x) => x['startedAt'])).size).toBe(1);
    expect(new Set(w.map((x) => x['pid'])).size).toBe(1);
    let prev = 0;
    for (const x of w) {
      expect(String(x['startedAt'])).toMatch(REPORT_TIME);
      expect(String(x['updatedAt'])).toMatch(REPORT_TIME);
      expect(Number(x['startedAt'])).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(t0);
      expect(Number(x['updatedAt'])).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t1);
      expect(Number(x['updatedAt'])).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(Math.max(prev, Number(x['startedAt'])));
      prev = Number(x['updatedAt']);
      expect(x['from']).toBe('cli');
      expect(Number.isInteger(x['pid'])).toBe(true);
      expect(x['detail']).toBeNull();   // no phase of a clean run carries one
    }
  });

  it('--from <word> and --from=<word> reach `from`; --to names the target from the first phase on', () => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-from-');
    plantOldBox(home, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    packRelease(home, stubTree(home, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0', latest: false });
    let r = runUpdate(home, ['--to', 'v2.0.0', '--from', 'pwa']);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    let w = reportWrites(home);
    expect(w.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const x of w) { expect(x['from']).toBe('pwa'); expect(x['target']).toBe('v2.0.0'); }
    const eq = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-from-eq-');
    plantOldBox(eq, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    packRelease(eq, stubTree(eq, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0' });
    r = runUpdate(eq, ['--from=rollout']);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    w = reportWrites(eq);
    for (const x of w) expect(x['from']).toBe('rollout');
  });

  const BAD_FROM: Array<[string[], RegExp]> = [
    [['--from', 'operator'], /^ccrc: --from expects one of cli pwa restore rollback watchdog rollout \(got: operator\)$/m],
    [['--from=CLI'], /^ccrc: --from expects one of cli pwa restore rollback watchdog rollout \(got: CLI\)$/m],
    [['--from'], /^ccrc: --from needs a value: one of cli pwa restore rollback watchdog rollout$/m],
  ];
  it.each(BAD_FROM)('%s is a usage error: exit 2, usage printed, nothing fetched, nothing reported (D-3228)', (args, msg) => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-badfrom-');

    expect(existsSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.json'))).toBe(false);

  it('--check and --from are exclusive — D-3139\'s shape: exit 2, nothing fetched, nothing reported', () => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-check-from-');
    const r = runUpdate(home, ['--check', '--from', 'pwa']);
    expect(r.code).toBe(2);
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/^ccrc: update: --check and --from are exclusive — --check measures and writes nothing, --from attributes a run that moves this box; pick one$/m);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'curl-argv')), 'a fetch ran before the refusal').toBe(false);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.json'))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a verdict on the RELEASE is reported `provenance: …` — the absent bundle and the failing one; a verifier that could not RUN is not (spec §8, D-3239)', () => {
    const detailOf = (home: string): string => {
      const rep = lastReport(home);
      expect(rep['phase']).toBe('failed');
      const d = String(rep['detail']);
      expect(d.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(200);

      return d;
    };
    const absent = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-prov-absent-');
    plantOldBox(absent, { version: 'v1.0.0' });

  it('a detail is printable ASCII, at most 200 characters, cut BEFORE it is escaped: a die naming a hostile URL arrives exactly', () => {
    // CCRC_RELEASE_BASE_URL is the one knob that puts arbitrary bytes into a
    // die sentence: `_upd_resolve`'s "download failed: <url>/SHA256SUMS …".
    // Position by position: "download failed: " (17) + "local://" (8) +
    // `é` — two UTF-8 bytes, two `?` — + `"` + `q` + `\` = 30, then 170 of
    // the 300 x's reach the 200-character cut, which runs before the two
    // escapes, so no escape is ever split.
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-detail-');
    const r = runUpdate(home, [], { CCRC_RELEASE_BASE_URL: `local://é"q\\${'x'.repeat(300)}` });
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/download failed: local:\/\//);
    const rep = lastReport(home);
    expect(rep['phase']).toBe('failed');
    expect(rep['detail']).toBe(`download failed: local://??"q\\${'x'.repeat(170)}`);
  });

  it('a report that cannot be written is a WARN line per phase and the update still completes — a directory squatting on the name is refused, never moved INTO', () => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-json-unwritable-');

    for (const from of ['restore', 'rollback', 'watchdog']) {

    expect(existsSync(join(pwa, 'ccrc-backups'))).toBe(false);

  it('_ccrc_die reports `failed` only once the run is reporting, only from the run\'s own shell, with the prefix in front (the one hook)', () => {
    // `ccrc-install.test.ts:4133`'s idiom: the ONE-LINE definition extracted
    // from the shipped file and run alone, `_upd_phase` shadowed by a recorder.
    const src = readFileSync(join(REPO, 'ccd', 'ccrc'), 'utf8');
    const progLine = /^PROG=.*$/m.exec(src);
    const dieLine = /^_ccrc_die\(\) \{.*\}$/m.exec(src);
    expect(progLine, 'ccd/ccrc has no PROG=').not.toBeNull();
    expect(dieLine, 'ccd/ccrc has no one-line _ccrc_die').not.toBeNull();
    const home = mkTmp('ccrc-update-die-hook-');
    const rec = join(home, 'phase-calls');
    const run = (body: string): Result => {
      const p = spawnSync(BASH, ['-c', [
        'set -uo pipefail', progLine![0], dieLine![0],
        `_upd_phase() { printf '%s|%s\\n' "$1" "$2" >> '${rec}'; }`,
        'UPD_FAIL_PREFIX=""', body,
      ].join('\n')], { encoding: 'utf8' });
      return { code: p.status ?? -1, stdout: p.stdout ?? '', stderr: p.stderr ?? '' };
    };
    let r = run('UPD_REPORTING=0; _ccrc_die before the lock');
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(existsSync(rec), 'a die before the run reports wrote a report').toBe(false);
    r = run('UPD_REPORTING=1; x="$(_ccrc_die inside a command substitution)"; echo "survived:$?"');
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^survived:1$/m);
    expect(existsSync(rec), 'a subshell\'s die reported the RUN as failed').toBe(false);
    r = run('UPD_REPORTING=1; UPD_FAIL_PREFIX="provenance: "; _ccrc_die the release failed');

# `_ccrc_die` — a bare refusal: this run cannot continue. Always exits 1 —

(g) `_upd_phase` and `_upd_json_str` — after `_upd_fleet_warn`'s closing `}` (`grep -n '^_upd_fleet_warn() {' ccd/ccrc`, `:11497`; its `}` is the line before the blank line preceding `# ── _upd_resolve / _upd_fetch`), add:

```bash

# ── _upd_phase <phase> [detail] — the node reports (design 2026-09-20 §10) ─
# One JSON line, keys in a fixed order — target, phase, startedAt, updatedAt,
# detail, from, pid (plan D-3237) — staged beside the file and
# placed by `mv -f`, so a reader (the inventory sweep, the watchdog, the
# lock's refusal) sees the previous report or this one, never half of
# either. Times are unix SECONDS (`date +%s`, the same on GNU and BSD) — the
# unit the server's inventory reads, converting once to ms and refusing a
# value above eleven digits (a ms stamp) as null; so a `now` that is not
# seconds-shaped writes nothing, and a preset `startedAt` that is not falls
# to `now`. NEVER FAILS THE UPDATE: a report the console cannot read is a lost phase,
# not a reason to leave a box half-moved — every failure is one WARN line and
# rc 0, and it never calls `_ccrc_die` (which calls it). A directory at the
# name is refused rather than moved INTO, which `mv` would do silently.
_upd_phase() {
  local phase="$1" detail="${2:-}" now target="null" det tmp
  now="$(date +%s 2>/dev/null)"
  [[ "$now" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,10}$ ]] || now=""
  [[ "$UPD_REPORT_STARTED" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,10}$ ]] || UPD_REPORT_STARTED="$now"
  [[ "$UPD_REPORT_TARGET" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] && target="\"$UPD_REPORT_TARGET\""
  det="$(_upd_json_str "$detail")"
  tmp="$BOX_UPDATE_JSON.tmp.$$"
  if [ -n "$now" ] \
     && { [ -d "${BOX_UPDATE_JSON%/*}" ] || mkdir -p "${BOX_UPDATE_JSON%/*}"; } 2>/dev/null \
     && [ ! -d "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" ] \
     && { printf '{"target":%s,"phase":"%s","startedAt":%s,"updatedAt":%s,"detail":%s,"from":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
            "$target" "$phase" "$UPD_REPORT_STARTED" "$now" "$det" "$UPD_FROM" "${UPD_REPORT_PID:-$$}" > "$tmp"; } 2>/dev/null \
     && chmod 644 "$tmp" 2>/dev/null \
     && mv -f -- "$tmp" "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" 2>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi
  rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  echo "update: WARN: could not write ~/.ccrc/update.json (phase $phase) — the console will not see this phase; the update continues"
  return 0
}

# `_upd_json_str <s>` — the JSON value for a report's detail: `null` for
# empty, else a quoted string of at most 200 printable-ASCII characters
# (spec §8's bound, which W2's reader applies too — the writer never relies
# on it). This file's sentences use three non-ASCII characters; they are
# spelled in ASCII first, so a die reaches the console as words, not `???`
# (plan D-3249).
# Every other byte outside 0x20-0x7E becomes `?` under LC_ALL=C, the cut runs
# BEFORE the two escapes so no escape is ever split, and the body is a
# SUBSHELL so its LC_ALL can never leak into the caller.
_upd_json_str() (
  s="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$s" ] || { printf 'null'; exit 0; }
  s="${s//—/-}"; s="${s//…/...}"; s="${s//→/->}"
  LC_ALL=C
  s="${s//[! -~]/?}"
  s="${s:0:200}"
  bs='\' q='"'
  s="${s//"$bs"/"$bs$bs"}"
  s="${s//"$q"/"$bs$q"}"
  printf '"%s"' "$s"
)
```

**Interfaces:**
- Constant: `BOX_UPDATE_LOCK="$HOME/.ccrc/update.lock"` (opened `>>`, never written — D-3230). Globals: `UPD_LOCK_FD=""`, `UPD_LOCK_INHERITED=0`.
- `_upd_lock_probe` → rc 0 nobody holds the lock (a subshell `( { exec {p}>>"$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK"; } 2>/dev/null && flock -n "$p" )` succeeded), rc 1 somebody holds it, rc 2 `flock` is not on PATH. Opens and closes its own descriptor inside the subshell; never leaves one open. Used by Tasks 2, 3 and 9. **Corrected — two additions:** rc 3 = UNMEASURED (the lock file exists but cannot be opened, or `flock` failed with a code other than contention's 1); folding it into rc 1 would grant the restore-child exemption on no evidence, and into rc 0 would let `--detach` spawn past a lock it could not see — «No overloaded null at a seam». And an ABSENT lock file answers rc 0 without creating it (a file nobody created is a lock nobody holds; the probe writes nothing). Tasks 3 and 9 must add an rc-3 arm. This departs from spec §10's literal text (D-3250, found planning this task): "skips iff … a fresh non-blocking `flock -n` … in a subshell FAILS" counts a subshell that failed to OPEN the file as a failed flock, i.e. as an exemption.
- `_upd_lock` → rc 0 when this process holds the lock or legitimately inherits it; otherwise exits 1 through `_ccrc_die` BEFORE `UPD_REPORTING=1`, so a refused run writes nothing to `update.json`. In order:
  1. idempotent per process: `[ -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD" ] || [ "$UPD_LOCK_INHERITED" -eq 1 ]` → return 0 (`cmd_rollback` takes it, then calls `cmd_update` in-process — Task 7; `_acct_marker_lock`'s one-acquisition-per-process rule, `ccd/ccrc:6320-6331`).
  2. `command -v flock` absent → Linux: `flock (util-linux) is required by 'ccrc update' — it serialises updates and refuses rather than racing; nothing on this box was changed`; Darwin: `flock is required by 'ccrc update' — it serialises updates and refuses rather than racing — and macOS does not ship it. Install it: brew install flock. Nothing on this box was changed` (`cmd_install`'s Darwin sentence shape, `:9160-9161`).
  3. `CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD` set: equal to `$PPID` AND `_upd_lock_probe` answers 1 → `UPD_LOCK_INHERITED=1; unset CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD; return 0`. Equal to `$PPID` and the probe answers 0 → die `update: CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD names this run's parent (pid <PPID>) but nobody holds ~/.ccrc/update.lock — refusing; a restore child runs only under its parent's lock`. **Corrected:** equal to `$PPID` and the probe answers 3 → die `update: CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD names this run's parent (pid <PPID>) but ~/.ccrc/update.lock could not be measured (probe rc 3) — refusing; a restore child runs only under a lock it can see`. Any other value → `unset CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD`, acquire normally. No `-ef` identity test anywhere (`/dev/fd -ef` is false on macOS). The marker is unset in every branch, before anything can spawn.
  4. `~/.ccrc` made when absent (die `cannot create ~/.ccrc, so ~/.ccrc/update.lock cannot be taken — nothing on this box was changed`); `{ exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>>"$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK"; } 2>/dev/null` (the compound form, `ccd/ccd:4381-4410`; die `cannot open ~/.ccrc/update.lock — nothing on this box was changed` on failure); `flock -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD"` fails → `exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-; UPD_LOCK_FD=""` then die `update: another update holds ~/.ccrc/update.lock (<_upd_lock_holder>)`.
- `_upd_lock_holder` → stdout `pid <n>, target <v>` read from `$BOX_UPDATE_JSON` with `jq -r`; `pid unknown, target unknown` when the file is absent, unreadable or not JSON; rc 0. **Corrected:** each field is shape-checked before it is printed — `pid` `^[0-9]+$`, `target` the tag shape — and any other value reads `unknown` (the file is same-user-writable by every session on the box, spec §8's premise; nothing raw from it reaches the terminal); a missing `jq` reads `unknown` too (the lock is taken BEFORE the preflight that names jq). **Corrected again (fix pass):** the field is TYPED in jq before bash splits the line — `pid` printed only when it is a JSON number, else `-`; `target` printed through `@json` only when it is a JSON string, else `-` — so the line is always two tokens, the first whitespace-free. The earlier `"\(.pid // "") \(.target // "")"` + `read -r a b` let one field's value land in the other's slot, measured 2026-09-23 with jq 1.7: `{"pid":null,"target":"v9.9.9"}` printed `pid unknown, target unknown` (the empty pid collapses under IFS and `v9.9.9` lands in `a`), `{"pid":"4242 v1.2.3","target":"x"}` printed `pid 4242` (a STRING pid split into the pid slot), and `{"pid":4242,"target":"v1.0.0\nv2"}` printed `target v1.0.0` (a newline cut the value to a tag shape it does not have). With the typed program the three read `pid unknown, target v9.9.9`, `pid unknown, target unknown`, `pid 4242, target unknown`.
- `_upd_unlock` → `{ exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-; } 2>/dev/null || true; UPD_LOCK_FD=""`; a no-op for an inherited lock (the parent closes its own).
- Call sites: `_upd_lock` in `cmd_update` after every argument refusal and after Task 3's detach return, on the install path only (never on `--check`); `UPD_REPORTING=1` on the next line; `_upd_unlock` immediately before `_upd_sweep` and before every return after the lock (the converged no-op included).
- No grandchild inherits the marker or the fd: `spine_env` becomes `(env -u CCRC_UPDATE_VERIFIED -u CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD)` / `(env -u CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD CCRC_UPDATE_VERIFIED=1)`, and the staged spine's command line carries `{UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-`. Task 6's arm-2 child is the ONE child that keeps the fd. **Corrected — the mechanism:** what a `{UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-` written on a simple command does to the CALLING shell is not settled across the versions this file supports: bash(1) says a `{varname}` redirection "persists beyond the scope of the command … The varredir_close shell option manages this behavior", which for a close would drop THIS run's lock mid-install, while bash 5.2.21 measured on this box (2026-09-23, `cmd {G}>&-` then `ls /proc/$$/fd`) scopes the close to the command and the parent keeps the descriptor. The floor is bash 4.4, so the plan relies on neither reading. The spine runs as `( exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-; exec "${spine_env[@]}" "${spine[@]}" ) || inst_rc=$?` — the subshell closes ITS copy and execs; the parent's stays held. The two role arms collapse into one `spine` array. An inherited run (`UPD_LOCK_FD` empty) runs the spine bare — it has no descriptor number to close (named hazard below).
- Tests hold the lock with a real background holder — one `bash -c 'exec 9>>"$1" && flock 9 && exec sleep 30'` process, so the pid that holds it is the pid that is killed (a plain `flock <file> sleep 30` hands the descriptor to a `sleep` child that outlives a kill of `flock`) — killed in `afterEach`, beside a hand-written `update.json` naming a pid and a target. Mutation rows: "one update at a time" (remove the `flock -n` → a second run proceeds), "the lock exemption is measured" (remove the probe → a marker with no holder runs), "the lock closes before the sweep" — **corrected fixture**: the skeleton's "a `systemctl` stub that sleeps in `try-restart` … a second run started during it" needs a concurrent spawn, and spec §18's own row names the simpler shape, "a lingering stub pins the lock": `try-restart` leaves a `sleep 30` behind (descriptors 0–2 on `/dev/null`, so the runner's pipes close when the run does) and the run exits; a second run afterwards, on `pathWithoutJq`'s PATH, dies at its own jq sentence if the lock is free and at the lock's sentence if the sweep inherited the fd. Synchronous, and the same fixture measures the staged spine's closure (the STUB shim lingers the same way) on both OSes. **Added (fix pass, ruling R16 — "`_upd_lock_probe`'s rc 3 … gets an explicit arm in every caller (Tasks 2, 3, 9): the lock and `--detach` refuse with their own sentence"):** the rc-3 arm gets its own pin — a mode-000 `update.lock` with the marker equal to `$PPID` refuses with the probe-rc-3 sentence, and the same file with no marker refuses at acquisition's `cannot open` sentence (`it.skipIf(process.getuid?.() === 0)`, the suite's mode-000 idiom) — and a mutation row for it; and the holder case gains three field-alignment rows (`pid-null`, `pid-string`, `target-newline`).

**Named hazards (this task's text, for the reviewer):**
- **A report written after the unlock.** `_upd_unlock` runs before `_upd_sweep` (spec §10), so `_upd_report` and the final `_upd_phase done` run unlocked: a second `ccrc update` started inside that window writes its own `resolving`, and this run's `done` can land on top of it until the second run's next phase. The window is the sweep's length; W2's precedence guard (a report whose `startedAt` predates the row's `updateStartedAt` never moves the lease) is what bounds its effect for a dispatched run. Not fixed here — the order is the spec's.
- **An inherited run cannot close what it cannot name.** Arm 2's restore child (Task 6) inherits the parent's descriptor but not its NUMBER (`UPD_LOCK_FD` is never exported), so its own staged spine — the PREVIOUS release's `ccrc install` — inherits the parent's lock copy. Measured at `d759c914`: `awk 'NR>=9100 && NR<=11300' ccd/ccrc | grep -nE '(^|[^&])&[[:space:]]*$|&[[:space:]]*;|nohup|setsid|disown|tmux (new|start)|_svc_run_detached|systemd-run'` over the `_inst_*` spine answers nothing — restarts go through the user manager, which is not a child — so nothing in `ccd/ccrc`'s own spine lingers today (the installers it runs from `ccd/` were not audited). Task 6 decides whether the parent passes the number.

(a) Constant — after Task 1's `BOX_UPDATE_JSON="$HOME/.ccrc/update.json"` line (`grep -n '^BOX_UPDATE_JSON=' ccd/ccrc`) add:

```bash
# `~/.ccrc/update.lock` — one `ccrc update` (or `ccrc rollback`) at a time
# (design §10). Opened append-only and never written (plan
# D-3230): the holder's pid and target are read from
# update.json, never from the lock file's bytes.
BOX_UPDATE_LOCK="$HOME/.ccrc/update.lock"
```

(b) Globals — after Task 1's `UPD_FAIL_PREFIX=""` line (`grep -n '^UPD_FAIL_PREFIX=' ccd/ccrc`) add:

```bash
UPD_LOCK_FD=""          # the descriptor _upd_lock holds; "" when not held, or when inherited
UPD_LOCK_INHERITED=0    # 1 = a restore child under its parent's lock — measured by _upd_lock_probe, never assumed
```

(c) The four lock functions — after Task 1's `_upd_json_str`'s closing `)` (`grep -n '^_upd_json_str() (' ccd/ccrc`; its body ends at the first line that is exactly `)` after it), before `# ── _upd_resolve / _upd_fetch`:

```bash

# ── THE LOCK (design 2026-09-20 §10) — one update at a time ───────────────
# flock(2) on ~/.ccrc/update.lock, taken by `cmd_update` after its argument
# refusals (and after the --detach re-exec point, so a detached run inherits
# no descriptor) and before anything is fetched or reported. A bash lock fd
# is inherited by every child and pins the lock until the LAST inheritor
# exits (measured 2026-09-13, the D-2605 lock design), so it is closed before
# every spawn that could outlive the run: the staged spine runs in a subshell
# that closes it first, and `_upd_unlock` runs before `_upd_sweep`.
#
# `_upd_lock_probe` → rc 0 nobody holds it, rc 1 somebody does, rc 2 `flock`
# is not on PATH, rc 3 UNMEASURED (the file exists and could not be opened,
# or flock failed for a reason other than contention) — never folded into
# "held", which would grant the restore-child exemption on no evidence, nor
# into "free" (plan D-3250). A FRESH open in a subshell: flock conflicts are per open file
# description, so a successful `flock -n` there proves nobody holds it, and
# the probe's own descriptor dies with the subshell. An absent file is a
# lock nobody holds, answered without creating it.
_upd_lock_probe() {
  command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
  [ -e "$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK" ] || return 0
  ( { exec {p}>>"$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK"; } 2>/dev/null || exit 3
    flock -n "$p"; r=$?
    case "$r" in 0|1) exit "$r" ;; *) exit 3 ;; esac )
}

# `_upd_lock_holder` → "pid <n>, target <v>" off update.json. The file is
# same-user-writable by every session on the box (spec §8), so each field is
# shape-checked before it is printed and anything else reads "unknown" —
# as do an absent, unreadable or non-JSON file and a box with no jq (the
# lock is taken BEFORE the preflight that names jq). jq TYPES each field
# before bash splits the line — the pid only when it is a JSON number, the
# target only as a JSON string through @json (one line, quoted), `-` for
# anything else — so the line is always two tokens and one field's value
# can never land in the other's slot. rc 0.
_upd_lock_holder() {
  local out="" pid="unknown" target="unknown" a="" b=""
  if [ -f "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" ] && [ -r "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    out="$(jq -r 'if type == "object" then "\(if (.pid | type) == "number" then .pid else "-" end) \(if (.target | type) == "string" then (.target | @json) else "-" end)" else empty end' "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" 2>/dev/null)" || out=""
  fi
  read -r a b <<<"$out"
  [[ "$a" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && pid="$a"
  [[ "$b" =~ ^\"(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)\"$ ]] && target="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  printf 'pid %s, target %s' "$pid" "$target"
}

# `_upd_lock` → rc 0 holding the lock (or legitimately inheriting it), or it
# dies (exit 1) — BEFORE `cmd_update` sets UPD_REPORTING=1, so a refused run
# writes nothing to update.json and cannot overwrite the holder's report.
_upd_lock() {
  # ONE ACQUISITION PER PROCESS — `_acct_marker_lock`'s rule: a second
  # `exec {fd}>>` of the same path is a STRANGER to the first, and
  # `cmd_rollback` takes the lock and then calls `cmd_update` in-process.
  [ -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD" ] && return 0
  [ "$UPD_LOCK_INHERITED" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  if ! command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ "$CCD_OS" = darwin ]; then
      _ccrc_die "flock is required by 'ccrc update' — it serialises updates and refuses rather than racing — and macOS does not ship it. Install it: brew install flock. Nothing on this box was changed"
    fi
    _ccrc_die "flock (util-linux) is required by 'ccrc update' — it serialises updates and refuses rather than racing; nothing on this box was changed"
  fi
  # THE RESTORE CHILD'S EXEMPTION, DECIDED ON A MEASUREMENT (design §10).
  # `_upd_restore`'s arm 2 runs `ccrc update` as a synchronous, reaped,
  # direct child that inherits the parent's descriptor; it skips acquisition
  # iff the marker names its OWN parent AND a fresh probe finds the lock
  # held. The env alone never exempts: a marker with no holder is refused,
  # whatever it says. No `/dev/fd … -ef` identity test — false on macOS.
  # The marker is unset in every branch, before anything here can spawn.
  if [ -n "${CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD:-}" ]; then
    local held="$CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD" prc=0
    unset CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD
    if [ "$held" = "$PPID" ]; then
      _upd_lock_probe || prc=$?
      case "$prc" in
        1) UPD_LOCK_INHERITED=1; return 0 ;;
        0) _ccrc_die "update: CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD names this run's parent (pid $PPID) but nobody holds ~/.ccrc/update.lock — refusing; a restore child runs only under its parent's lock" ;;
        *) _ccrc_die "update: CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD names this run's parent (pid $PPID) but ~/.ccrc/update.lock could not be measured (probe rc $prc) — refusing; a restore child runs only under a lock it can see" ;;
      esac
    fi
  fi
  { [ -d "${BOX_UPDATE_LOCK%/*}" ] || mkdir -p "${BOX_UPDATE_LOCK%/*}"; } 2>/dev/null \
    || _ccrc_die "cannot create ~/.ccrc, so ~/.ccrc/update.lock cannot be taken — nothing on this box was changed"
  # The COMPOUND form: a bare `exec {fd}>>… 2>/dev/null` leaks bash's own
  # open-failure diagnostic (`ccd/ccd:4381-4410` records why).
  { exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>>"$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK"; } 2>/dev/null \
    || { UPD_LOCK_FD=""; _ccrc_die "cannot open ~/.ccrc/update.lock — nothing on this box was changed"; }
  if ! flock -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD"; then
    { exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-; } 2>/dev/null
    UPD_LOCK_FD=""
    _ccrc_die "update: another update holds ~/.ccrc/update.lock ($(_upd_lock_holder))"
  fi
  return 0
}

# `_upd_unlock` — closes THIS process's descriptor, which releases the lock
# unless a child still holds a copy (why it runs BEFORE the sweep). A no-op
# for an inherited lock: the parent closes its own.
_upd_unlock() {
  [ -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD" ] || return 0
  { exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-; } 2>/dev/null || true
  UPD_LOCK_FD=""
}
```

  if [ -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD" ]; then
    ( exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>&-; exec "${spine_env[@]}" "${spine[@]}" ) || inst_rc=$?
  else
    "${spine_env[@]}" "${spine[@]}" || inst_rc=$?
  fi
```

/** ONE ccrc function, run in a shell that SOURCED the checkout's ccd/ccrc (its

 *  whose arms the verb cannot reach on this platform — `CCD_OS` is computed
 *  from `$OSTYPE` at source time, so an assignment AFTER the `.` is the one
 *  way a Linux run measures a Darwin arm. */
function sourcedCcrc(home: string, script: string): Result {
  const r = spawnSync(BASH, ['-c', `. "$1"; ${script}`, 'ccrc-under-test', join(REPO, 'ccd', 'ccrc')],

  return { code: r.status ?? -1, stdout: r.stdout ?? '', stderr: r.stderr ?? '' };
}

- [ ] **Step 5: `_upd_detach` and the re-exec point**

Add immediately after `_upd_fleet_warn`'s closing `}` (`grep -n '^_upd_fleet_warn() {' ccd/ccrc`, `:11497` at `d759c914`):

```bash
# ── --detach (design §10, W4 Task 3) ───────────────────────────────────────
# A run that restarts `ccrc.service` / `ccrc-agent.service` from INSIDE that
# unit's cgroup dies with it: `_inst_enable`'s `systemctl --user restart` is a
# full restart and neither unit sets KillMode. `systemd-run --user --collect`
# (`_svc_run_detached`'s Linux arm) gives the real run a cgroup of its own —
# the one idiom in this tree measured to survive a unit restart (ccd's
# detached swap tail). macOS's arm is `nohup … &`, which promises less (its
# own comment), so macOS refuses by name and never writes the `detach` cap.
_upd_detach_os_check() {
  [ "$CCD_OS" = darwin ] && _ccrc_die "--detach is Linux-only (decision 17)"
  return 0
}

# `_upd_detach <verb> <tag> <from> [flag…]` — queue the run, hand it to a
# transient unit, return. Called with `update` by `cmd_update` and with
# `rollback` by `cmd_rollback`, both BEFORE `_upd_lock`: the parent never
# holds the lock, so the unit it spawns inherits no descriptor that could pin
# the lock after this process has gone (a bash lock fd is inherited by every
# child — measured 2026-09-13). The busy check is a PROBE, never an acquire,
# and it runs before the `queued` write: a queued report written over a live
# run's would erase what that run is doing. The flags are the caller's, in
# the caller's fixed order; the argv is the child's whole contract, because
# it runs under the user manager's environment, not this shell's.
_upd_detach() {
  local verb="$1" tag="$2" from="$3" prc=0 rc=0
  shift 3
  _upd_detach_os_check
  _upd_lock_probe || prc=$?
  # Every probe answer has its own arm (ruling R16). An UNMEASURED lock (rc 3,
  # or any rc the probe does not define) is neither held nor free. Folding it
  # into busy would print a holder nobody measured. Folding it into free would
  # spawn past a lock this box cannot see.
  case "$prc" in
    0) ;;
    1) _upd_busy_die ;;
    2) _upd_flock_die ;;
    *) _ccrc_die "update: ~/.ccrc/update.lock could not be measured (probe rc $prc) — refusing to detach a run past a lock this box cannot see; nothing on this box was changed" ;;
  esac
  UPD_REPORT_TARGET="$tag"
  UPD_FROM="$from"
  _upd_phase queued
  _svc_run_detached "$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" "$verb" --to "$tag" --from "$from" "$@" || rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    _upd_phase failed "detach: systemd-run exited $rc"
    _ccrc_die "update: could not start the detached run (systemd-run exited $rc) — nothing on this box was changed"
  fi
  echo "update: detached — '$verb --to $tag' runs as a transient systemd --user unit; its progress is ~/.ccrc/update.json"
}
```

  # unit could inherit. `--from` rides the argv (the child attributes its own
  # report); so does every flag typed with it, in one fixed order — dropping

  if [ "$detach" -eq 1 ]; then
    local -a dflags=()
    [ "$force" -eq 1 ] && dflags+=(--force)

    const home = freshBox('ccrc-install-step-blocked-');
    // A directory at the marker's path: `_plat_mv_notdir` refuses to place a

Add:

```bash
# `install-step` (design §11, W4 Task 4) — the spine step `ccrc install` is
# ENTERING, written before each step by `_inst_step` and removed by
# `_inst_installed` once the completed-install record is placed. A spine that
# died leaves it naming the step it died in; `cmd_update` reads it to tell a
# death before `_inst_tree` (nothing replaced) from one at or after it (the
# tree IS replaced — the unit may already run new code).
BOX_INSTALL_STEP_FILE="$HOME/.ccrc/install-step"
```

Immediately above `cmd_install() {` (`:9049`), add:

```bash
# ── THE SPINE, STATED ONCE (D-3241, W4 Task 4) ────────────
# `cmd_install` runs these in this order through `_inst_step`, and
# `cmd_update`'s spine-death classifier (`_upd_step_moved`) reads the same
# array to know which steps precede `_inst_tree`. One list: a step added here
# runs on install and on update, and is classified, without anyone
# remembering a second copy. One name per line and nothing else inside the
# parentheses — `ccrc-install.test.ts`'s order pin, the graphify step census
# and `runbook-holds.test.ts` read it line by line.
CCRC_INST_SPINE=(
  _inst_banner
  _inst_roster
  _inst_accounts_sh
  _inst_env
  _inst_agent_env
  _inst_rc
  _inst_node_id
  _inst_tree
  _inst_bins
  _inst_files
  _inst_stamp
  _inst_caps
  _inst_units
  _inst_enable
  _inst_linger
  _inst_dirs
  _inst_graphify_engine
  _inst_hooks
  _inst_skills
  _inst_graphify_skill
  _inst_graph_always_on_off
  _inst_graph_noise
  _inst_graph_excludes
  _inst_ws_build_excludes
  _inst_graph_hooks_off
  _inst_wrappers
  _inst_installed
)

# `_inst_step <fn>` — record the step, then run it. The marker is placed
# BEFORE the step, so a spine that dies leaves the name of the step it died
# IN; a marker that cannot be written dies here, before `<fn>` does anything,
# which classifies right as well — the surviving marker names the step
# before, and that is before-the-tree exactly when `_inst_tree` had not run.
# `_plat_mv_notdir`, not `mv -f`: a bare `mv -f` onto a directory standing at
# the path moves the temp INSIDE it and answers 0.
_inst_step() {   # <fn>
  local fn="$1" tmp="$BOX_INSTALL_STEP_FILE.tmp.$$"
  if ! { mkdir -p "$HOME/.ccrc" && printf '%s\n' "$fn" > "$tmp" && chmod 644 "$tmp" \
         && _plat_mv_notdir "$tmp" "$BOX_INSTALL_STEP_FILE"; }; then
    rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    _ccrc_die "could not record the install step marker ~/.ccrc/install-step before $fn — nothing of $fn ran"
  fi
  "$fn"
}
```

Immediately after `_upd_converged`'s closing `}` (`grep -n '^_upd_converged() {' ccd/ccrc`), add:

```bash
# ── _upd_write_previous <old_version> <old_sha> — the baseline (design §10) ─
# A `--from restore|rollback|watchdog` run is a RETURN to a known tag, not a
# new baseline: were it to write, arm 2's child would record the FAILED tag
# as `previous`, and the next bare `ccrc rollback` would roll the box forward
# onto the release that just reverted. A write that fails REMOVES the old
# file rather than leave it naming a baseline that is no longer the truth;
# only when even that fails does the update stop — before anything is
# installed. `_plat_mv_notdir` for `_inst_step`'s reason.
#
# D-3254: two more keeps, on any other
# `--from`, where the RUNNING stamp is not a completed baseline. A spine that
# dies after `_inst_stamp` leaves the stamp on the new tag and no record, and
# the rerun its own sentence prescribes (`ccrc update --to <v> --force`)
# would then record `previous: <v>` — the release that just failed — and
# lose the tag that last completed. (a) the stamp already reads the tag this
# run installs: a reinstall is not a new baseline. (b) the record is ABSENT
# (read here, before `cmd_update` removes it for this run): an earlier
# update's spine never finished. Absent only, not a record that disagrees —
# a `deploy.sh` push leaves the old record beside its own stamp, and that
# tree IS what ran. Both keep only a WELL-FORMED `previous` (rc 0 or 2);
# with none, the stamp is written as before — a keep never invents an
# absence.
_upd_write_previous() {
  local line1="untagged" line2="unstamped" tmp="$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE.tmp.$$" kept="none" why="" prc=0
  [[ "${1:-}" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] && line1="$1"
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] && line2="$2"
  case "$UPD_FROM" in
    restore|rollback|watchdog)
      why="a --from $UPD_FROM run returns to a known tag; it is not a new baseline" ;;
    *)
      if [ "$line1" != untagged ] && [ "$line1" = "$UPD_VERSION" ]; then
        why="this box's stamp already reads $UPD_VERSION, the tag this run installs; a reinstall is not a new baseline"
      elif [ ! -e "$BOX_INSTALLED_FILE" ]; then
        why="this box's stamp has no completed-install record, so an earlier update's spine never finished and the stamp is not a new baseline"
      fi
      # Either keep needs a baseline TO keep: with no well-formed `previous`
      # the stamp is still the best record of what ran, and is written.
      if [ -n "$why" ]; then
        _upd_read_previous || prc=$?
        case "$prc" in 0|2) ;; *) why="" ;; esac
      fi ;;
  esac
  if [ -n "$why" ]; then
    if [ -e "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" ]; then
      kept="unreadable"
      if [ -f "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" ] && [ -r "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" ]; then
        kept=""
        IFS= read -r kept < "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" || :
        [ -n "$kept" ] || kept="empty"
      fi
    fi
    echo "update: previous: kept ($kept) — $why"
    return 0
  fi
  if { mkdir -p "$HOME/.ccrc" && printf '%s\n%s\n' "$line1" "$line2" > "$tmp" && chmod 644 "$tmp" \
         && _plat_mv_notdir "$tmp" "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE"; }; then
    if [ "$line1" = untagged ]; then
      echo "update: previous: untagged ($line2) — this build carries no release tag, so an automatic restore of it is arm 3 and a bare 'ccrc rollback' refuses (name one with --to)"
    else
      echo "update: previous: $line1 ($line2) — the tag a restore or a bare 'ccrc rollback' returns to"
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  rm -f -- "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" \
    || _ccrc_die "could not write ~/.ccrc/previous, and could not remove the stale one either — a restore could target the wrong tag, so this update stops here, before anything is installed. Remove ~/.ccrc/previous by hand and re-run"
  echo "update: WARN: could not write ~/.ccrc/previous — removed the stale one so no restore can target the wrong tag; this update proceeds without an automatic arm-2 restore"
}

# ── _upd_read_previous — the ONE reader of ~/.ccrc/previous ────────────────
# rc 0 a tag (UPD_PREV_TAG/UPD_PREV_SHA set), 1 absent, 2 `untagged` (the sha
# still set), 3 not a regular readable file or not the two-line grammar.
# Never dies: each caller (arm 2, `rollback`, the watchdog) has its own
# answer to each word, and absent is not malformed.
_upd_read_previous() {
  UPD_PREV_TAG=""; UPD_PREV_SHA=""
  [ -e "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" ] || return 1
  { [ -f "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" ] && [ -r "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" ]; } || return 3
  local -a pl=()
  { mapfile -t pl < "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE"; } 2>/dev/null || return 3
  [ "${#pl[@]}" -eq 2 ] || return 3
  [[ "${pl[1]}" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+$ ]] || return 3
  if [[ "${pl[0]}" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    UPD_PREV_TAG="${pl[0]}"; UPD_PREV_SHA="${pl[1]}"; return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pl[0]}" = untagged ]; then
    UPD_PREV_TAG=untagged; UPD_PREV_SHA="${pl[1]}"; return 2
  fi
  return 3
}

# ── the spine-death classifier (design §11, W4 Task 4) ─────────────────────
# `_upd_spine_step` prints the step the staged spine was in: `none` (no
# marker — a spine older than W4, or a death before `_inst_step` ran),
# the step's name, or `unreadable` for anything that is not an `_inst_*`
# name, so no byte the spine wrote reaches a sentence or update.json
# unvalidated.
_upd_spine_step() {
  local s=""
  if [ ! -e "$BOX_INSTALL_STEP_FILE" ]; then echo none; return 0; fi
  { IFS= read -r s < "$BOX_INSTALL_STEP_FILE"; } 2>/dev/null || :
  [[ "$s" =~ ^_inst_[a-z_]+$ ]] || s=unreadable
  echo "$s"
}

# `_upd_step_moved <step>` — rc 0 when the tree was (or may have been)
# replaced, rc 1 when the spine died before `_inst_tree`. Read against THIS
# tree's `CCRC_INST_SPINE` (the running ccrc; the step came from the staged
# one): a name it does not list — a newer spine's step, or `unreadable` —
# is at-or-after, the direction that runs the gate rather than skip it.
_upd_step_moved() {   # <step>
  local want="$1" s
  [ "$want" = none ] && return 1
  for s in "${CCRC_INST_SPINE[@]}"; do
    [ "$s" = _inst_tree ] && return 0
    [ "$s" = "$want" ] && return 1
  done
  return 0
}

# `_upd_stamp_moved <old_sha>` — rc 0 iff the box's own stamp now parses to
# a sha other than <old_sha>, the one `cmd_update` read before the staged
# install (D-3252). `_inst_stamp` runs after
# `_inst_tree`, so rc 0 PROVES the tree was placed. rc 1 is not the converse:
# a death in `_inst_tree`/`_inst_bins`/`_inst_files`, a stamp step that
# skipped, or a reinstall of the running build all leave the stamp where it
# was. (Not `~/ccrc/build.json`: `_inst_tree`'s rsync copies `server agent
# shared deploy ccd` and never the release root's stamp.) `BOX_BUILD` is
# saved and restored around the parse, as `_upd_converged` does.
_upd_stamp_moved() {   # <old_sha>
  local old="${1:-}" now=""
  local -a box=(${BOX_BUILD[@]+"${BOX_BUILD[@]}"})
  _box_build_fields && now="${BOX_BUILD[0]}"
  BOX_BUILD=(${box[@]+"${box[@]}"})
  [ -n "$now" ] && [ "$now" != "$old" ]
}
```

  rm -f -- "$BOX_PREVIOUS_FILE" "$BOX_INSTALL_STEP_FILE" "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" "$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK" \
    || _ccrc_die "removing the node's update state files failed"
```

That rc is `_box_server_addr`'s SKIP for the doctor's `build` check (a box with no address "runs no server of its own"), but the gate only probes on a `server`/`both` box, which DOES run one — and a server whose env file names neither key binds exactly `config.ts:305-318`'s defaults, the pair `cmd_install`'s landing block already falls back to (`ccd/ccrc:9247-9248`). - **D-3256** (found planning Task 5) — spec §11 says the gate waits for the role's signal "Then `cmd_doctor` runs as today". Today (and here) the doctor is the staged spine's LAST act (`cmd_install` ends with `cmd_doctor`, `ccd/ccrc:9239`; `cmd_update`'s header, step 3: "The staged verb ends with `cmd_doctor` from the NEW tree, which is this verb's doctor too"), so it has run before `cmd_update` regains control and the gate runs after it. Running a second doctor after the gate would print every verdict twice with the same table. The exit codes are the spec's either way: doctor FAIL + gate pass → 3; gate fail → 4 whatever the doctor said. Cost if wrong: the doctor's `services`/`build` lines may read a unit mid-restart that the gate, seconds later, measures up — the gate's line is the later measurement and decides the exit code.

  const gateBox = (prefix: string, role?: 'server' | 'fleet' | 'both', installExit = 0): string => {

    if (role !== undefined) {
      mkdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc'), { recursive: true });
      // What `_inst_env` seeds (a fleet box's env file names no server).
      writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'ccrc.env'), role === 'fleet'
        ? 'CCRC_ROLE=fleet\n'

  // THE ARMS, SOURCED. `ccrc` recomputes CCD_OS from $OSTYPE at source time
  // (ccd/ccrc:109-114), so the Darwin arms of a whole `ccrc update` run only

  // Sourced (the `_check_routing` idiom in ccrc-doctor.test.ts), CCD_OS is
  // set AFTER the file computed it, and `_ccrc_job_stayed_up` is shadowed to
  // record its argument, so every leg measures which arm ran: the arm's
  // CHOICE is the subject here, the two-sample check is the itDarwin case's.
  const probe = (home: string, os: 'linux' | 'darwin', role: string): { rc: number; why: string } => {
    replantDoctorStubs(home);
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-health-pin'), 'v2.0.0\n');
    const script = [
      'set -uo pipefail',
      '. "$1"',
      'CCD_OS="$2"',
      '_ccrc_job_stayed_up() { printf \'%s\\n\' "$1" >> "$HOME/stayed-up-calls"; CCRC_STAYED_DETAIL="pid 4242 -> 4242 across 0s+0s"; [ ! -f "$HOME/fixture-shadow-churn" ]; }',
      'rc=0; _upd_gate_probe "$3" v2.0.0 || rc=$?',
      'printf \'rc=%s\\nwhy=%s\\n\' "$rc" "$UPD_GATE_WHY"',

**4e — the three functions.** Immediately above the line `# ── _upd_floor_check` (`grep -n '^# ── _upd_floor_check' ccd/ccrc`; `_upd_converged` ends just above it) insert:

```bash
# ── _upd_health_version — what the server on THIS box says it runs ───────
# `GET /health` is auth-EXEMPT (server/src/auth/gate.ts:195-198) and carries
# `version` for a versioned build only (server/src/server.ts:1073-1078). The
# address is `_box_server_addr`'s — CCRC_ADDR, then ccrc.env's
# CCRC_HOST/CCRC_PORT — and NOTHING CONFIGURED is the server's own default
# bind, 127.0.0.1:7788 (server/src/config.ts:305-318; the pair
# `cmd_install`'s landing block falls back to), not a failure: the gate only
# asks on a server/both box, which runs a server whether or not its seed-once
# env file names the two keys (D-3255). An address
# that is configured and unusable fails, in the resolver's own sentence. The
# answered value is never echoed — it came off the network.
# Called DIRECTLY, never in `$(…)`: its out-parameters are the answer.
#   0 -> UPD_HEALTH_VERSION = a vX.Y.Z the server answered
#   1 -> the address is unusable            (UPD_GATE_WHY says why)
#   2 -> no answer (curl's exit is named)   (UPD_GATE_WHY)
#   3 -> answered, without a release version (UPD_GATE_WHY)
_upd_health_version() {
  local out rc=0 v=""
  UPD_HEALTH_VERSION=""; UPD_HEALTH_ADDR=""
  out="$(_box_server_addr)" || rc=$?
  case "$rc" in
    0) UPD_HEALTH_ADDR="${out%%$'\n'*}" ;;
    1) UPD_HEALTH_ADDR="127.0.0.1:7788" ;;
    *) UPD_GATE_WHY="${out%%$'\n'*}"; return 1 ;;
  esac
  rc=0
  out="$(curl -fsS --max-time "$CCRC_HEALTH_TIMEOUT" "http://$UPD_HEALTH_ADDR/health" 2>/dev/null)" || rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    UPD_GATE_WHY="GET http://$UPD_HEALTH_ADDR/health got no answer (curl exited $rc)"
    return 2
  fi
  v="$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.version // empty' 2>/dev/null)" || v=""
  if [[ ! "$v" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    UPD_GATE_WHY="GET http://$UPD_HEALTH_ADDR/health answered without a release version"
    return 3
  fi
  UPD_HEALTH_VERSION="$v"
  return 0
}

# ── _upd_gate_probe <role> <version> — ONE measurement of the role's signal ─
# Design §11, per OS. The UNIT first (a dead unit never costs a request),
# then — for a role that runs the server — `/health` on the STAGED version.
#   server/both, Linux:  is-active ccrc.service, and /health
#   server/both, Darwin: _ccrc_job_stayed_up ccrc.service, and /health
#   fleet, Linux:        is-active ccrc-agent.service, and deploy/verify-service.sh
#                        — the Linux twin of `_ccrc_job_stayed_up`, which reads
#                        launchctl and is Darwin-only by call site (its own
#                        header); `_inst_enable` guards it with the same `[ -f ]`
#                        (D-3242). The
#                        agent's `ready` is the server's to measure, not ours.
#   fleet, Darwin:       _ccrc_job_stayed_up ccrc-agent.service
# No Darwin arm reaches systemctl. rc 0 pass, 1 fail; UPD_GATE_WHY says what
# was measured either way. An empty role is `both`, the staged spine's own
# default for a box that recorded none. Task 9's watchdog runs this same
# function — one gate, two callers.
_upd_gate_probe() {   # <role> <version> -> 0 pass, 1 fail; UPD_GATE_WHY
  local role="${1:-both}" want="$2" unit st vrc=0 hrc=0
  UPD_GATE_WHY=""
  case "$role" in
    server|both) unit=ccrc.service ;;
    fleet)       unit=ccrc-agent.service ;;
    *) UPD_GATE_WHY="no health gate is defined for role '$role'"; return 1 ;;
  esac
  if [ "$CCD_OS" = darwin ]; then   # the launchd arm: two pid samples, never systemctl
    if ! _ccrc_job_stayed_up "$unit"; then
      UPD_GATE_WHY="$unit did not stay up ($CCRC_STAYED_DETAIL)"
      return 1
    fi
  else
    st="$(_svc_is_active "$unit")"
    if [ "$st" != active ]; then
      UPD_GATE_WHY="$unit is ${st:-unanswered} (systemctl --user is-active), not active"
      return 1
    fi
    if [ "$role" = fleet ] && [ -f "$CCRC_HERE/../deploy/verify-service.sh" ]; then
      bash "$CCRC_HERE/../deploy/verify-service.sh" "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1 || vrc=$?
      if [ "$vrc" -ne 0 ]; then
        UPD_GATE_WHY="$unit did not stay up (deploy/verify-service.sh exited $vrc; systemctl --user status $unit says why)"
        return 1
      fi
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$role" = fleet ]; then
    UPD_GATE_WHY="$unit up and staying up"
    return 0
  fi
  _upd_health_version || hrc=$?
  [ "$hrc" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  if [ "$UPD_HEALTH_VERSION" != "$want" ]; then
    UPD_GATE_WHY="/health at $UPD_HEALTH_ADDR answers $UPD_HEALTH_VERSION, not $want"
    return 1
  fi
  UPD_GATE_WHY="$unit up, /health at $UPD_HEALTH_ADDR answers $want"
  return 0
}

# ── _upd_gate <role> <version> — the probe, until it passes or time is up ─
# Probes at once, then every 2 s, for CCRC_UPDATE_HEALTH_S (default 90): a
# restarted server takes seconds to bind, and the first `/health` after a
# restart answering nothing is the ordinary case, not a verdict. The ONLY
# writer of the `checking` phase.
_upd_gate() {   # <role> <version> -> 0 at the first pass, 1 when the window ends first
  local role="${1:-both}" want="$2" limit="${CCRC_UPDATE_HEALTH_S:-90}" start
  case "$limit" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*)
      echo "update: WARN: CCRC_UPDATE_HEALTH_S='${limit//[![:print:]]/?}' is not a number of seconds — using 90"
      limit=90 ;;
  esac
  _upd_phase checking
  start=$SECONDS
  while :; do
    if _upd_gate_probe "$role" "$want"; then
      echo "update: gate: $role answers on $want ($UPD_GATE_WHY)"
      return 0
    fi
    [ "$((SECONDS - start))" -lt "$limit" ] || break
    sleep 2
  done
  echo "update: gate FAILED after $((SECONDS - start))s — $UPD_GATE_WHY"
  return 1
}
```

Deleting only the moved `_ccrc_die` would NOT reach the gate: control would leave the inner `if` and fall straight into the before-the-tree `UPD_REPORTING=0` / `_ccrc_die` below it — every moved death would print "nothing was replaced" and exit 1. Replace those seven lines with:

        # gone, and a later die on this path is a `failed` report like any other.
        UPD_SPINE_DIED="$step_desc"
      else
        UPD_REPORTING=0

(the not-moved die's text byte-identical to Task 4's, its `$place` clause included, so Task 4's `dies BEFORE _inst_tree` and `unmoved stamp` cases and its mutation rows 5 and 11 still read it). Keep every other line Tasks 1, 2 and 4 wrote in the branch exactly as committed. Then, between the `fi` that closes the `if [ "$inst_rc" -ne 0 ]` branch and the `_upd_phase restarting` line (Task 1) that precedes `_upd_unlock` (Task 2) and `_upd_sweep`, insert:

```bash
  # ── THE HEALTH GATE (design §11) ─────────────────────────────────────────
  # The staged spine restarted the role's unit onto the new tree (and ran its
  # doctor — D-3256); this measures whether the box
  # CAME BACK on it, before the sweep moves a single supervisor. Two failures,
  # two exit codes, because they have two remedies: a doctor FAIL with the
  # unit up is D-3114's 3 (the box's health, no revert); a dead unit or a
  # `/health` on the wrong version is 4. A spine that died AFTER the tree
  # moved (Task 4) is gated too: the unit may well answer on the new version.
  if [ "$no_gate" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "update: gate: skipped (--no-gate) — nothing measured whether $UPD_VERSION came back up on this box"
  elif ! _upd_gate "$role" "$UPD_VERSION"; then
    # ONE failed-report line for both shapes (a completed spine, or one that
    # died after the tree): Task 6 replaces exactly this line with its restore.
    local gate_fail="gate: $UPD_GATE_WHY"
    [ -n "$UPD_SPINE_DIED" ] && gate_fail="spine died at $UPD_SPINE_DIED; $gate_fail"
    _upd_phase failed "$gate_fail"
    _upd_unlock
    echo "$PROG: update: $UPD_VERSION was installed, but the box did not come back healthy on it ($UPD_GATE_WHY) — exit 4. The backup taken BEFORE the install is complete at $UPD_BACKUP_DIR" >&2
    exit 4
  fi
  # D-3240: the box moved and answers, but its spine did
  # not finish — no sweep (the supervisors are not moved onto a half-placed
  # install) and no restore (the box is healthy). The report is re-asserted:
  # the gate's own `checking` overwrote Task 4's `failed`.
  if [ -n "$UPD_SPINE_DIED" ]; then
    _upd_phase failed "spine died at $UPD_SPINE_DIED"
    _upd_unlock
    local measured="answers on $UPD_VERSION"
    [ "$no_gate" -eq 1 ] && measured="was not measured (--no-gate)"
    echo "$PROG: update: the box moved and $measured, but its install never completed (spine died at $UPD_SPINE_DIED) — rerun: ccrc update --to $UPD_VERSION --force" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
```

Neither exit goes through `_ccrc_die`, deliberately: its report hook (Task 1) would overwrite the precise `failed` detail just written with the die's sentence. `_upd_report` is not run on a failed gate — the box's state is what the gate line says, not a from→to.

- [ ] **Step 6: Mutation check (spec §18 rows "the gate has per-OS arms", "the gate restores", "doctor FAIL does not restore"; plan rows)**

From the repository root. `mut` replaces EXACTLY one occurrence or refuses, so a mis-typed anchor cannot measure green:

```bash
KEEP="$(mktemp -d)"; cp ccd/ccrc "$KEEP/ccrc"
mut() { python3 -c 'import sys; p="ccd/ccrc"; s=open(p).read(); a,b=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]; n=s.count(a); assert n==1, f"{n} matches for {a!r}"; open(p,"w").write(s.replace(a,b))' "$1" "$2"; }
restore() { cp "$KEEP/ccrc" ccd/ccrc && cmp ccd/ccrc "$KEEP/ccrc" && echo restored; }

const OLD_SHA = 'oldsha0000000000000000000000000000000000';
/** Records its argv, the lock marker it was handed, its own $PPID and
 *  whether ~/.ccrc/update.lock was HELD while it ran — a fresh `flock -n`
 *  that FAILS is the measurement (spec §10's own), and it can only fail
 *  because the parent holds its descriptor. Exits `fixture-restore-exit`. */
const RESTORE_RECORDER = [
  '#!/bin/sh',
  'printf \'%s\\n\' "$0" "$@" > "$HOME/restore-child-argv"',
  'locked=no',
  'if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! flock -n "$HOME/.ccrc/update.lock" true; then locked=yes; fi',
  'printf \'held=%s ppid=%s locked=%s\\n\' "${CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD:-unset}" "$PPID" "$locked" > "$HOME/restore-child-env"',
  'code=0; [ -f "$HOME/fixture-restore-exit" ] && IFS= read -r code < "$HOME/fixture-restore-exit"',
  'exit "$code"',
].join('\n') + '\n';
/** The hazard spec §11's arm 2 carries: a new tree whose own ccrc is broken. */
const RESTORE_BROKEN = '#!/bin/sh\necho "fixture: the new tree\'s ccd/ccrc is broken" >&2\nexit 1\n';

interface RestoreBoxOpts {
  /** The running stamp's version; `null` = an unversioned box. Default `v1.0.0`. */
  oldVersion?: string | null;
  /** `~/.ccrc/installed` BEFORE the update; `null` = absent. Default the verified one-line marker. */
  marker?: string | null;
  /** The previous release ships a provenance bundle. Default true. */
  prevBundle?: boolean;
  /** What the new tree places at `~/ccrc/ccd/ccrc`. Default `recorder`. */
  child?: 'recorder' | 'broken' | 'none';
  /** More sh lines the new tree's `install` runs, before it places the child. */
  onInstall?: string[];
  /** The new tree's staged install exit code. Default 0. */
  installExit?: number;
}

/** A box whose update to the STUB release v2.0.0 FAILS its health gate:
 *  `/health` answers the OLD build (Task 5's `fixture-health-pin`), which is
 *  spec §11's "wrong `/health` version" — exit 4, and `_upd_restore` runs.
 *  The previous release is published under `download/<old>/` so arm 2 has
 *  something to ask about. */
function plantRestoreBox(home: string, opts: RestoreBoxOpts = {}): void {
  const oldVersion = opts.oldVersion === undefined ? 'v1.0.0' : opts.oldVersion;
  if (oldVersion === null) plantOldBox(home); else plantOldBox(home, { version: oldVersion });
  mkdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc'), { recursive: true });
  const marker = opts.marker === undefined ? `${OLD_SHA}\n` : opts.marker;
  if (marker !== null) writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'installed'), marker);
  if (oldVersion !== null) {
    packRelease(home, stubTree(home, { version: oldVersion }),
      { tag: oldVersion, latest: false, bundle: opts.prevBundle !== false });
  }
  packRelease(home, stubTree(home, { version: 'v2.0.0', installExit: opts.installExit }), { tag: 'v2.0.0' });
  const lines = [...(opts.onInstall ?? [])];
  const child = opts.child ?? 'recorder';
  if (child !== 'none') {
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-restore-child'), child === 'recorder' ? RESTORE_RECORDER : RESTORE_BROKEN);
    lines.push('mkdir -p "$HOME/ccrc/ccd" && cp "$HOME/fixture-restore-child" "$HOME/ccrc/ccd/ccrc"');
  }
  writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-on-install'), `${lines.join('\n')}\n`);
  writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-health-pin'), `${oldVersion ?? 'v0.0.1'}\n`);
}

// The reports this run placed are read through Task 1's file-scope
// `reportWrites` (every `update.json` the `mv` recorder saw, in order) and
// `lastReport` (the file on disk) — never a second copy of either.
const restoreChildArgv = (home: string): string[] | null => (existsSync(join(home, 'restore-child-argv'))
  ? readFileSync(join(home, 'restore-child-argv'), 'utf8').split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '') : null);
```

    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^update: REVERTED \(arm 3\): /m);
    if (process.platform === 'darwin') {
      const calls = readFileSync(join(home, 'launchctl-calls'), 'utf8');
      expect(calls).toMatch(/^bootout \S+\/app\.ccrc\.ccrc-agent$/m);
      expect(calls).toMatch(/^bootstrap \S+ \S+\/app\.ccrc\.ccrc-agent\.plist$/m);
      expect(calls).not.toMatch(/^bootout \S+\/app\.ccrc\.ccrc$/m);
      expect(calls).not.toMatch(/^bootstrap \S+ \S+\/app\.ccrc\.ccrc\.plist$/m);
    } else {
      const calls = readFileSync(join(home, 'systemctl-calls'), 'utf8');
      expect(calls).toMatch(/^--user restart ccrc-agent\.service$/m);
      expect(calls).not.toMatch(/^--user restart ccrc\.service$/m);
    }
  });

  it('a release host that answers 503 to the bundle question is not "ships no bundle": arm 2 runs the child without --allow-unsigned and lets its own fetch decide', () => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-restore-host-5xx-');
    // Planted by the new tree's install, i.e. AFTER the parent fetched its own
    // release: only arm 2's question meets the 503.
    plantRestoreBox(home, { onInstall: ['printf \'503\\n\' > "$HOME/fixture-release-http"'] });
    const r = runUpdate(home);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(4);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^update: arm 2: could not ask the release host whether v1\.0\.0 ships a bundle \(curl failed, or the host answered neither 200 nor 404\) — the restore child's own fetch decides$/m);
    expect(r.stdout).not.toMatch(/arm2-refused/);
    expect(restoreChildArgv(home)).toEqual([
      join(home, 'ccrc', 'ccd', 'ccrc'), 'update', '--to', 'v1.0.0', '--no-gate', '--from', 'restore',
    ]);
    expect(String(lastReport(home)['detail'])).toMatch(/^arm2: restored v1\.0\.0; gate: /);
  });

  it('a spine that COMPLETED and then failed its gate, restored by arm 3: the completed-install record goes, so the box reads incomplete — never converged on the release it backed out of', () => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-restore-unrecord-');
    // What a completed v2.0.0 spine leaves before the gate runs: its stamp and
    // its completed-install record, agreeing. That pair is what
    // `_upd_converged` and `update --check` read as "current at v2.0.0".
    const newSha = 'newsha0000000000000000000000000000000000';
    plantRestoreBox(home, {
      child: 'broken',
      onInstall: [
        `printf '%s\\n' '${shippedStamp('v2.0.0', newSha).trim()}' > "$HOME/.ccrc/build.json"`,
        `printf '%s\\n' '${newSha}' > "$HOME/.ccrc/installed"`,
      ],
    });
    const r = runUpdate(home);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(4);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^update: REVERTED \(arm 3\): /m);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^update: arm 3: the completed-install record is gone — this box reads install: incomplete until deploy\.sh or a completed update records it again$/m);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'installed')), 'arm 3 left the reverted build\'s record').toBe(false);
    // The stamp still names v2.0.0 (arm 3 copies no stamp back; the tree is
    // MIXED), so the honest word is `incomplete` — never `current`.
    const c = runUpdate(home, ['--check']);
    expect(c.code, `stderr: ${c.stderr}\nstdout: ${c.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    expect(c.stdout).toMatch(new RegExp(`^check: box=v2\\.0\\.0 sha=${newSha} target=v2\\.0\\.0 (.* )?state=incomplete$`, 'm'));   // Task 12 adds fields before `state=`
  });

  it('--from restore is refused unless this run is the child of an update holding the lock — it is not a typed way past the floor or the sweep', () => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-from-restore-bare-');
    plantOldBox(home, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    packRelease(home, stubTree(home, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0', latest: false });
    // No marker at all, and a marker naming a pid that is not this run's parent.
    for (const extra of [{}, { CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD: '1' }]) {
      const r = runUpdate(home, ['--to', 'v2.0.0', '--from', 'restore'], extra);
      expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(2);
      expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/^ccrc: update: --from restore is the automatic restore's own word — it runs only as the child of an update holding ~\/\.ccrc\/update\.lock \(it skips the floor, previous and the sweep\); to move this box to a tag by hand: ccrc update --to <tag> --downgrade$/m);
      expect(existsSync(join(home, 'staged-ccrc-argv'))).toBe(false);
      expect(existsSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.json'))).toBe(false);
      expect(localUrls(home)).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  it('FULL flavour: the arm-2 child is a REAL `ccrc update` that completes under the parent\'s lock — no lock sentence, no sweep, the previous tag re-installed (§18 "arm 2 runs under the parent\'s lock"; Review Focus 4)', () => {
    // The parent installs the FULL v2.0.0 tree (the real spine places the
    // real `ccd/ccrc` at ~/ccrc/ccd/ccrc), fails its gate, and arm 2 runs that
    // placed ccrc as a child against the STUB v1.0.0 release. The child's own
    // lock (Task 2) must INHERIT — marker = its $PPID, and a fresh flock -n
    // fails because the parent holds the lock — or it refuses with "another
    // update holds …" and every restore silently becomes arm 3.
    const home = freshUpdateBox('ccrc-update-restore-full-');
    plantOldBox(home, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'installed'), `${OLD_SHA}\n`);
    packRelease(home, stubTree(home, { version: 'v1.0.0' }), { tag: 'v1.0.0', latest: false });
    packRelease(home, fullTree(home, { version: 'v2.0.0', sha: 'newsha0000000000000000000000000000000000' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0' });
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-health-pin'), 'v1.0.0\n');
    const r = runUpdate(home);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(4);
    expect(`${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`).not.toMatch(/another update holds/);
    expect(`${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`).not.toMatch(/ambiguous redirect/);
    expect(r.stderr).not.toMatch(/--from restore is the automatic restore's own word/);
    // The child's own transcript: it kept `previous`, skipped the sweep, and
    // its staged install (the STUB v1.0.0 shim) actually ran.
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^update: previous: kept \(v1\.0\.0\)/m);
    // The two exemptions a bare --from restore can no longer be typed to
    // reach (Step 1 (c)), measured here on the real child: the parent's
    // completed spine raised the floor to v2.0.0, and the restore goes below
    // it saying so, without lowering it (spec §9, Task 1's `--from` arm).
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^update: WARN: v1\.0\.0 is below this box's floor v2\.0\.0 \(resolved by --to v1\.0\.0\) — proceeding because this run is --from restore; the floor stays v2\.0\.0$/m);
    expect(readFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'floor'), 'utf8')).toBe('v2.0.0\n');
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^update: sweep: skipped — a --from restore run returns the supervisors' own build; they never moved$/m);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'staged-ccrc-argv')), 'the restore child\'s staged install never ran').toBe(true);
    expect(localUrls(home)).toContain(`local://${home}/releases/download/v1.0.0/ccrc-v1.0.0.tar.gz`);
    const writes = reportWrites(home);
    expect(writes.some((w) => w['from'] === 'restore' && w['phase'] === 'installing'),
      'the child reported no install of its own').toBe(true);
    const last = lastReport(home);
    expect(last['phase']).toBe('reverted');
    expect(last['from']).toBe('cli');
    expect(String(last['detail'])).toMatch(/^arm2: restored v1\.0\.0; gate: /);
    expect(r.stdout).not.toMatch(/REVERTED \(arm 3\)/);
    expect(readFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'previous'), 'utf8').split('\n')[0]).toBe('v1.0.0');
  });
});
```

and define the helper that capture calls, immediately above `_upd_resolve() {` (`:11519`; Step 6 later adds `_upd_release_base` directly above `_upd_resolve() {`, which puts it between this helper and `_upd_resolve`):

```bash
# `_upd_marker_unsigned` — rc 0 iff the completed-install record's line 2 reads
# `unsigned`. It is the one read of that line for an update: `cmd_update`'s
# arm-2 precondition capture and `cmd_rollback`'s --allow-unsigned both ask
# it, and neither names the record. An absent, unreadable or one-line record
# answers 1 (verified). That is the safe direction, because it refuses a
# bundle-less target instead of admitting it.
_upd_marker_unsigned() {
  local m1="" m2=""
  [ -f "$BOX_INSTALLED_FILE" ] && [ -r "$BOX_INSTALLED_FILE" ] || return 1
  { IFS= read -r m1; IFS= read -r m2; } < "$BOX_INSTALLED_FILE" || :
  [ "$m2" = unsigned ]
}
```
