Locate each spot by the grep given, never by the line number alone.

(a) The constant — immediately ABOVE the line `# ── THE EXPOSURE FILE, WHICH \`expose\` WRITES AND THE SERVER UNIT READS ────` (`grep -n '^# ── THE EXPOSURE FILE, WHICH' ccd/ccrc`, `:1146`):

```bash
# ── THE CONTROL PLANE'S PROJECTION (design 2026-09-20 §9; W4 Task 8) ─────
# `~/.ccrc/update-intent` — nine lines, `epoch`/`issued`/`lease` in unix
# SECONDS, ending `end`: the server's resolution for THIS node. A fleet
# node's `ccd-update-sync` pulls it every minute; on a server or `both` node
# the server process writes it at every resolution and inventory sweep.
# `ccrc update` with no --to follows it and `ccrc channel` prints it — both
# through `_upd_intent_state` and nothing else. ccrc itself never writes it;
# `_uninst_tree_bins` removes it.
BOX_INTENT_FILE="$HOME/.ccrc/update-intent"

```

(b) The globals — immediately ABOVE the comment line ``# `cmd_rollout`'s out-parameters (release/rollout design §4), declared at file`` (`grep -n "^# \`cmd_rollout\`'s out-parameters" ccd/ccrc`, `:1408`):

```bash
# The projection reader's answer and the target chosen from it (design
# 2026-09-20 §9; W4 Task 8), at file scope for the same `set -u` reason:
# `_upd_intent_state` fills UPD_INTENT_*, `_upd_target` reads them and fills
# UPD_TARGET*, and `--check`, the floor and `ccrc channel` read those.
UPD_INTENT_STATE=""           # ok|none|not-configured|unreadable|stale|malformed
UPD_INTENT_ROLE=""            # the recorded CCRC_ROLE (fleet|server|both), or "" — absent or unrecognised
UPD_INTENT_WHY=""             # the state's reason; spliced into its sentence, never a byte of the file
UPD_INTENT_EPOCH=""           # the eight document fields — set on ok|none ONLY
UPD_INTENT_ISSUED=""
UPD_INTENT_LEASE=""
UPD_INTENT_CHANNEL=""
UPD_INTENT_DESIRED=""
UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_STABLE=""
UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_DEV=""
UPD_INTENT_AUTO=""
UPD_TARGET=""                 # the tag _upd_resolve is handed; "" = latest/download
UPD_TARGET_VIA=""             # how it was chosen, in the floor's words: --to <t> | the control plane (channel <c>) | latest/download
UPD_TARGET_CHANNEL=""         # the channel whose desired line was taken (projection only)
UPD_TARGET_LINE=""            # the one stdout sentence naming that choice, or "" for --to
UPD_TARGET_NONE=""            # --check only: the desired key whose line read none, else "" (never folded into UPD_TARGET="")

```

(c) The reader, its sentence, the target decision and the verb — immediately ABOVE the line `# ── _upd_resolve / _upd_fetch — SHA256SUMS first, then the tarball ────────` (`grep -n '^# ── _upd_resolve / _upd_fetch' ccd/ccrc`, `:11508`):

```bash
# ── _upd_intent_state — the projection, measured (design 2026-09-20 §9) ──
# `_acct_pool_state`'s vocabulary (`ccd/ccd:2162`) re-derived for this file,
# plus `none` — `ok`'s twin for a document that resolves no target — and made
# ROLE-AWARE, because "is a control plane configured here" is measured
# differently per role (spec §9's table), and the timer-unit test alone is
# false on exactly the node that is most centrally managed:
#   macOS — never configured (decision 17), decided before anything is read.
#   fleet, or no role recorded — `ccd-update-sync.timer`'s unit FILE is
#       installed (`_pool_sync_installed`'s rule, `ccd/ccd:2116-2122`: the
#       artifact the installer left, NEVER the projection's own absence,
#       which is the thing being told apart). Absent file and no unit file:
#       `not-configured`, the one answer that falls back to stable. Absent
#       file WITH the unit file: `unreadable` (never synced) — never the
#       fallback, or a stopped timer would silently follow stable.
#   server / both — the recorded role IS the configuration: the server
#       process is the writer, so an absent file is `unreadable`, always.
# NAMED HAZARD: `CCRC_ROLE` is seed-once in ccrc.env (`_inst_env`), so a box
# re-installed with another --role keeps its first; this reader trusts the
# recorded role exactly as `cmd_update`'s role passthrough and rollout's
# preflight already do. And the server DERIVES a role when none is recorded
# (W2's D-3174) and writes its own projection, while this reader keys
# "configured" on the RECORDED role, as spec §9's table does: a no-role box
# with no timer unit file reads an ABSENT projection as `not-configured`.
# rollout refuses a no-role box (D-3106), so no release-lane box is one.
# A present file is judged the same way on every role: a bounded, NUL-aware
# read (`_acct_pool_state`'s INVERTED rc, `ccd/ccd:2252-2254` — 0 means the
# read stopped short of EOF, at the 65536-byte cap or a NUL), `end` as the
# last line (the torn-write detector), exactly nine lines in spec order,
# each its own grammar, and `lease` against `date +%s` — SECONDS, spec §9's
# unit (the C1 defect, `server.ts:2679-2688`) — STRICTLY, so a lease equal
# to now is still in force. A number wider than 18 digits is malformed
# (plan D-3265): bash arithmetic wraps past 2^63-1, and a
# 20-digit lease wraps to a POSITIVE value decades out — a garbage document
# read as in force. `UPD_INTENT_WHY` is built from this function's own words,
# never from the file's bytes. Always rc 0; prints nothing.
_upd_intent_state() {
  local LC_ALL=C   # `-n 65536` is a BYTE cap only under C (`_acct_pool_state`'s reason)
  local f="$BOX_INTENT_FILE" role="" body="" tail="" rest="" now="" k v i
  local -a lines=() vals=() keys=(epoch issued lease channel desired desired-stable desired-dev auto)
  UPD_INTENT_STATE="" UPD_INTENT_ROLE="" UPD_INTENT_WHY=""
  UPD_INTENT_EPOCH="" UPD_INTENT_ISSUED="" UPD_INTENT_LEASE="" UPD_INTENT_CHANNEL=""
  UPD_INTENT_DESIRED="" UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_STABLE="" UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_DEV="" UPD_INTENT_AUTO=""
  if [ "$CCD_OS" = darwin ]; then
    UPD_INTENT_STATE=not-configured; UPD_INTENT_WHY=macos
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -f "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ] && [ -r "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ]; then
    role="$(_box_env_value "$BOX_ENV_FILE" CCRC_ROLE)"
  fi
  case "$role" in server|fleet|both) ;; *) role="" ;; esac
  UPD_INTENT_ROLE="$role"
  if [ ! -e "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ]; then
    case "$role" in
      server|both) UPD_INTENT_STATE=unreadable; UPD_INTENT_WHY=absent ;;
      *) if [ -f "$BOX_UNIT_DIR/ccd-update-sync.timer" ]; then
           UPD_INTENT_STATE=unreadable; UPD_INTENT_WHY="never synced"
         else
           UPD_INTENT_STATE=not-configured; UPD_INTENT_WHY="no ccd-update-sync.timer"
         fi ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$f" ] || [ ! -r "$f" ]; then
    UPD_INTENT_STATE=unreadable; UPD_INTENT_WHY="not a readable regular file"
    return 0
  fi
  if { IFS= read -r -d '' -n 65536 body; } 2>/dev/null < "$f"; then
    UPD_INTENT_STATE=malformed; UPD_INTENT_WHY="65536 bytes or more, or a NUL byte"
    return 0
  fi
  tail="$body"
  [[ "$tail" == *$'\n' ]] && tail="${tail%$'\n'}"
  if [[ "${tail##*$'\n'}" != end ]]; then
    UPD_INTENT_STATE=malformed; UPD_INTENT_WHY="its last line is not end"
    return 0
  fi
  # Split with builtins, and stop at ten lines: a document of 60 000
  # newlines is as malformed at line 10 as at line 60 000.
  rest="$tail"
  while [ "${#lines[@]}" -lt 10 ] && [[ "$rest" == *$'\n'* ]]; do
    lines+=("${rest%%$'\n'*}")
    rest="${rest#*$'\n'}"
  done
  lines+=("$rest")
  if [ "${#lines[@]}" -ne 9 ]; then
    UPD_INTENT_STATE=malformed; UPD_INTENT_WHY="not exactly nine lines"
    return 0
  fi
  for i in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do
    k="${keys[$i]}"
    v="${lines[$i]#"$k "}"
    if [[ "${lines[$i]}" != "$k "* ]] || ! case "$k" in
         epoch|issued|lease) [[ "$v" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,17})$ ]] ;;
         channel) [[ "$v" == stable || "$v" == dev ]] ;;
         auto) [[ "$v" == off || "$v" == stable || "$v" == channel ]] ;;
         *) [[ "$v" == none || "$v" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] ;;
       esac; then
      UPD_INTENT_STATE=malformed; UPD_INTENT_WHY="line $((i + 1)) is not a well-formed $k line"
      return 0
    fi
    vals[i]="$v"
  done
  # An unmeasurable clock is not "in force": without this, `(( > ))` on an
  # empty `now` reads 0 and every lease passes.
  now="$(date +%s)"
  if [[ ! "$now" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,17}$ ]]; then
    UPD_INTENT_STATE=unreadable; UPD_INTENT_WHY="the clock did not answer: date +%s"
    return 0
  fi
  if (( now > 10#${vals[2]} )); then
    UPD_INTENT_STATE=stale; UPD_INTENT_WHY="its lease ended $(( now - 10#${vals[2]} ))s ago"
    return 0
  fi
  UPD_INTENT_EPOCH="${vals[0]}" UPD_INTENT_ISSUED="${vals[1]}" UPD_INTENT_LEASE="${vals[2]}"
  UPD_INTENT_CHANNEL="${vals[3]}" UPD_INTENT_DESIRED="${vals[4]}"
  UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_STABLE="${vals[5]}" UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_DEV="${vals[6]}" UPD_INTENT_AUTO="${vals[7]}"
  if [ "$UPD_INTENT_DESIRED" = none ]; then UPD_INTENT_STATE=none; else UPD_INTENT_STATE=ok; fi
  return 0
}

# `_upd_intent_say` — the sentence for a projection nobody may follow
# (unreadable, stale, malformed), ending in the remedy for WHOEVER WRITES
# THIS BOX'S COPY (spec §9's words): the puller's oneshot on a fleet node,
# and a server restart where the server process is the writer. A box that
# records no role is either: the puller when its timer unit file is
# installed, else the server — which DERIVES a role from CCRC_FLEET when
# none is recorded and writes its own projection (W2's D-3174), so there the
# puller's unit does not even exist. `_upd_target` refuses with it (prefixed
# `update: `); `ccrc channel` prints it bare. One line, stdout.
_upd_intent_say() {
  local puller="systemctl --user start ccd-update-sync.service"
  local server="restart ccrc.service (it writes ~/.ccrc/update-intent on every sweep)"
  local remedy="$puller"
  case "$UPD_INTENT_ROLE" in
    server|both) remedy="$server" ;;
    "") [ -f "$BOX_UNIT_DIR/ccd-update-sync.timer" ] || remedy="$server" ;;
  esac
  case "$UPD_INTENT_STATE" in
    unreadable) printf '%s\n' "~/.ccrc/update-intent is unreadable ($UPD_INTENT_WHY) — $remedy" ;;
    stale)      printf '%s\n' "the control plane's projection (~/.ccrc/update-intent) is stale — $UPD_INTENT_WHY; $remedy" ;;
    malformed)  printf '%s\n' "~/.ccrc/update-intent is malformed ($UPD_INTENT_WHY) — refusing to follow a projection this reader does not recognise; $remedy" ;;
  esac
}

# ── _upd_target <to> <channel> — which release this run resolves (§9) ────
# One decision before `_upd_resolve`, on the install path AND on --check (so
# --check's `target=` is what update would install). --to wins outright;
# otherwise the projection decides, through its ONE reader:
#   ok | none      → `desired`, or `desired-<ch>` under --channel; a `none`
#                    there refuses, pointing at where the server's reason is
#                    — the document carries none (plan
#                    D-3245);
#   not-configured → stable through latest/download, SAID (spec §9's two
#                    sentences) — unless --channel asked for the control
#                    plane, which is refused: the fetch layer has no URL that
#                    means "newest prerelease", and a node never resolves a
#                    channel locally;
#   anything else  → refused with `_upd_intent_say`'s sentence.
# Every refusal is `_ccrc_die` — exit 1, nothing fetched. Sets UPD_TARGET,
# UPD_TARGET_VIA, UPD_TARGET_CHANNEL, UPD_TARGET_LINE and UPD_TARGET_NONE,
# and prints UPD_TARGET_LINE: --check silences it here and prints it AFTER
# its machine line. `none` is also the STEADY STATE of a converged managed
# node — W2 names a tag only when one is strictly newer than the floor — so
# with a third argument `check` it does not die: UPD_TARGET_NONE names the
# key and --check compares the box against itself (plan
# D-3266). The install path keeps spec §9's
# refusal, and its sentence names the ordinary reason first.
_upd_target() {
  local to="$1" ch="$2" mode="${3-}" key="desired" v="" none_why=""
  UPD_TARGET="" UPD_TARGET_VIA="" UPD_TARGET_CHANNEL="" UPD_TARGET_LINE="" UPD_TARGET_NONE=""
  if [ -n "$to" ]; then
    UPD_TARGET="$to"; UPD_TARGET_VIA="--to $to"
    return 0
  fi
  _upd_intent_state
  case "$UPD_INTENT_STATE" in
    ok|none)
      UPD_TARGET_CHANNEL="${ch:-$UPD_INTENT_CHANNEL}"
      v="$UPD_INTENT_DESIRED"
      case "$ch" in
        stable) key="desired-stable"; v="$UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_STABLE" ;;
        dev)    key="desired-dev";    v="$UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_DEV" ;;
      esac
      UPD_TARGET_VIA="the control plane (channel $UPD_TARGET_CHANNEL)"
      if [ "$v" = none ]; then
        none_why="the control plane resolves no target for this box ($key none) — nothing newer than this box's floor is eligible, or the server declined one; its reason is on the console's update screen (GET /api/updates, resolveDetail)"
        [ "$mode" = check ] || _ccrc_die "update: $none_why; name one with --to <tag>"
        UPD_TARGET_NONE="$key"
        UPD_TARGET_LINE="update: $none_why"
      else
        UPD_TARGET="$v"
        UPD_TARGET_LINE="update: following the control plane — channel $UPD_TARGET_CHANNEL, desired $v"
      fi ;;
    not-configured)
      [ -z "$ch" ] \
        || _ccrc_die "update: --channel needs the control plane (no projection resolves on this box); use --to <tag>"
      UPD_TARGET_VIA="latest/download"
      if [ "$UPD_INTENT_WHY" = macos ]; then
        UPD_TARGET_LINE="update: no control plane on this box (macOS: not centrally managed) — following stable"
      else
        UPD_TARGET_LINE="update: no control plane on this box — following stable"
      fi ;;
    *) _ccrc_die "update: $(_upd_intent_say)" ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$UPD_TARGET_LINE"
}

# ── cmd_channel — the projection, read-only (design 2026-09-20 §14) ──────
# What `_upd_intent_state` measured, as one fixed-shape machine line —
# `channel: state=<w> channel=<c> desired=<t> desired-stable=<t>
# desired-dev=<t> auto=<a>`, `-` for every field a state carries no document
# for — which `ccrc rollout --channel` reads over ssh (plan
# D-3234), then one sentence. Exit 0 while a
# document is in force (ok, none), 1 otherwise. READ-ONLY BY DESIGN: a node
# never writes intent — the one credential it holds is the box token, and
# decision 15 forbids that token any intent write — so every argument is
# refused and the channel is set from the console.
cmd_channel() {
  case "${1-}" in -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;; esac
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "$PROG: channel: set the channel from the console — a node never writes intent (decision 15)" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  local c="-" d="-" ds="-" dd="-" a="-"
  _upd_intent_state
  case "$UPD_INTENT_STATE" in
    ok|none)
      c="$UPD_INTENT_CHANNEL"; d="$UPD_INTENT_DESIRED"; ds="$UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_STABLE"
      dd="$UPD_INTENT_DESIRED_DEV"; a="$UPD_INTENT_AUTO" ;;
  esac
  echo "channel: state=$UPD_INTENT_STATE channel=$c desired=$d desired-stable=$ds desired-dev=$dd auto=$a"
  case "$UPD_INTENT_STATE" in
    ok)
      echo "this box follows channel $c: the control plane resolves $d (stable $ds, dev $dd; auto $a) — 'ccrc update' with no --to installs $d; the channel is set from the console"
      return 0 ;;
    none)
      echo "this box follows channel $c: the control plane resolves no target for it (desired none) — its reason is on the console's update screen (GET /api/updates, resolveDetail)"
      return 0 ;;
    not-configured)
      if [ "$UPD_INTENT_WHY" = macos ]; then
        echo "no control plane on this box (macOS: not centrally managed) — 'ccrc update' follows stable"
      else
        echo "no control plane on this box — 'ccrc update' follows stable"
      fi
      return 1 ;;
    *)
      _upd_intent_say
      return 1 ;;
  esac
}
```

```bash

if s.count(old) != 1: sys.exit('sentinel count %d' % s.count(old))
open('ccd/ccrc', 'w').write(s.replace(old, new))
PY
  echo "== $1"

mut M7 '[[ "$v" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,17})$ ]] ;;' '[[ "$v" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]] ;;' 'ccrc channel'
```

```ts
  /** `$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc` — the launcher the watchdog's rollback runs
   *  through — as a RECORDER: its argv; whether ~/.ccrc/update.lock was FREE
   *  when it ran (the rollback takes that lock itself, so the watchdog must
   *  have let go of it); whether a lock marker reached it; an optional report
   *  it writes as its own; its exit code. What `ccrc rollback` DOES is Task
   *  7's subject — this block owns who calls it, when, and what is recorded
   *  around it. */
  const LAUNCHER = [
    '#!/bin/sh',
    'printf \'%s\\n\' "$*" >> "$HOME/launcher-argv"',
    'if flock -n "$HOME/.ccrc/update.lock" true; then echo free; else echo held; fi >> "$HOME/launcher-lock"',
    'printf \'%s\\n\' "${CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD:-unset}" >> "$HOME/launcher-marker"',
    '[ -f "$HOME/fixture-rollback-report" ] && cp "$HOME/fixture-rollback-report" "$HOME/.ccrc/update.json"',
    'code=0',
    '[ -f "$HOME/fixture-rollback-exit" ] && IFS= read -r code < "$HOME/fixture-rollback-exit"',
    'exit "$code"',
  ].join('\n') + '\n';

  const stampSha = (home: string): string =>
    (JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'build.json'), 'utf8')) as { sha: string }).sha;
  /** A server box on stamp `version`, carrying the three facts "converged"
   *  is made of when a report names that version: the recorded role, the
   *  loopback address `_upd_gate_probe`'s `/health` read resolves through
   *  `_box_server_addr`, and a completed-install record naming the stamp's
   *  sha — read off the stamp, never retyped. `role: null` records none. */
  const watchBox = (prefix: string, opts: { version?: string; role?: string | null } = {}): string => {
    const home = freshUpdateBox(prefix);
    plantOldBox(home, { version: opts.version ?? 'v2.0.0' });
    const role = opts.role === undefined ? 'server' : opts.role;
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'ccrc.env'),
      `${role === null ? '' : `CCRC_ROLE=${role}\n`}CCRC_HOST=127.0.0.1\nCCRC_PORT=7788\n`);
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'installed'), `${stampSha(home)}\n`);
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccrc'), LAUNCHER, { mode: 0o755 });
    return home;
  };

  type WatchReport = { target: string | null; phase: string; startedAt: number; updatedAt: number;
    detail: null; from: string; pid: number };
  const jsonPath = (home: string): string => join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.json');
  /** A report in Task 1's exact shape — seven keys, in order — last written
   *  `ageS` seconds ago. */
  const report = (home: string,
    r: { phase: string; ageS: number; target?: string | null; pid?: number; from?: string }): WatchReport => {
    const updatedAt = nowS() - r.ageS;
    const doc: WatchReport = {
      target: r.target === undefined ? 'v2.0.0' : r.target,
      phase: r.phase,
      startedAt: updatedAt - 45,
      updatedAt,
      detail: null,
      from: r.from ?? 'pwa',
      pid: r.pid ?? 4321,
    };
    writeFileSync(jsonPath(home), `${JSON.stringify(doc)}\n`);
    return doc;
  };
  const readReport = (home: string): Record<string, unknown> =>
    JSON.parse(readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8')) as Record<string, unknown>;
  const lines = (home: string, name: string): string[] => (existsSync(join(home, name))
    ? readFileSync(join(home, name), 'utf8').split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '') : []);
  /** The gate's own `/health` read ran: the watchdog MEASURED a healthy unit. */
  const healthProbed = (home: string): boolean =>
    lines(home, 'curl-argv').some((u) => u === 'http://127.0.0.1:7788/health');
  /** The probe STARTED at all. `_upd_gate_probe` measures the unit before it
   *  spends a `/health` request (Task 5), so on a box whose `fixture-unit-state`
   *  reads `failed` `healthProbed` is false whether or not a probe ran — the
   *  "nothing probed" negatives read the unit question instead. */
  const probed = (home: string): boolean =>
    lines(home, 'systemctl-calls').some((c) => c === '--user is-active ccrc.service');
  const lockFree = (home: string): boolean =>
    spawnSync('flock', ['-n', join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.lock'), 'true']).status === 0;

  const runWatchdog = (home: string, args: string[] = [],
    extraEnv: Record<string, string | undefined> = {}): Result => {
    mkdirSync(join(home, 'tmp'), { recursive: true });
    const env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
      ...updateEnv(home), TMPDIR: join(home, 'tmp'), CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: DEADLINE_MS,
    };
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(extraEnv)) {
      if (v === undefined) delete env[k]; else env[k] = v;
    }
    replantDoctorStubs(home);
    const r = spawnSync(BASH, [join(REPO, 'ccd', 'ccrc'), 'watchdog', ...args], { env, encoding: 'utf8' });
    return { code: r.status ?? -1, stdout: r.stdout ?? '', stderr: r.stderr ?? '' };
  };

  const release = (pgid: number): void => {
    try { process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch { /* already gone */ }
  };
  /** A LIVE holder: a real `flock` on the real lock file, in its own process
   *  group, returned once the lock measurably IS held. `flock <file> sleep 30`
   *  hands its descriptor to the `sleep` child, which a kill of `flock` alone
   *  would leave holding the lock (Task 2's reason for its one-process
   *  `bash -c 'exec 9>>…'` holder); `release` kills the whole GROUP, so both go. */
  const holdLock = async (home: string): Promise<number> => {
    const holder = spawn('flock', [join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.lock'), 'sleep', '30'],
      { stdio: 'ignore', detached: true });
    const until = Date.now() + 5000;
    while (Date.now() < until) {
      if (!lockFree(home)) return holder.pid!;
      await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 20));
    }
    release(holder.pid!);
    throw new Error('the fixture holder never took ~/.ccrc/update.lock');
  };

  itLinux('leaves an absent, a settled, an unreadable and a fresh report alone — one line each, exit 0, nothing probed, nothing rolled back', () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-quiet-');
    // A box that WOULD be rolled back if any of these acted.
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    let r = runWatchdog(home);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe('watchdog: no update report\n');
    for (const phase of NOT_IN_FLIGHT) {
      report(home, { phase, ageS: 3600 });
      const before = readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8');
      r = runWatchdog(home);
      expect(r.code, `${phase}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(r.stdout).toBe(`watchdog: last update ${phase} — nothing to do\n`);
      expect(readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8')).toBe(before);
    }
    for (const bad of ['not json\n', '[1,2]\n', '{"phase":"installing"}\n',
      '{"phase":"installing","updatedAt":"yesterday"}\n', '{"phase":"installing","updatedAt":1.5}\n',
      // A MILLISECOND stamp (13 digits): not this file's unit (rulings R1,
      // R14), and past W2's REPORT_TIME_MAX_S — unreadable, never "fresh".
      `{"phase":"installing","updatedAt":${Date.now()}}\n`,
      '{"phase":"install\\u001bing","updatedAt":1}\n']) {
      writeFileSync(jsonPath(home), bad);
      r = runWatchdog(home);
      expect(r.code, `${bad}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(r.stdout).toBe('watchdog: ~/.ccrc/update.json is unreadable or malformed — not acting on what cannot be read\n');
      expect(readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8')).toBe(bad);
    }
    report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 30 });
    r = runWatchdog(home);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^watchdog: update in progress \(installing, 3\ds old\)\n$/);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
    expect(probed(home)).toBe(false);
  });

  itLinux('acts on exactly the nine in-flight phases — W2\'s IN_FLIGHT_UPDATE_PHASES — declared once in ccd/ccrc', () => {
    const src = readFileSync(join(REPO, 'ccd', 'ccrc'), 'utf8');
    const m = /^UPD_IN_FLIGHT_PHASES=\(([^)]*)\)$/m.exec(src);
    expect(m, 'ccd/ccrc declares no UPD_IN_FLIGHT_PHASES').toBeTruthy();
    expect(m![1]!.split(' ')).toEqual(IN_FLIGHT);
    expect(src.split('\n').filter((l) => l.startsWith('UPD_IN_FLIGHT_PHASES=')).length).toBe(1);
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-inflight-');
    for (const phase of IN_FLIGHT) {
      report(home, { phase, ageS: 90 });
      const r = runWatchdog(home);
      expect(r.code, `${phase}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(readReport(home).phase, phase).toBe('failed');
      expect(readReport(home).detail, phase).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box measures converged at v2.0.0');
    }
  });

  itLinux('stale, no holder, and the box measures CONVERGED at the target: rewritten failed: abandoned…converged, the updater\'s attribution kept, NO rollback (§18 "the watchdog re-measures before it reverts")', () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-converged-');
    const was = report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90, from: 'pwa', pid: 4321 });
    const r = runWatchdog(home);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    const now = readReport(home);
    expect(Object.keys(now)).toEqual(['target', 'phase', 'startedAt', 'updatedAt', 'detail', 'from', 'pid']);
    expect(now.phase).toBe('failed');
    expect(now.detail).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box measures converged at v2.0.0');
    expect(now.target).toBe('v2.0.0');
    expect(now.from).toBe('pwa');
    expect(now.pid).toBe(4321);
    expect(now.startedAt).toBe(was.startedAt);
    expect(now.updatedAt as number).toBeGreaterThan(was.updatedAt);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^watchdog: stale report \(installing, 9\ds\) on a box that measures converged at v2\.0\.0 and answers healthy — recorded as abandoned; nothing was reverted$/m);
    // It MEASURED — the gate's own /health read ran — and it did not revert.
    expect(healthProbed(home)).toBe(true);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
    // …and it let go: a later update is never refused by a watchdog that ended.
    expect(lockFree(home)).toBe(true);
  });

  itLinux('stale, no holder, healthy but NOT converged: rewritten with what the box IS, never a rollback (D-3246, D-3268)', () => {
    // The updater died before the tree moved: healthy on the OLD build.
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-healthy-old-', { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    report(home, { phase: 'fetching', ageS: 90, target: 'v2.0.0' });
    let r = runWatchdog(home);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(readReport(home).detail).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box measures healthy at v1.0.0, not at v2.0.0');
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/\(only a failing probe reverts\)$/m);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
    // On the target and healthy, but the spine never reached `_inst_installed`:
    // a box to FINISH, not to revert — and the sentence says how.
    const home2 = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-healthy-incomplete-');
    writeFileSync(join(home2, '.ccrc', 'installed'), 'a-record-for-some-other-build\n');
    report(home2, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90 });
    r = runWatchdog(home2);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(readReport(home2).detail).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box answers healthy on v2.0.0 but its install never completed (the completed-install record does not name its stamp); rerun: ccrc update --to v2.0.0 --force');
    expect(existsSync(join(home2, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
    // …and when the run that died was a ROLLBACK, `update --force` would be
    // refused below the floor (M7): the remedy is Task 7's `_upd_rerun_hint`.
    report(home2, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90, from: 'rollback' });
    r = runWatchdog(home2);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(readReport(home2).detail).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box answers healthy on v2.0.0 but its install never completed (the completed-install record does not name its stamp); rerun: ccrc rollback --to v2.0.0');
    // A report with no target (null) is never "converged", and stays null.
    const home3 = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-healthy-notarget-');
    report(home3, { phase: 'resolving', ageS: 90, target: null });
    r = runWatchdog(home3);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(readReport(home3).detail).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box measures healthy at v2.0.0, not at its target');
    expect(readReport(home3).target).toBe(null);
  });

  itLinux('stale, no holder, healthy but NOT at the target, in a phase that may have moved the tree: left non-terminal and re-measured every tick, so a later failing probe still reverts it (D-3246, design §11)', () => {
    // The updater was killed INSIDE `_inst_tree`, `_inst_bins` or `_inst_files`,
    // which run before `_inst_stamp` and `_inst_enable`. The stamp still names
    // v1.0.0 and ccrc.service is still the old in-memory process, so the probe
    // passes on v1.0.0, over a tree that is partly v2.0.0 on disk. A terminal
    // `failed` here would answer "nothing to do" on the tick after ccrc.service
    // restarts onto that tree, which is design §11's own scenario.
    for (const phase of ['installing', 'restarting', 'checking', 'restoring']) {
      const home = watchBox(`ccrc-watchdog-healthy-moving-${phase}-`, { version: 'v1.0.0' });
      report(home, { phase, ageS: 90, target: 'v2.0.0' });
      const before = readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8');
      let r = runWatchdog(home);
      expect(r.code, `${phase}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(r.stdout).toMatch(new RegExp(`^watchdog: stale report \\(${phase}, 9\\ds\\) on a box that answers healthy at v1\\.0\\.0, not at v2\\.0\\.0 — its tree may be partly replaced; not acting, re-measuring every tick$`, 'm'));
      expect(readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8'), phase).toBe(before);
      // It MEASURED, and it let go of the lock.
      expect(healthProbed(home), phase).toBe(true);
      expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv')), phase).toBe(false);
      expect(lockFree(home), phase).toBe(true);
      // ccrc.service restarts onto the half-placed tree and fails: the NEXT
      // tick still reverts, because nothing above closed the report.
      writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
      r = runWatchdog(home);
      expect(r.code, `${phase}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(lines(home, 'launcher-argv'), phase).toEqual(['rollback --from watchdog']);
    }
  });

  itLinux('stale, no holder, and the box FAILS its health probe: ccrc rollback --from watchdog, with the lock FREE and no marker; the rollback owns update.json after (§18 "the watchdog reverts a dead updater")', () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-revert-');
    report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90 });
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    // An ambient marker must never reach the rollback: it takes the lock itself.
    const r = runWatchdog(home, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD: String(process.pid) });
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^watchdog: stale report \(installing, 9\ds\) and the box fails its health probe \(.+\) — rolling back$/m);
    expect(lines(home, 'launcher-argv')).toEqual(['rollback --from watchdog']);
    expect(lines(home, 'launcher-lock')).toEqual(['free']);
    expect(lines(home, 'launcher-marker')).toEqual(['unset']);
    expect(readReport(home).phase).toBe('installing');
    expect(lockFree(home)).toBe(true);
    // /health answering the OLD version on a box whose stamp moved — the
    // half-replaced tree restart-looping on the previous server — fails the
    // same probe.
    const home2 = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-revert-oldhealth-');
    report(home2, { phase: 'restarting', ageS: 90 });
    writeFileSync(join(home2, 'fixture-health-pin'), 'v1.0.0\n');
    expect(runWatchdog(home2).code).toBe(0);
    expect(lines(home2, 'launcher-argv')).toEqual(['rollback --from watchdog']);
  });

  itLinux('a refused rollback is relayed; when it wrote nothing it is recorded, verdict first — when it wrote its own report, that report stands', () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-refused-');
    const was = report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90 });
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-rollback-exit'), '1\n');
    let r = runWatchdog(home);
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^watchdog: ccrc rollback --from watchdog exited 1$/m);
    const now = readReport(home);
    expect(now.phase).toBe('failed');
    expect(String(now.detail)).toMatch(/^watchdog: rollback refused \(exit 1\); box unhealthy: ./);
    expect(now.startedAt).toBe(was.startedAt);
    expect(now.pid).toBe(was.pid);
    const home2 = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-refused-own-');
    report(home2, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90 });
    writeFileSync(join(home2, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    writeFileSync(join(home2, 'fixture-rollback-exit'), '1\n');
    const own = `${JSON.stringify({ target: 'v1.0.0', phase: 'failed', startedAt: nowS(), updatedAt: nowS(),
      detail: 'rollback: nothing to roll back to', from: 'watchdog', pid: 777 })}\n`;
    writeFileSync(join(home2, 'fixture-rollback-report'), own);
    r = runWatchdog(home2);
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(readFileSync(jsonPath(home2), 'utf8')).toBe(own);
  });

  itLinux('a LIVE holder of ~/.ccrc/update.lock is never acted on — exit 0 and the sentence, nothing probed, the report byte-identical (§18 "the watchdog reverts a dead updater": the lock check)', async () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-live-');
    report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90, pid: 4321 });
    // The probe WOULD fail: only the lock stands between this box and a rollback.
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    const before = readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8');
    const holder = await holdLock(home);
    try {
      const r = runWatchdog(home);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^watchdog: updater pid 4321 holds ~\/\.ccrc\/update\.lock — its report is 9\ds old; not acting while it lives$/m);
      expect(readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8')).toBe(before);
      expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
      expect(probed(home)).toBe(false);
    } finally { release(holder); }
  });

  itLinux('a holder whose report has not advanced in twice the deadline is recorded WEDGED — its pid, the instant it last reported — and nothing is reverted (§18 "the watchdog bounds a wedged holder")', async () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-wedged-');
    const was = report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 200, pid: 4321, from: 'cli' });
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    const holder = await holdLock(home);
    try {
      const r = runWatchdog(home);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      const now = readReport(home);
      expect(now.phase).toBe('failed');
      expect(now.detail).toBe(`watchdog: updater pid 4321 wedged holding ~/.ccrc/update.lock since ${String(was.updatedAt)}`);
      expect(now.pid).toBe(4321);
      expect(now.from).toBe('cli');
      expect(now.target).toBe('v2.0.0');
      expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/recorded as wedged; nothing was reverted$/m);
      expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
      // The verdict is terminal: the next tick leaves it alone.
      expect(runWatchdog(home).stdout).toBe('watchdog: last update failed — nothing to do\n');
    } finally { release(holder); }
  });

  itLinux('a lock that cannot be MEASURED is neither a live holder nor a free lock — exit 0 and the one sentence, nothing probed, nothing rewritten (ruling R16, D-3250)', () => {
    // Both of `_upd_lock_probe`'s rc-3 conditions (Task 2), on a report that
    // is past TWICE the deadline and a box whose probe would fail — so folding
    // rc 3 into "held" rewrites it as wedged, and folding it into "taken"
    // probes and rolls back. Only the rc-3 arm leaves both alone.
    const quiet = 'watchdog: the update lock could not be measured — not acting\n';
    // (1) The OPEN fails: a directory where the lock file belongs.
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-lock-unopenable-');
    report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 200 });
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    mkdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'update.lock'));
    const before = readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8');
    let r = runWatchdog(home);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe(quiet);
    expect(readFileSync(jsonPath(home), 'utf8')).toBe(before);
    expect(probed(home)).toBe(false);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
    // (2) `flock -n` answers neither 0 (taken) nor contention's 1: a `flock`
    // on the fixture's PATH (its `~/.local/bin`, first) that fails the way a
    // bad descriptor does. `lockFree` uses the host's own flock, not this one.
    const home2 = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-flock-unmeasured-');
    report(home2, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 200 });
    writeFileSync(join(home2, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    writeFileSync(join(home2, '.local', 'bin', 'flock'),
      '#!/bin/sh\necho "flock: fixture: Bad file descriptor" >&2\nexit 64\n', { mode: 0o755 });
    const before2 = readFileSync(jsonPath(home2), 'utf8');
    r = runWatchdog(home2);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe(quiet);
    expect(readFileSync(jsonPath(home2), 'utf8')).toBe(before2);
    expect(probed(home2)).toBe(false);
    expect(existsSync(join(home2, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
  });

  itLinux('the deadline is CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS, else ccrc.env\'s, else fifteen minutes — a positive integer of ms, or it is not read', () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-deadline-');
    const inProgress = /^watchdog: update in progress \(installing, 9\ds old\)$/m;
    report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90 });
    // No environment, no key: fifteen minutes, so 90 s is in progress.
    let r = runWatchdog(home, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: undefined });
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(inProgress);
    // Not a positive integer: read as absent — never as zero, which would make
    // every live update stale the instant it wrote.
    for (const bad of ['0', 'soon', '-5', '']) {
      r = runWatchdog(home, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: bad });
      expect(r.stdout, `CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS='${bad}'`).toMatch(inProgress);
    }
    // The environment wins over the file…
    appendFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'ccrc.env'), 'CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS=60000\n');
    r = runWatchdog(home, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: '600000' });
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(inProgress);
    // …and the file — the key W2's server reads — is read when it has none.
    r = runWatchdog(home, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: undefined });
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(readReport(home).detail).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box measures converged at v2.0.0');
    // Past fifteen minutes is stale on the default.
    const home2 = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-deadline-default-');
    report(home2, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 16 * 60 });
    expect(runWatchdog(home2, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: undefined }).code).toBe(0);
    expect(readReport(home2).phase).toBe('failed');
  });

  itLinux('a fleet node has nothing to watch; an unrecorded role is the spine\'s default, both; any argument is a usage error', () => {
    const fleet = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-fleet-', { role: 'fleet' });
    report(fleet, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 3600 });
    writeFileSync(join(fleet, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    let r = runWatchdog(fleet);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe('watchdog: a fleet node is covered by the server\'s own deadline — nothing to watch here\n');
    expect(existsSync(join(fleet, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
    const bare = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-norole-', { role: null });
    report(bare, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 90 });
    r = runWatchdog(bare);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(readReport(bare).detail).toBe('abandoned by its updater; box measures converged at v2.0.0');
    r = runWatchdog(bare, ['--now']);
    expect(r.code).toBe(2);
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/^ccrc: unknown argument: --now$/m);
  });

  itDarwin('macOS is not centrally managed: exit 0 and the sentence, whatever the report says (decision 17)', () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-darwin-');
    report(home, { phase: 'installing', ageS: 3600 });
    const r = runWatchdog(home);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe('watchdog: macOS is not centrally managed (decision 17) — nothing to watch\n');
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
  });

  itLinux('a REAL update killed mid-install: the watchdog reads the real writer\'s report in its own unit, leaves it while fresh, and reverts it once stale on a box that fails its probe (design §16, Review Focus 5)', async () => {
    const home = watchBox('ccrc-watchdog-killed-', { version: 'v1.0.0' });
    packRelease(home, stubTree(home, { version: 'v2.0.0' }), { tag: 'v2.0.0', latest: false });
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-install-hang'), '');
    mkdirSync(join(home, 'tmp'), { recursive: true });
    const env = {
      ...updateEnv(home), TMPDIR: join(home, 'tmp'), CCRC_RELEASE_BASE_URL: `local://${home}/releases`,
    };
    replantDoctorStubs(home);
    // Its own process group, so one kill takes the update AND its hung spine —
    // the OOM that ends a detached run mid-install.
    const child = spawn(BASH, [join(REPO, 'ccd', 'ccrc'), 'update', '--to', 'v2.0.0'],
      { env, detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' });
    let phase = '';
    try {
      const until = Date.now() + 15_000;
      while (Date.now() < until) {
        try { phase = String(readReport(home).phase); } catch { phase = ''; }
        if (phase === 'installing' && existsSync(join(home, 'staged-ccrc-argv'))) break;
        await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 50));
      }
    } finally {
      release(child.pid!);
    }
    expect(phase, 'the update never reached its staged install').toBe('installing');
    const until = Date.now() + 5000;
    while (!lockFree(home) && Date.now() < until) await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 20));
    expect(lockFree(home), 'the lock outlived the killed updater').toBe(true);
    const left = readReport(home);
    expect(left.phase).toBe('installing');
    expect(left.pid).toBe(child.pid);
    // FRESH on the default deadline. The writer's instant and the watchdog's
    // clock are one unit — seconds — or this reads as decades stale (a
    // seconds writer against a ms clock) or as from the future (the reverse).
    let r = runWatchdog(home, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: undefined });
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^watchdog: update in progress \(installing, [0-9]{1,2}s old\)$/m);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, 'launcher-argv'))).toBe(false);
    // STALE (a 1 ms deadline — 0 s once divided, so the report must be at
    // least one whole second old), no holder, and the half-replaced server
    // will not stay up: the one case the watchdog reverts.
    while (nowS() <= (left.updatedAt as number)) await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 50));
    writeFileSync(join(home, 'fixture-unit-state'), 'failed\n');
    r = runWatchdog(home, [], { CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS: '1' });
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    expect(lines(home, 'launcher-argv')).toEqual(['rollback --from watchdog']);
    expect(lines(home, 'launcher-lock')).toEqual(['free']);
  }, 60_000);
});
```

In `ccd/ccrc`, immediately above the comment line `# One warning, or silence — never a refusal and never a guess. Address` (grep `^# One warning, or silence`), insert:

```bash
# ── _upd_deadline_ms — the one deadline, read the way the server reads it ──
# (W4a Task 9). W2's server takes `CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS` from ccrc.env
# through `ccrc.service`'s EnvironmentFile (its `updateDeadlineMs`); this
# node's watchdog runs under a timer whose environment is the user manager's,
# which never saw that file — so the file is read here by name, after an
# exported value (a test's, or an operator's one-off). A value that is not a
# positive integer of at most 15 digits is not read at all: zero would make
# every live update "stale" the moment it wrote, and 15 digits is a JavaScript
# safe integer — so W2's `updateDeadlineMs` (`Number.isSafeInteger(n) && n > 0`)
# reads the same value from the same key — and keeps every product below inside
# bash's 64-bit arithmetic. MILLISECONDS by name: the one caller divides by
# 1000 (update.json is seconds, rulings R1/R14). Default: 15 minutes (spec §10).
_upd_deadline_ms() {
  local v="${CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS:-}"
  if [[ ! "$v" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,14}$ ]]; then
    v=""
    if [ -f "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ] && [ -r "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ]; then
      v="$(_box_env_value "$BOX_ENV_FILE" CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS)"
    fi
    [[ "$v" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,14}$ ]] || v=900000
  fi
  printf '%s' "$v"
}

# ── ccrc watchdog — the server box's own measure of a self-update that died ─
# (design 2026-09-20 §11; D-3227). W2's deadline sweep measures
# a node's update from INSIDE the server process, and on a server-role box
# that is the process the update restarts. A detached `ccrc update` that dies
# mid-install (OOM, a crash) leaves nothing measuring: the lock dies with it,
# `update.json` stays non-terminal, and `ccrc.service`'s `Restart=always`
# restart-loops a half-replaced tree into systemd's start limit. This verb,
# run every minute by `ccrc-update-watchdog.timer` (server and both roles,
# Linux — `_inst_units`), is that measure, and it NEVER acts on a timestamp
# alone:
#   - absent, settled, unreadable or fresh → one line, exit 0, nothing else;
#   - stale with a LIVE holder of ~/.ccrc/update.lock → left alone (slow is
#     not dead), and past twice the deadline recorded WEDGED, so the inventory
#     shows a wedged box instead of silence;
#   - stale with NO holder → RE-MEASURED — the stamp, the completed-install
#     record, and the gate's own probe (`_upd_gate_probe`, the one the update
#     itself ends with). Healthy → the report is rewritten `failed:
#     abandoned…` and nothing moves: a hand-run `ccrc update` over a dropped
#     ssh session leaves exactly this file on a box that finished. The one
#     exception is healthy but NOT at the target, in a phase that may have
#     moved the tree (`installing` onward). There nothing is written, and the
#     next tick measures again. Only a FAILING probe runs
#     `$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc rollback --from watchdog`.
# THE LOCK IS HELD across the re-measure and the rewrite
# (D-3267): probe-then-act would leave a window in
# which an operator's fresh `ccrc update` takes the lock, writes `resolving`,
# and has that LIVE report replaced by `failed: abandoned…`. It is RELEASED
# before the rollback, which takes it itself (Task 7) and would otherwise be
# refused by its own parent. A lock that cannot be MEASURED — the file will not
# open, or `flock -n` answers neither 0 nor contention's 1 (`_upd_lock_probe`'s
# rc 3, Task 2) — is neither a live holder nor a free lock, and is not acted
# on (ruling R16, D-3250). The rollback runs in this oneshot's cgroup,
# which a `ccrc.service` restart does not touch; the unit file bounds it.
# Nothing here writes a report through `_ccrc_die`: `UPD_REPORTING` is never
# set by this verb, so its refusals leave `update.json` exactly as they found
# it. Every detail it writes is printable ASCII — `_upd_json_str` turns each
# non-ASCII byte into `?`.
UPD_IN_FLIGHT_PHASES=(queued resolving fetching verifying backing-up installing restarting checking restoring)
cmd_watchdog() {
  case "${1:-}" in -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;; esac
  [ $# -eq 0 ] || _ccrc_usage_die "$1"
  if [ "$CCD_OS" = darwin ]; then
    echo "watchdog: macOS is not centrally managed (decision 17) — nothing to watch"
    return 0
  fi
  # The RECORDED role, `cmd_update`'s own read: an absent or unknown value is
  # the staged spine's default, `both`, which runs the server this guards.
  local role=""
  if [ -f "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ] && [ -r "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ]; then
    role="$(_box_env_value "$BOX_ENV_FILE" CCRC_ROLE)"
  fi
  case "$role" in server|fleet|both) ;; *) role="" ;; esac
  if [ "$role" = fleet ]; then
    echo "watchdog: a fleet node is covered by the server's own deadline — nothing to watch here"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ ! -e "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" ] && [ ! -L "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" ]; then
    echo "watchdog: no update report"
    return 0
  fi
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || _ccrc_die "watchdog: jq is not on PATH, so ~/.ccrc/update.json cannot be read — nothing was re-measured or reverted"
  # ONE parse into a fixed seven-line shape closed by an END sentinel —
  # `_box_build_fields`' rule: `$( )` strips trailing newlines, so an empty
  # last field would vanish silently without it. Not JSON, not an object, a
  # phase that is not a word, an `updatedAt` that is not an integer: all
  # UNREADABLE, and unreadable is never acted on. `updatedAt` is unix SECONDS
  # (rulings R1, R14) — Task 1's `now` shape, at most W2's REPORT_TIME_MAX_S
  # eleven digits — so a millisecond stamp is malformed here, never "fresh".
  local out=""
  out="$(jq -r '
    try (
      if type == "object" and (.phase | type == "string") and (.updatedAt | type == "number")
      then "\(.phase)\n\(.updatedAt)\n\(.target // "")\n\(.pid // "")\n\(.startedAt // "")\n\(.from // "")\nEND"
      else empty
      end
    ) catch empty' -- "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" 2>/dev/null)" || out=""
  local -a f=()
  [ -n "$out" ] && mapfile -t f <<< "$out"
  local phase="${f[0]:-}" upd="${f[1]:-}" tgt="${f[2]:-}" pid="${f[3]:-}" started="${f[4]:-}" from="${f[5]:-}"
  if [ "${#f[@]}" -ne 7 ] || [ "${f[6]}" != END ] \
     || [[ ! "$phase" =~ ^[a-z-]{1,32}$ ]] || [[ ! "$upd" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,10}$ ]]; then
    echo "watchdog: ~/.ccrc/update.json is unreadable or malformed — not acting on what cannot be read"
    return 0
  fi
  local p inflight=0
  for p in "${UPD_IN_FLIGHT_PHASES[@]}"; do [ "$p" = "$phase" ] && inflight=1; done
  if [ "$inflight" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "watchdog: last update $phase — nothing to do"
    return 0
  fi
  # THE UPDATER'S ATTRIBUTION SURVIVES every rewrite below: `_upd_phase`
  # stamps target, startedAt, from and pid from these globals, preset from
  # the report. Each is held to its shape first, because the file is data —
  # a value that fails falls to the writer's own default (a null target, a
  # startedAt of now, `from` watchdog, this process's pid).
  [[ "$tgt" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || tgt=""
  [[ "$pid" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || pid=""
  [[ "$started" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,10}$ ]] || started=""
  local w known_from=0
  for w in "${UPD_FROM_WORDS[@]}"; do [ "$w" = "$from" ] && known_from=1; done
  [ "$known_from" -eq 1 ] || from=watchdog
  UPD_REPORT_TARGET="$tgt"; UPD_REPORT_STARTED="$started"; UPD_FROM="$from"; UPD_REPORT_PID="$pid"
  # ONE UNIT, the report's own: unix SECONDS (rulings R1, R14). `_upd_phase`
  # (Task 1) stamps `updatedAt` with `date +%s`, so `now` is read by the same
  # call. The deadline is milliseconds BY NAME (`CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS`, the
  # knob W2's server reads) and is divided by 1000 HERE, the one place it is
  # compared — a sub-second deadline is 0 s, so a report one second old is
  # stale.
  local now deadline lim age
  now="$(date +%s)"
  # A `date` that did not answer would make the subtraction below a bash
  # arithmetic error, not an age — Task 1's `_upd_phase` refuses the same.
  [[ "$now" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,10}$ ]] \
    || _ccrc_die "watchdog: date +%s did not answer with unix seconds — nothing was re-measured or reverted"
  deadline="$(_upd_deadline_ms)"
  lim=$(( deadline / 1000 ))
  age=$(( 10#$now - 10#$upd ))
  if [ "$age" -le "$lim" ]; then
    echo "watchdog: update in progress ($phase, ${age}s old)"
    return 0
  fi
  command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || _ccrc_die "watchdog: flock (util-linux) is not on PATH, so a live updater cannot be told from a dead one — nothing was re-measured or reverted"
  # The compound form (`ccd/ccd:4381-4410`): a failed open is this line's
  # answer, never bash's own diagnostic on stderr. THREE answers, never two
  # (ruling R16; `_upd_lock_probe`'s contract, Task 2): 0 this process took
  # it, 1 a LIVE holder (contention), 3 UNMEASURED — the open failed, or
  # `flock` failed with anything but contention's 1. Folding 3 into 1 would
  # record a wedge nobody measured; folding it into 0 would probe and roll
  # back past a lock this process could not see.
  local lrc=0
  if { exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>>"$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK"; } 2>/dev/null; then
    flock -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD" || lrc=$?
  else
    UPD_LOCK_FD=""; lrc=3
  fi
  case "$lrc" in 0|1) ;; *) lrc=3 ;; esac
  if [ "$lrc" -eq 3 ]; then
    _upd_unlock
    echo "watchdog: the update lock could not be measured — not acting"
    return 0
  fi
  local who="${pid:-unknown}"
  if [ "$lrc" -eq 1 ]; then
    _upd_unlock
    if [ "$age" -gt $(( 2 * lim )) ]; then
      _upd_phase failed "watchdog: updater pid $who wedged holding ~/.ccrc/update.lock since $upd"
      echo "watchdog: updater pid $who has held ~/.ccrc/update.lock with no report for ${age}s, past twice the deadline — recorded as wedged; nothing was reverted"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "watchdog: updater pid $who holds ~/.ccrc/update.lock — its report is ${age}s old; not acting while it lives"
    return 0
  fi
  # ── RE-MEASURE, holding the lock. The three facts "converged" is made of
  # (the stamp's version is the target, the completed-install record names
  # the stamp's sha, the probe passes) and nothing the report claims.
  local src=0 cur_v="" cur_sha="" rec="" prc=0
  _box_build_fields || src=$?
  if [ "$src" -eq 0 ]; then cur_sha="${BOX_BUILD[0]}"; cur_v="${BOX_BUILD[4]}"; fi
  # ONE line, so ONE entry in single-definition's census of this record's
  # readers. `-f` first: a FIFO or a directory at that path is not read.
  [ -f "$BOX_INSTALLED_FILE" ] && { IFS= read -r rec < "$BOX_INSTALLED_FILE"; } 2>/dev/null || true
  # An unversioned stamp is asked for version "" — which `/health` can never
  # answer (it carries `version` only for a versioned build), so that box
  # reads as unhealthy here, and the rollback below then refuses `untagged`
  # by name (Task 7) and is recorded: nothing moves on a box with no tag.
  _upd_gate_probe "$role" "$cur_v" || prc=$?
  if [ "$prc" -eq 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$tgt" ] && [ "$cur_v" = "$tgt" ] && [ -n "$cur_sha" ] && [ "$rec" = "$cur_sha" ]; then
      _upd_phase failed "abandoned by its updater; box measures converged at $cur_v"
      echo "watchdog: stale report ($phase, ${age}s) on a box that measures converged at $cur_v and answers healthy — recorded as abandoned; nothing was reverted"
    elif [ -n "$tgt" ] && [ "$cur_v" = "$tgt" ]; then
      # D-3268: on the target and healthy, but the
      # spine never reached `_inst_installed` — a box to finish, not revert.
      # The remedy is Task 7's ONE helper, read against the report's own
      # `from` (preset above): a rollback's target sits below the floor, where
      # `update --force` is refused (M7), so its rerun is `ccrc rollback --to`.
      local hint
      hint="$(UPD_VERSION="$cur_v" _upd_rerun_hint)"
      # No path in the sentence: single-definition allows one non-comment
      # line naming the record's path, and it is the declaration.
      _upd_phase failed "abandoned by its updater; box answers healthy on $cur_v but its install never completed (the completed-install record does not name its stamp); rerun: $hint"
      echo "watchdog: stale report ($phase, ${age}s) on a box that answers healthy on $cur_v, but its install never completed — recorded as abandoned; nothing was reverted. Rerun: $hint"
    else
      # D-3246: healthy, but not at the target.
      # Split by the phase the updater died in, because a probe that passes
      # on the OLD build does not show that the tree on disk is the old tree.
      # `installing` spans `_inst_tree`/`_inst_bins`/`_inst_files`, which run
      # before `_inst_stamp` and `_inst_enable`: killed there, the stamp and
      # the running ccrc.service are still the old build over a partly-new
      # tree. A terminal report would close this verb on that box for good.
      case "$phase" in
        queued|resolving|fetching|verifying|backing-up)
          # The tree cannot have moved, so the box it left is the box it found.
          _upd_phase failed "abandoned by its updater; box measures healthy at ${cur_v:-an unversioned build}, not at ${tgt:-its target}"
          echo "watchdog: stale report ($phase, ${age}s) on a box that answers healthy at ${cur_v:-an unversioned build}, not at ${tgt:-its target} — recorded as abandoned; nothing was reverted (only a failing probe reverts)"
          ;;
        *)
          # installing, restarting, checking, restoring, and any in-flight
          # word added later (the fail-safe direction): NOTHING is written, so
          # the next tick re-measures, and a failing probe then rolls back.
          echo "watchdog: stale report ($phase, ${age}s) on a box that answers healthy at ${cur_v:-an unversioned build}, not at ${tgt:-its target} — its tree may be partly replaced; not acting, re-measuring every tick"
          ;;
      esac
    fi
    _upd_unlock
    return 0
  fi
  local why="${UPD_GATE_WHY:-the probe gave no reason}" rrc=0
  echo "watchdog: stale report ($phase, ${age}s) and the box fails its health probe ($why) — rolling back"
  # Released FIRST: the rollback takes the lock itself, and a child that
  # inherited this descriptor would pin it past this process (the D-2605
  # measurement §10 cites). `env -u` so an ambient marker can never make the
  # rollback skip acquiring it.
  _upd_unlock
  env -u CCRC_UPDATE_LOCK_HELD "$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" rollback --from watchdog || rrc=$?
  if [ "$rrc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "watchdog: ccrc rollback --from watchdog exited $rrc"
    # Recorded only when the rollback wrote nothing of its own (the report's
    # `updatedAt` never moved) and nobody has taken the lock since — a
    # rollback that refused through its own report, or an operator's run that
    # started after it, owns update.json now. The verdict leads and the
    # probe's words follow, so the 200-character bound cuts the probe, never
    # the verdict. A re-lock that is contended OR unmeasured records nothing:
    # only a lock this process holds licenses a write.
    if { exec {UPD_LOCK_FD}>>"$BOX_UPDATE_LOCK"; } 2>/dev/null && flock -n "$UPD_LOCK_FD"; then
      local after=""
      after="$(jq -r 'try (.updatedAt | tostring) catch empty' -- "$BOX_UPDATE_JSON" 2>/dev/null)" || after=""
      [ "$after" != "$upd" ] \
        || _upd_phase failed "watchdog: rollback refused (exit $rrc); box unhealthy: $why"
    fi
    _upd_unlock
  fi
  return "$rrc"
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement the units, the spine sites and doctor**

Create `deploy/systemd/ccrc-update-watchdog.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Re-measure a stale self-update and revert it only if the box is unhealthy
[Service]
Type=oneshot
# user units carry no ~/.local/bin on PATH (measured, ccrc-models.service); a
# rollback this may run is a whole `ccrc update`, which an operator runs with
# it, so the same PATH is spelled out.
Environment=PATH=%h/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
# A oneshot has NO start timeout by default (systemd.service(5), TimeoutStartSec=:
# "except when Type=oneshot is used, in which case the timeout is disabled"),
# and while this unit runs its timer starts no second instance — so a rollback
# that hung (a download that never ends) would silence the one actor that
# bounds a wedged update. Thirty minutes is twice the default deadline
# (CCRC_UPDATE_DEADLINE_MS); on expiry systemd stops this cgroup, the
# rollback included, and the next tick re-measures.
TimeoutStartSec=1800
# A restore or rollback onto a release older than this unit runs THAT
# release's spine, which neither knows nor removes this pair, so the timer
# stays enabled over a tree with no `watchdog` verb. Skip there: an
# ExecCondition rc of 1-254 skips the run and does not mark the unit failed.
# %h/ccrc is the tree ~/.local/bin/ccrc execs.
ExecCondition=/bin/sh -c 'grep -q "^cmd_watchdog()" %h/ccrc/ccd/ccrc'
ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/ccrc watchdog
```

Create `deploy/systemd/ccrc-update-watchdog.timer`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Periodically re-measure a stale self-update on the server box
[Timer]
OnBootSec=90s
OnUnitActiveSec=60s
AccuracySec=10s
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

In `ccd/ccrc`'s `_inst_units`, immediately above `  _inst_atomic "$tree/deploy/systemd/claude-session@.service.d/limits.conf" \`, insert:

```bash
  # W4a Task 9 (design §11): the server-role watchdog's pair, gated
  # `!= fleet` — the complement of pool-sync's `= fleet`, and derived like it
  # from the unit's own precondition rather than from a sibling's gate:
  # `ccrc watchdog` guards the update that restarts THIS box's
  # `ccrc.service`, and a fleet box runs no server (the server's own deadline
  # covers its updates). `both` — the default role — runs the server, so it
  # gets the pair. Linux only by construction: the Darwin arm returned at the
  # top of this function, and `_inst_units_darwin` installs no timer at all
  # (decision 17 — macOS is not centrally managed).
  if [ "$INST_ROLE" != fleet ]; then
    _inst_atomic "$tree/deploy/systemd/ccrc-update-watchdog.service" "$dir/ccrc-update-watchdog.service" 644
    _inst_atomic "$tree/deploy/systemd/ccrc-update-watchdog.timer" "$dir/ccrc-update-watchdog.timer" 644
  fi
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Mutation measurement**

From the repo root, with the implementation in place and uncommitted, save the two edited scripts and the watchdog unit file, and define a one-occurrence replacer (a restore by copy, never `git checkout --`, which would eat the uncommitted implementation):

```bash
keep="$(mktemp -d)"; cp ccd/ccrc ccd/ccrc-doctor-checks deploy/systemd/ccrc-update-watchdog.service "$keep/"
mut() {  # <file> <old> <new> — the old text must occur exactly once, or the mutation is void
  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" <<'PY'
import sys, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); s = p.read_text(); old, new = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
assert s.count(old) == 1, f'{old!r} occurs {s.count(old)} times in {p}'
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))
PY
}
restore() {
  cp "$keep/ccrc" ccd/ccrc && cp "$keep/ccrc-doctor-checks" ccd/ccrc-doctor-checks \
    && cp "$keep/ccrc-update-watchdog.service" deploy/systemd/ccrc-update-watchdog.service \
    && cmp -s "$keep/ccrc" ccd/ccrc && cmp -s "$keep/ccrc-doctor-checks" ccd/ccrc-doctor-checks \
    && cmp -s "$keep/ccrc-update-watchdog.service" deploy/systemd/ccrc-update-watchdog.service \
    && echo RESTORED
}
wd() { (cd server && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/ccrc-update.test.ts -t 'ccrc watchdog'); }
```

- The request: one `curl -sS -K - -o - -w '\n%{http_code}' --max-time "$TIMEOUT" "$url/api/updates/intent/$nid"`, the config line `header = "x-ccrc-mail-token: <tok>"` fed on stdin, `tok=""` on the next line; `status="${out##*$'\n'}"`, `body="${out%$'\n'*}"`.
- **The validator [corrected — three passes, not two; see the return notes]** (python3 under `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, the body's raw bytes on stdin, strict UTF-8 decode): **pass 1**, per line, for the diagnostic — `zip(GRAMMAR, lines)` over the text with ONE trailing `\n` removed, each present line `re.fullmatch`ed against the grammar its position names (`epoch N`, `issued N`, `lease N`, `channel (stable|dev)`, `desired T`, `desired-stable T`, `desired-dev T`, `auto (off|stable|channel)`, `end`; N `0|[1-9][0-9]*`, T `v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+|none` — the grammar Task 8's reader holds), refusing `line <n> (<key>) is off-grammar: <repr ≤200>`; it never counts lines and never looks for `end`, deliberately; **pass 2**, the whole document — raw length `< 65536`, then ONE `DOC.fullmatch` over the text (the nine patterns, each followed by `\n`): the torn-write, terminator, count, order and trailing-newline detector, and the only one; **pass 3**, the values — `issued` and `lease` carry at most 11 digits (unix seconds until the year 5138; a millisecond value carries 13), `|issued − now| ≤ 86400`, `issued ≤ lease ≤ issued + 86400`, and `desired` equals `desired-<channel>` (D-3270). The RAW bytes reach stdout only when all three pass (`sys.stdout.buffer.write`).
- Units: `ccd-update-sync.service` — `[Unit] Description=Pull the update-intent projection (leased cache; absence means never-synced)`, `[Service] Type=oneshot`, `ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/ccd-update-sync`. `.timer` — `[Unit] Description=Periodically pull this node's update intent from the control plane`, `[Timer] OnBootSec=50s`, `OnUnitActiveSec=60s`, `AccuracySec=10s`, `[Install] WantedBy=timers.target`.
